The rain arrived before another tank could be found. {{hero}} watched the lane as a missing worker returned carrying fuel on a handcart, the barrier’s mud still on their boots. They pointed down the street: two more workers were trapped where the first wall had fallen.

endings.heroWins: The crew reached the trapped workers, and {{heroPlayer}}’s people held the shed for the barrier repair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers kept the tools while the hired crew sought equipment elsewhere.
endings.draw: The workers escaped together; both groups spent the night raising a temporary wall.

paragraphs: A survey beacon had been insured against lightning, but each morning a fresh lightning scar appeared beside it under clear skies. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors came to inspect the claim; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers guarded the beacon because its signal marked their only safe route through the flats. The next scar appeared while both crews were watching.

{{hero}} checked the ground beneath the beacon and found a damaged conductor buried just under the salt. The specialist traced it to an old battery casing, still charged and connected to a timer. Someone had built a machine that imitated a strike closely enough to fool the distant weather sensors.

The timer clicked toward its next cycle. {{hero}} lifted the conductor out of the salt while a settler held the beacon upright. Out on the flats, a caravan followed the beacon light toward them, too far away to hear a warning if the machine failed or the signal went dark.

endings.heroWins: The false strikes stopped, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the beacon lit for the caravan.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers took the beacon while the contractors withdrew with the battery casing.
endings.draw: The caravan arrived safely; both parties remained to learn who had buried the conductor.

paragraphs: A small airship carrying emergency post caught its tether on the colony’s hilltop windmill. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue contractors came to bring it down; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the mill while its sails turned dangerously near the envelope. The postmaster inside could steer, but the tether kept pulling the ship back.

{{hero}} covered the hill path as a figure moved to start the mill’s stalled drive. The fighter fired at a metal cover plate to turn them from the controls, buying the rescue crew time to reach the tether. From the airship window, the postmaster held up a bag marked for the colony clinic.

A gust drove the envelope toward a sail. {{hero}} held the path while a rescuer climbed the mill ladder and cut the snagged end free. The airship drifted above the hill, close enough for a rope to be caught but too high for the postmaster to jump.

endings.heroWins: The airship landed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the windmill stopped until its post reached the clinic.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s settlers held the mill while the rescue crew followed the drifting ship.
endings.draw: The post was saved, but both groups watched the empty airship rise beyond the hills.

paragraphs: Two emergency teams reached the same municipal archive with orders to protect different collections. {{heroPlayer}}’s team marked the ground floor; {{otherPlayer}}’s team claimed the upper vault. Water from an activated sprinkler system was running down the central stair between them, soaking both floors at once.

{{hero}} found the sprinkler valve in a locked service closet and traced its trigger to a smoke detector that showed no smoke. The specialist shut off one zone, saving the lower documents but directing the remaining water toward the upper vault. From above came a call that a real fire had just started inside a copy room.

The two teams met on the stair with dry blankets and fire gear. {{hero}} opened a narrow bypass to feed the copy room while keeping the collection shelves dry. The valve shuddered under pressure, and both team leaders had to choose which documents to carry before anyone could bring the fire under control.

endings.heroWins: The fire was contained, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team preserved the lower archive and its stair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team controlled the upper vault and directed the final salvage.
endings.draw: Both collections survived in part; the teams shared the stair until the building dried.

paragraphs: A hillside aqueduct had brought water to a growing district until a quake opened a crack above the footpath. {{heroPlayer}}’s field engineers came to stop the leak; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic detail held the lower gate to keep pedestrians away. A family still lived in the small house beneath the damaged arch.

{{hero}} climbed onto the aqueduct and found the crack spreading beneath a newer patch. The specialist lowered a temporary seal into place while a civic worker led the family from its house. Their youngest child stopped at the gate to point out a second leak running from the arch’s dry side.

The seal began to lift in the current. {{hero}} held it down with the repair line while the family crossed the footpath and the workers opened a pressure release. The aqueduct shivered overhead, sending a fine spray across the gate before the water level finally began to fall.

endings.heroWins: The arch held, and {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers kept the path safe for the returning family.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s civic detail closed the aqueduct while the engineers withdrew.
endings.draw: The family reached safety; both groups left the water channel shut until a permanent repair.

paragraphs: An ice dome protecting a city food market lost its heating grid during a bitter night. {{heroPlayer}}’s cold-weather patrol brought portable heaters; {{otherPlayer}}’s security team guarded the market’s emergency generator. Vendors were still inside, trying to keep their produce from freezing beneath the glass.

{{hero}} covered the generator entrance from a delivery cart when a figure moved to lock the patrol out. The fighter fired at an empty latch plate, holding the door ajar while technicians rolled in a heater. Frost had already spread across the dome’s lower panels, obscuring the nearest exit.

A vendor called that the glass above the fruit stalls was cracking. {{hero}} kept the entrance clear as workers moved their carts away from the falling frost. The generator turned over once, failed, then caught while the patrol’s heater battery warned it had only minutes left.

endings.heroWins: The dome warmed and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol kept the market open until morning.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s security team held the generator while vendors carried their stock into the street.
endings.draw: The vendors saved their stalls, but both teams closed the dome until its glass could be checked.

paragraphs: A tidal siren above the harbor fell silent as a spring surge approached. {{heroPlayer}}’s marine technicians came to restart it; {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal crew controlled the pump house below. The siren’s painted warning line was already wet, and fishermen still worked on the lowest pier.

{{hero}} reached the siren motor by a narrow stair and found its main belt wrapped around a broken signal flag. The specialist freed the belt while a pump operator called that the lower intake was blocked. They could sound the warning or help restore the pumps, but the same power feed ran to both machines.

The tide rose past the pier steps. {{hero}} held the belt in place with one hand and signaled the fishermen with the other, using the siren’s inspection lamp. The pump house lights returned below, and the motor began to turn before the flag was fully clear.

endings.heroWins: The siren sounded in time, and {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians kept the harbor warnings working.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew held the pump house as the marine technicians retreated from the rising tide.
endings.draw: The fishermen reached shore; both groups left the damaged siren off until the pumps stabilized.

paragraphs: A rooftop data cache above the central station contained the names of people waiting to be reunited after a long evacuation. {{heroPlayer}}’s search team came to retrieve it; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic guards held the stair because the roof’s safety rail had failed. Families were arriving below with photographs and little else.

{{hero}} covered the upper landing when someone moved to take the cache across the exposed roof. The fighter fired at an empty metal frame, forcing them back from the broken rail. A searcher reached the cache and found its power pack loose, its stored names disappearing a few at a time.

The rooftop sign began to sway in the wind. {{hero}} held the landing while the searcher braced the pack and read the remaining names down to families waiting at the stair. One family heard its missing person called just as the pack’s warning light went red.

endings.heroWins: The cache was saved, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the station roof open for the families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the roof and held the cache for later review.
endings.draw: The families received the names that survived, while both groups searched for the missing records.

paragraphs: A city registry issued two residency cards with the same number to people who had never met. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to compare the original forms; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic staff held the office until its morning queue could be served. Both cardholders were waiting with families who depended on their addresses.

{{hero}} found a duplicate printing plate beside the registry press. The specialist traced it to a night shift when the machine had been repaired by a clerk now absent from the office. Beneath the plate lay a third form carrying the same number, but its address was a building demolished years ago.

The queue reached the front desk as {{hero}} brought out the forms. A clerk recognized the demolished building as an old shelter and offered its paper sign-in book. One of the cardholders began turning its pages, stopping at a signature in handwriting unmistakably their own.

endings.heroWins: The cardholders kept their homes, and {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators secured the registry for correction.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the office and deferred the duplicate-card review.
endings.draw: Both residents were served, but the third form remained unresolved in the shelter book.

paragraphs: A power substation on the city fringe failed just as a lunar eclipse began. {{heroPlayer}}’s armored repair escort came to protect the transformers; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic team controlled the lower switchyard. The hospital beyond the ridge had enough backup charge for only one more procedure.

{{hero}} covered the transformer lane when a figure moved toward an open breaker. The fighter fired into the empty steel frame beside them, making space for an electrician to reach the damaged insulation. A line of sparks crossed the lane, and the hospital’s distant windows went dark one row at a time.

The electrician called for a manual reset from the lower switchyard. {{hero}} held the lane while a messenger carried the request toward the civic team. Overhead the moon entered shadow, and every work lamp on the substation flickered as the two crews tried to synchronize their switches.

endings.heroWins: The hospital lights returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the substation through the repair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s civic team took the switchyard and directed power elsewhere.
endings.draw: The hospital received its procedure’s power, but both crews kept the damaged station under joint watch.

paragraphs: An old observatory in the foothills had sealed its entrance after a snow slide exposed a room missing from its plans. {{heroPlayer}}’s mountain guides came to open a safe approach; {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers held the telescope room and guarded its fragile plates. A diagram on the hidden room’s door showed the sky without its brightest star.

{{hero}} followed a ventilation shaft around the snow blockage and found the hidden room filled with empty plate boxes. The specialist checked a brass index against the researchers’ collection: the missing plates had all been exposed on the same winter night. One box held a note asking whoever found it to watch the east ridge at dawn.

The snow shifted beneath the entrance stair. {{hero}} guided the researchers through the ventilation passage with the index in hand, then climbed a safe ledge facing east. The first light reached the ridge, revealing a line of old survey markers where no trail had been mapped.

endings.heroWins: The plates and index survived, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guides kept the approach open for a survey.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers secured the observatory while the guides withdrew from the unstable slope.
endings.draw: Both groups saw the markers at dawn and left the hidden room sealed until the snow settled.

paragraphs: A new marketplace was built over a concrete bunker that no city plan acknowledged. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew came for an old family archive inside; {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal guard held the market for its opening day. A vendor discovered that every stall drain led toward the bunker door rather than the street.

{{hero}} covered the stairwell while the crew lifted a rusted hatch. When a figure moved to shut the market gate behind them, the fighter fired into an empty hinge plate, leaving a route for shoppers to leave. Beneath the hatch, water was rising around shelves of photographs wrapped in oilcloth.

The crew passed the photographs up as the market fountains switched on overhead. {{hero}} held the stair clear and shouted for the vendors to turn off the water. One bundle carried a picture of the square before the bunker was buried, including a doorway where the newest stall now stood.

endings.heroWins: The photographs reached daylight, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the bunker accessible beneath the market.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard sealed the hatch while the recovery crew escaped with only a few pictures.
endings.draw: The market opened late; both groups agreed to survey the old doorway before sealing the bunker.

paragraphs: An abandoned velodrome had become a shelter for racing dogs during the city’s storm season. {{heroPlayer}}’s handlers arrived to move them before demolition; {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers held the service tunnel beneath the track. The oldest dog refused to leave its kennel, watching an empty place in the stands.

{{hero}} met a defender at the tunnel mouth, close enough that raising a firearm would put the kennels behind them in danger. The fighter pressed through at arm’s length and kept the passage clear while handlers carried the smaller dogs out. Above, the roof sheeting lifted in the wind.

The old dog bolted for the stands just as a section of roof came loose. {{hero}} left the tunnel and followed it up the banking, finding a collar beside the empty seat. Its engraved name matched a memorial plaque on the wall, and a handler called from below that the storm had reached the track.

endings.heroWins: The last dog reached shelter, and {{heroPlayer}}’s handlers kept the track open long enough to clear every kennel.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers retained the tunnel while the handlers found another exit.
endings.draw: All the dogs escaped; the storm settled the question of who could still use the old velodrome.

paragraphs: A hillside emergency archive held paper maps for a city whose digital navigation had failed. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts came to fetch the evacuation routes; {{otherPlayer}}’s civil detail guarded the narrow road above a school. Children had been asked to wait there until someone knew which street remained open.

{{hero}} covered the archive steps while a scout carried map rolls toward the school. A vehicle descended the road without lights, and the fighter fired at a roadside barrier to turn it away from the children. Its driver shouted that the lower bridge was gone, contradicting the map in the scout’s hands.

The detail brought an older roll from the archive. {{hero}} held the road as both maps were spread across the school wall, revealing a footpath between two gardens that no vehicle could follow. Teachers gathered the children in pairs, and the scout went first to check the gate.

endings.heroWins: The children found the footpath, and {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts kept the archive open for the next evacuees.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s civil detail held the maps while the scouts took the children by another route.
endings.draw: The school emptied safely; both groups stayed behind to correct the marked bridge.

paragraphs: A decommissioned landing capsule stood inside a planetarium, its guidance lights kept on for visitors. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to remove its black box; {{otherPlayer}}’s curators wanted it left in place for the school tour. That morning the capsule announced a landing sequence, though its engines had been removed.

{{hero}} opened the instrument bay and found a second, handwritten checklist tucked behind the black box. The specialist followed its steps to a switch marked for a place no longer shown on the planetarium’s star chart. As the switch moved, the domed ceiling displayed a horizon instead of constellations.

The tour group watched a distant light approach that horizon. {{hero}} kept the capsule powered while a curator read the checklist aloud to the children, pausing at a line that instructed the crew to count every passenger. One child reported an extra shadow among their reflections on the capsule window.

endings.heroWins: The black box was secured, and {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians kept the planetarium safe for the tour.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s curators retained the capsule and ended the inspection.
endings.draw: The tour departed together; the horizon stayed on the dome until the last visitor left.

paragraphs: A freight tunnel below the city began freezing despite warm trains passing through it. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to protect workers replacing the track heaters; {{otherPlayer}}’s transit guards held the signal cabin. The final night train was approaching, loaded with food that could not be delayed another day.

{{hero}} covered the service gallery when a figure tried to throw a frozen switch beneath the train’s path. The fighter fired at an empty mounting bracket and forced them back. A heater worker knelt beside the rails and found the ice growing outward from a sealed cable trench, not from the tunnel walls.

The train horn sounded beyond the bend. {{hero}} kept the gallery clear while workers pulled the trench cover free and saw a small refrigerated box connected to the power line. Its label gave a delivery address on the train itself, and the switch began to stiffen again under their hands.

endings.heroWins: The switch held for the train, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol kept the tunnel open while the box was examined.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the signal cabin and routed the train elsewhere.
endings.draw: The food arrived, but both groups closed the frozen gallery until the box could be traced.

paragraphs: A city garden opened a veterinary nursery for animals recovered from the frontier. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers came to reunite a young pack animal with its mother; {{otherPlayer}}’s park staff held the gate after finding an untagged animal among the new arrivals. The mother waited outside, refusing food from anyone.

{{hero}} checked the nursery tags and discovered one had been copied from an animal that died during the journey. The specialist found the untagged youngster inside a quiet side pen, its coat marked by a familiar white stripe. At the sight of the mother, it stood, but the gate latch had jammed.

A crowd gathered as {{hero}} worked the latch from the inside. The youngster pressed against it and the mother answered from outside the park rail. The staff asked for a final identity check, while the two animals kept calling to one another across the narrow passage.

endings.heroWins: The pair reunited, and {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers kept the nursery open for the remaining animals.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the nursery while the rangers waited outside with the mother.
endings.draw: The animals left together; both groups stayed to correct the tags on the other pens.

paragraphs: A city bathhouse became a temporary examination center after workers reported the same strange rash. {{heroPlayer}}’s clinicians needed samples from its old water pipes; {{otherPlayer}}’s city staff held the building while families waited for test results. The rash appeared only on workers from one street, regardless of where they lived.

{{hero}} inspected the pipe junction beneath the baths and found a narrow repair sleeve made from the wrong metal. The specialist scraped a sample from its inner edge while the staff traced the supply back toward the street in question. A child watching the basin said the water had tasted like coins after a recent repair.

The sample kit changed color at once. {{hero}} shut the affected branch and asked the staff to keep the families inside for clean water and instructions. Outside, more workers arrived from the street, carrying bottles filled from the same taps before anyone had warned them.

endings.heroWins: The source was isolated, and {{heroPlayer}}’s clinicians kept the bathhouse open for those needing care.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff controlled the building while the clinicians took their samples elsewhere.
endings.draw: The affected workers received care; both groups kept the pipes shut for an independent test.

paragraphs: A wind farm on the eastern roofline stored an old map inside its maintenance computer. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came for the route it marked; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail guarded the turbines after a blade lost power. Below, a procession headed for the quarter the map claimed had no streets.

{{hero}} climbed to the stalled turbine and found a service cable threaded through its map reader. The specialist restored power just long enough to print the route. Its path ended at the procession’s destination, but a note alongside it warned that the entrance would close at sunset.

A gust set the turbine turning while {{hero}} held the paper against the ladder rail. The security detail called for everyone to leave the roof, and the couriers watched the procession disappear into the unmapped quarter. Delivering the route meant reaching the people below before the last light left the roofs.

endings.heroWins: The route reached the procession, and {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers held the wind farm long enough to guide them through.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail secured the turbines while the couriers lost the roof path.
endings.draw: The procession reached its destination; the printed map showed no way back after sunset.

paragraphs: A customs pier held a suspended cargo container that had arrived without a ship. {{heroPlayer}}’s harbor guards came to inspect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic team held the crane controls until the owner could be found. The container’s listed cargo was dried fish, yet fresh water dripped steadily from its door.

{{hero}} covered the crane walkway when a figure reached for the release lever. The fighter fired at an unoccupied railing and kept the container above the pier. A worker slipped a sample cup beneath the dripping seam and found clean river water, warmer than the harbor surrounding them.

The crane motor began to lower the container anyway. {{hero}} held the walkway while technicians stopped the descent by hand, and a fisherman called from the far end of the pier that the river had run dry at his landing. The drops became a steady trickle as the lock gave way.

endings.heroWins: The container was opened safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guards kept the pier clear for an inspection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s civic team took the crane and sealed the container again.
endings.draw: Both groups saved the pier; the warm river water kept flowing after the container was emptied.

paragraphs: An outpatient clinic used a rooftop greenhouse to grow medicines that spoiled quickly after harvest. {{heroPlayer}}’s care team came to collect a batch for an arriving ambulance; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors had closed the roof after its glass panels cracked in the wind. A patient downstairs was waiting for that particular crop.

{{hero}} went up the protected service stair and found the plants alive beneath broken glass. The specialist carried a padded tray along the dry side of the roof while an inspector marked the unsafe panels. A shard slipped toward the plants, and the tray caught it before it reached the leaves.

The ambulance sounded below. {{hero}} cut the ready stems and covered them as the greenhouse doors rattled in another gust. Through the roof window, the patient’s family held open the clinic entrance. The crop had to cross the exposed landing before the medicine could be prepared.

endings.heroWins: The medicine reached the patient, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the greenhouse safe until repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors retained the roof while the team looked for another supply.
endings.draw: The patient received the batch; both groups left the greenhouse closed to everyone else.

paragraphs: A rooftop radio station broadcast a call for help from a tower marked empty on the city map. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew came to trace it; {{otherPlayer}}’s police detail controlled the lower floors. Every caller gave the same room number, though the roof had no rooms at all.

{{hero}} covered the broadcast deck while a technician climbed toward the antenna. A figure moved to cut the feeder cable, and the fighter fired at an empty support spar to stop them. The technician found a second cable running down the outside wall to a maintenance balcony hidden between floors.

The caller answered again as {{hero}} held the deck clear. A small hand appeared through the balcony grating, waving a strip of fabric with the room number written on it. The station microphone picked up the child’s voice before anyone on the rooftop could reach the balcony.

endings.heroWins: The child reached the deck, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the transmitter available for others.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail secured the building and took over the rescue.
endings.draw: The child escaped; both teams spent the night checking every unmarked balcony.

paragraphs: A public aquarium had built a temporary art installation among its empty tanks. {{heroPlayer}}’s designers came to collect a mirrored sculpture before the exhibit closed; {{otherPlayer}}’s staff held the hall when its largest tank reported a water leak. Every reflection in the sculpture showed a different corridor.

{{hero}} followed the leak behind the tank and discovered an old access valve hidden by the exhibit wall. The specialist closed it slowly, preserving the fish in the smaller tanks, then saw a worker reflected in the sculpture who was not visible in the corridor. The worker pointed toward a service hatch under the floor.

The hall alarm brought visitors toward the exits. {{hero}} held the valve and asked the staff to check the hatch before moving the sculpture. Beneath it was a trapped maintenance worker whose flashlight had been flashing against the mirrored surface all afternoon.

endings.heroWins: The worker escaped and {{heroPlayer}}’s designers kept the exhibit open for a final visit.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the hall and closed the installation after the rescue.
endings.draw: The tanks were saved; both parties left the sculpture in place until the leak was repaired.

paragraphs: A window-cleaning cradle stopped halfway down the city’s tallest residential tower with two workers inside. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers came to free it; {{otherPlayer}}’s building staff held the roof controls while a crowd gathered below. One worker could not stand without the cradle pitching toward the glass.

{{hero}} reached the rooftop winch and found a second safety line wrapped around a vent. The specialist freed it a loop at a time, keeping the cradle still while the workers talked one another through the wait. A resident opened a window above them and offered a climbing harness through the gap.

The vent cover began to move under the strain. {{hero}} secured the safety line to a stronger anchor and asked the resident to hold the harness where the workers could reach it. Below, the crowd fell quiet as the cradle descended its first few centimeters.

endings.heroWins: Both workers reached the roof, and {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers kept the winch safe for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff took the controls and guided the rescue without the riggers.
endings.draw: The workers survived; both groups closed the tower’s exterior access pending inspection.

paragraphs: A city escrow office held a sample of a new fuel that both its inventor and its investor claimed to own. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors arrived with the signed deposit record; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards kept the cold locker closed until a hearing. The sample had developed a pale ring inside its sealed flask.

{{hero}} checked the locker temperature and found it falling whenever the deposit record was scanned. The specialist disconnected the reader, then held the flask to the light. A second, tiny capsule sat within the pale ring, carrying a batch number not listed on either claim.

The hearing clerk arrived as the locker alarm sounded. {{hero}} kept the sample cool with a portable case while both claimants read the new batch number. One recognized it as a failed trial that had been destroyed, and asked the clerk not to open the capsule in the occupied office.

endings.heroWins: The sample remained secure, and {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors kept the office open for a full inventory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards retained the locker while the auditors left with copies of the records.
endings.draw: The hearing paused; both claimants signed a joint order to keep the capsule sealed.

paragraphs: The subway’s central junction began drawing passengers onto a platform that did not appear on the route map. {{heroPlayer}}’s reconnaissance team entered from the service tunnel; {{otherPlayer}}’s transit guards kept the public stairs closed. A train announcement named a destination none of the waiting passengers recognized.

{{hero}} covered the junction as a figure tried to switch the track beneath an arriving train. The fighter fired at the unused signal housing, forcing them away from the lever while a technician reached the controls. The new platform lights came on, revealing fresh chalk arrows pointing toward an older tunnel behind the wall.

The train slowed with its doors aligned to the unknown platform. {{hero}} held the junction while the technician stopped the switch from turning again. Several passengers stepped forward, each holding a ticket dated tomorrow, and the guard on the public stair called for them to remain behind the safety line.

endings.heroWins: The train passed safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the junction open for inspection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards retained the junction and closed the unknown platform.
endings.draw: The passengers returned upstairs; both teams left the chalk arrows untouched until the next train.

paragraphs: A fuel convoy stopped beneath an elevated road after its lead driver found the underpass too low for the last tanker. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to secure the intersection; {{otherPlayer}}’s traffic team held the upper ramp while ambulances waited for fuel. The tanker had already scraped a support beam.

{{hero}} covered the underpass when a figure moved to release the tanker’s parking brake. The fighter fired at an empty wheel stop to turn them back while mechanics measured the damaged beam. The convoy’s smallest vehicle could fit beneath it, but its transfer hose did not reach the tanker where it stood.

The mechanics carried the hose by hand into the open lane. {{hero}} held the intersection as traffic above shook dust from the beam, and a driver began the careful transfer. At the far end, the first ambulance arrived with its engine running on its last fuel.

endings.heroWins: The ambulances filled safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s escort kept the underpass clear.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s traffic team controlled the intersection and rerouted the fuel convoy.
endings.draw: The ambulances departed; both groups closed the damaged underpass to heavier vehicles.

paragraphs: An adoption archive kept its oldest records on audio cassettes because the first families had never been entered into the newer database. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers came for one recorded surname; {{otherPlayer}}’s clerks guarded the listening room for people with appointments. The cassette labeled with the surname was blank until the door closed.

{{hero}} rewound the tape and heard a woman describing the child she hoped to find, followed by a second voice asking why the recording was being made today. The specialist checked the cassette shell: its date was forty years old, and the clerk beside the machine recognized the woman’s name from a recent appointment.

A visitor knocked at the listening-room door. {{hero}} kept the cassette running as the clerk let her in, then watched her listen to her own younger voice. She recognized the child’s surname but said the description belonged to someone she had never met.

endings.heroWins: The visitor heard the complete tape, and {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers kept the archive open for the family.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s clerks took the cassette back into storage before the search could continue.
endings.draw: Both parties made a copy; the visitor left with one unanswered name to pursue.

paragraphs: A radio telescope above the city began receiving an instruction to dismantle itself, one component at a time. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery team wanted its receiver; {{otherPlayer}}’s observatory staff held the control room, keeping the dish pointed away from occupied districts. Each instruction arrived in a voice borrowed from a different staff member.

{{hero}} covered the service deck when a figure moved toward the motor disconnect. The fighter fired at a vacant bracket to force them back while an engineer locked the dish in place. A technician opened the receiver and found its channel selector set to a frequency the telescope could not normally hear.

The borrowed voices began naming people on the deck. {{hero}} held the approach as the engineer copied the final transmission onto a portable recorder. It gave no more instructions; instead it counted the steps from the dish to a hatch the staff insisted had been welded shut.

endings.heroWins: The transmission was saved, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the telescope while the hatch was checked.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff kept the receiver and sealed the service deck.
endings.draw: The dish stayed intact; both groups heard one last borrowed voice from behind the welded hatch.

paragraphs: An evacuation checkpoint counted one more resident leaving the district than it had registered entering. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts came to examine the passenger logs; {{otherPlayer}}’s city guards held the final gate while families waited for transport. The unmatched name belonged to a person everyone in the queue remembered seeing, but none could describe.

{{hero}} followed the name through paper forms and found each witness had placed the stranger beside a different family. The specialist compared the forms under a work light, discovering the same small ink mark beside every account. An exhausted clerk recognized the mark as one used to flag children traveling without an adult.

The last bus opened its doors. {{hero}} checked the queue again and found a child standing alone beneath a borrowed coat, carrying the unmatched name on a folded card. The guards began closing the gate, and the specialist held out a hand before the bus pulled away.

endings.heroWins: The child boarded safely, and {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts kept the checkpoint open for those still missing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards closed the gate and handled the child’s registration themselves.
endings.draw: The child reached shelter; both groups kept the logs for families still searching.

paragraphs: The city’s talking crossings fell silent during the morning commute. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers came to repair the central signal box; {{otherPlayer}}’s traffic officers controlled the intersection while pedestrians waited for guidance. The lights still changed, but their spoken directions sent people toward the wrong curb.

{{hero}} found two map versions running at once inside the signal box. The specialist traced the newer one to a road that had been closed months earlier and moved the pedestrian route back to the real crossing. A person with a white cane tested the first spoken instruction and stopped before reaching the roadway.

A tram approached while the traffic officers held vehicles at the line. {{hero}} kept the crossing in manual mode and listened to the next instruction beside the pedestrian. This time it named the correct curb, and the person crossed with enough time for the tram to wait behind them.

endings.heroWins: The crossings spoke correctly again, and {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers held the signal box through the repair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers retained manual control while the engineers withdrew to test another map.
endings.draw: Everyone crossed safely under a human guide; both groups left the automated directions off for the day.

paragraphs: A neighborhood archive began sending residents notices that their buildings had never existed. {{heroPlayer}}’s records team came to restore the addresses; {{otherPlayer}}’s city guards held the street while families waited with keys to homes missing from the official map. The archive printer kept producing blank deeds for the same block.

{{hero}} found an obsolete municipal robot still sorting the archive’s basement cards. The specialist traced its route and discovered a box labeled for a demolished district had been placed among current records. Inside lay photographs of the supposedly missing homes, each with a newer handwritten address on its back.

The guards prepared to clear the building as {{hero}} carried the box upstairs. A resident recognized her front door in a photograph and held it beside her key. The robot returned for another card, stopping when the specialist showed it a deed with the correct street number.

endings.heroWins: The addresses returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the archive open for the residents.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the archive while the records team left with the misplaced box.
endings.draw: Both groups restored the street on paper, but the public map still showed an empty block.

paragraphs: An old aqueduct crossed the city plaza above a memorial procession. {{heroPlayer}}’s honor guard came to carry a banner beneath it; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail had closed the plaza after a masonry inspection. The procession was already gathering at the gate when a stone fell into the empty basin.

{{hero}} met a defender at the narrow walkway that led to the aqueduct’s control hatch. The fighter forced a passage at arm’s length without striking the crumbling parapet. At the hatch, a loose chain held the cracked arch against a temporary brace placed there before the plaza was closed.

The chain slipped as the procession began to sing below. {{hero}} braced the hatch and called for the crowd to move back while workers secured the support from the other side. The banner waited folded at the gate, and the first row of mourners could see the fighter holding the arch steady.

endings.heroWins: The arch held, and {{heroPlayer}}’s guard carried the banner safely across the plaza.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail kept the plaza closed while the procession found another route.
endings.draw: The mourners gathered outside the gate as both teams worked through the night to secure the arch.

paragraphs: A public evidence room contained the final recording from a bridge collapse, but its custody seal bore a date after the bridge was rebuilt. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came to examine the original; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic officials held the room ahead of an anniversary ceremony. Survivors wanted to hear what the recording actually said.

{{hero}} compared the seal to the room’s entry ledger and found it had been replaced during a power outage. The specialist copied the untouched audio beneath a conservation hood. Under the sound of the collapse came a voice calling for workers to leave the bridge several minutes before the official warning.

The anniversary guests arrived while {{hero}} carried the copy toward the hearing desk. An official asked that the recording remain sealed until the ceremony ended, but a survivor was standing beside the desk with a photograph of the person whose voice they had recognized.

endings.heroWins: The survivors heard the warning, and {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators preserved the recording for review.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officials retained the room while the investigators left with their copy.
endings.draw: The recording was played once; both parties agreed to keep its original under joint custody.

paragraphs: A space elevator’s transfer deck stopped with a passenger car suspended just above the station floor. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock patrol came to open a rescue path; {{otherPlayer}}’s facility guards held the deck while technicians inspected the traction cable. The passengers could see the floor but could not reach it.

{{hero}} covered the deck when a figure moved to release the car’s emergency brake before the rescue lift was ready. The fighter fired into an empty guardrail behind them and kept the brake engaged. A technician found the cable wound around a dropped luggage frame that had become lodged in the machinery.

The rescue lift climbed toward the car while {{hero}} held the platform clear. From the passenger window, a child passed out a scarf to mark the frame’s exact position. The technician pulled on it gently, and the traction cable moved for the first time since the car had stopped.

endings.heroWins: The passengers reached the deck, and {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol held the elevator for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s facility guards took the rescue lift and kept the dock closed.
endings.draw: The car emptied safely, but both groups left the traction system stopped until the frame was removed.

paragraphs: A night museum reported a visitor trapped inside its new planetarium exhibit after a citywide blackout. {{heroPlayer}}’s search team entered through the loading bay; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the main doors while a crowd waited outside. The exhibit projected stars even without power, slowly rotating toward a painted exit that did not exist.

{{hero}} covered the dark hallway as a figure moved to shut a fire door on the search team. The fighter fired into the door’s empty closer mechanism, leaving it open while a rescuer followed the trapped visitor’s voice. Behind the painted exit was a maintenance panel with scratches on its inner side.

The rescuer pulled the panel free and found the visitor in a narrow service space. {{hero}} held the hallway clear as they emerged, blinking into the starlight that still crossed the ceiling. The visitor said the painted exit had opened for a moment just before the blackout.

endings.heroWins: The visitor reached the street, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the museum open for a final sweep.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the exhibit and directed the evacuation themselves.
endings.draw: The visitor escaped; both teams closed the museum until its unexplained projection ended.

paragraphs: A riverside theater displayed costumes from a performance canceled generations earlier. {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors came for a ceremonial mask kept backstage; {{otherPlayer}}’s museum detail guarded the collection during a charity rehearsal. A performer discovered that the missing final scene was written inside the mask.

{{hero}} reached the narrow backstage bridge as a defender stepped across it to block the costume room. The fighter met them at arm’s length, careful not to send either of them into the orchestra pit. The mask slipped from a performer’s hands and hung by its ribbon over the gap.

The fighter caught the ribbon while the rehearsal continued onstage. {{hero}} held the bridge as the performer read the final scene by the work lights: it required the audience to leave the theater before the curtain fell. In the seats, volunteers had begun to take their places.

endings.heroWins: The mask was carried out and {{heroPlayer}}’s visitors helped clear the theater before the final curtain.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail retained the costume room and ended the rehearsal.
endings.draw: The audience left safely; both groups kept the mask backstage until its warning could be checked.

paragraphs: A communal kiln fired the last clay water filters needed by the district before summer. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came to collect them; {{otherPlayer}}’s city staff kept the workshop closed after its chimney developed a crack. The kiln was already hot, and removing the filters early would ruin them.

{{hero}} entered by a side service hatch and found smoke leaking into a storeroom of finished pieces. The specialist set a temporary draft plate beneath the crack while the potter packed the safe filters. A child outside called that the chimney bricks had begun falling into the public lane.

The workshop needed more time than the chimney could offer. {{hero}} held the draft plate as staff cleared the lane and the potter took the final tray from the heat. The new filters glowed faintly; they would survive only if they cooled without another rush of cold air.

endings.heroWins: The filters cooled intact, and {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers kept the workshop safe until the chimney was rebuilt.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff closed the kiln while the couriers carried away only the finished stock.
endings.draw: The district received some filters; both groups left the kiln idle for repairs.

paragraphs: An archive of folded paper birds hung above the city’s central fountain, one for every person who helped rebuild the district. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came to repair the hanging frame; {{otherPlayer}}’s officials controlled the fountain after one bird fell into the water with a fresh name written inside.

{{hero}} climbed the scaffold to inspect the frame and found a strand of new thread tied among the old knots. The specialist followed it to a sealed envelope perched at the highest point. Inside was a list of people still working on the district, including the fountain mechanic standing beneath the scaffold.

The frame began to slip as {{hero}} handed down the envelope. The mechanic closed the fountain pump and reached for the falling line while the caretakers steadied the scaffold. Dozens of paper birds lifted in the breeze, and the new one landed dry in the mechanic’s open hand.

endings.heroWins: The birds remained aloft, and {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers kept the fountain open for its neighbors.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officials closed the site and took the envelope into custody.
endings.draw: The frame was repaired, but both groups left the new name unread until the mechanic chose to open it.

paragraphs: A living canopy over the district playground stopped opening its leaves each morning, leaving the ground dark and damp. {{heroPlayer}}’s gardeners came to examine its roots; {{otherPlayer}}’s city crew held the playground until its support posts could be tested. Children watched from the fence with drawings of the canopy in full light.

{{hero}} followed a root to a maintenance trench, where a new cable had been laid across its growing tip. The specialist moved the cable onto a bracket and found the root bruised but alive. Above, the leaves began turning toward a patch of sunlight that had not reached the ground in weeks.

The support posts creaked when the canopy lifted. {{hero}} held the root in a padded sling while the city crew tightened the posts and the children asked to come back inside. A single leaf unfolded over the gate, making a small, dry place for the first visitor to stand.

endings.heroWins: The canopy recovered, and {{heroPlayer}}’s gardeners kept the playground safe for the children.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s city crew retained the grounds while the gardeners withdrew for more tests.
endings.draw: The gate reopened briefly; both groups agreed to watch the support posts before full use.

paragraphs: A scrap yard held the only working pump motor available for a flooded neighborhood. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired retrieval team came to claim it; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic guards held the yard while a mechanic tested whether the motor would run. The rising water had already reached the neighborhood’s lowest apartments.

{{hero}} covered the yard entrance when a figure moved toward the motor with a cutting tool. The fighter fired at an empty sheet-metal frame, stopping the approach without striking the mechanic. The motor turned once on its test stand, then rattled loose from a bolt hidden beneath years of rust.

The mechanic braced the motor while {{hero}} held the lane open for a cart. From the neighborhood came a call that an older resident was trapped above the waterline. The retrieval team loaded the motor carefully, knowing the next jolt could break the bolt before they reached the pumps.

endings.heroWins: The motor reached the pumps, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team kept the yard route open for the rescue.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards retained the motor and sent their own repair crew to the apartments.
endings.draw: The resident escaped; both groups worked together to fit the motor before the next surge.

paragraphs: A ferry terminal held sealed relief packages that had spent a week circling the harbor on an automated boat. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors came to unload them; {{otherPlayer}}’s civic guards controlled the pier until the packages could be checked. Their labels named streets the city had renamed after the shipment left.

{{hero}} covered the pier as the boat drifted against a piling. A figure moved to release its mooring, and the fighter fired into an empty bollard to stop them without striking the workers. When one package split, dried blankets spilled out beside a photograph of the family who had packed them.

The workers began matching the old addresses to current homes. {{hero}} held the gangway steady while residents arrived with their own photographs, recognizing packages meant for neighbors. The boat’s engine started again without a pilot, and the last parcel was still across the water on its deck.

endings.heroWins: The parcels reached their homes, and {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors kept the terminal open for the final delivery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards retained the boat and checked the parcels after the contractors left.
endings.draw: Most packages were delivered; both crews waited for the boat to return with the last one.

paragraphs: An old arena kept a trophy made from the first city tram, soon to be moved into private storage. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired crew came to secure it for the neighborhood; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the display hall while the transfer papers were checked. The trophy contained a hand-cranked emergency bell that still worked.

{{hero}} covered the hall as a trolley rolled toward the locked service exit with the trophy aboard. The fighter fired at an empty wheel bracket, stopping the trolley before it reached the door. A former tram driver recognized a brass plate on its base and asked to read the names behind it.

The guards entered as {{hero}} kept the service corridor clear. The driver lifted the plate and found the workers’ names, including a relative who had never been listed in the city’s records. Outside, the bell rang through the open hall and brought other families to the entrance.

endings.heroWins: The names were displayed, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the trophy in the neighborhood.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards moved it to storage while the driver copied the inscription.
endings.draw: The trophy stayed in the arena for the families to see while its ownership was reviewed.

paragraphs: A weather station rented its unused upper floor to artists, who turned the old forecast charts into a public exhibition. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors came to recover a missing instrument case; {{otherPlayer}}’s city staff held the stair during an incoming storm. The exhibition’s central drawing showed the storm bending around the station.

{{hero}} checked the gallery and found the instrument case supporting a canvas frame. The specialist removed it carefully, revealing a barometer whose needle had passed beyond its printed scale. An artist said the case had been under the painting all week, yet the needle had begun moving only that morning.

Wind struck the roof while {{hero}} carried the case downstairs. The city staff opened the shelter beneath the gallery, and visitors followed with the paintings rolled under their arms. On the newly exposed canvas backing was a second forecast, drawn in charcoal, showing the station itself missing from the hill.

endings.heroWins: The visitors reached shelter, and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the station instruments running through the storm.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the station and stored the instrument case upstairs.
endings.draw: The exhibition survived; both parties stayed to compare the drawing with the storm’s path.

paragraphs: A high-altitude laboratory opened a viewing deck for visitors on the same day a research drone failed to return. {{heroPlayer}}’s security team came to search the lower slope; {{otherPlayer}}’s facility guards held the deck until everyone was accounted for. From the railing, a child spotted the drone balanced above a ravine.

{{hero}} covered the cable bridge while a technician crossed to retrieve it. A figure moved to cut the anchor, and the fighter fired into an empty support panel to turn them away. The technician found the drone’s camera still running, its screen showing a second bridge beneath the snow.

A gust lifted the drone from its perch. {{hero}} held the anchor path while the technician caught its tether and crawled back across. On the viewing deck, visitors counted the figures in the drone’s latest image: all of them, photographed from beneath the ravine minutes before the search began.

endings.heroWins: The drone and technician returned, and {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the deck until the visitors were safe.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the laboratory while the security team left the slope.
endings.draw: Everyone left the deck; both groups kept the drone’s image for the next survey.

paragraphs: Two reforestation crews received identical orders to plant the same cleared hillside before the rains. {{heroPlayer}}’s workers brought young trees in red-marked trays; {{otherPlayer}}’s crew arrived with blue-marked trays. Their soil maps disagreed about where the old riverbed lay beneath the grass.

{{hero}} dug a test hole along the disputed line and found a buried irrigation tile stamped with both crews’ district marks. The specialist followed it downhill to a blocked outlet, where water had collected just below the surface. Planting either tray without opening the outlet would drown its roots.

The first rain began while {{hero}} cleared the outlet by hand. Both crews carried their trays up the slope and waited for the water to run. At the lowest planting row, a worker found a living sapling from the old forest, rooted exactly on the line neither map could settle.

endings.heroWins: The outlet drained and {{heroPlayer}}’s crew planted its trees around the surviving sapling.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew kept the hillside and chose the first planting rows.
endings.draw: Both crews planted around the old tree and left their boundary flags in the truck.

paragraphs: In a glacial survey camp, a warm spring began leaving black grit on the snow. {{heroPlayer}}’s geologists crossed the frozen lake to collect a sample; {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors had already marked the spring as unsafe. The only dry approach ran below an old avalanche shelf.

{{hero}} held the approach while a geologist lowered a vial into the warm water. Shapes appeared on the ridge, and the fighter drove them away from the sampling line without firing toward the shelf. The geologist pulled up a vial of ordinary water and a glove dusted with ash.

A low crack sent everyone back across the lake. By the time the ice stopped trembling, a fresh seam had opened beside the spring, exposing a layer of charred timber deep within the glacier. No one could say what had burned there or how long the ice had kept it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the safe bank and carried the sample to the camp laboratory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors closed the approach and retained the spring for a later inspection.
endings.draw: Both teams returned across the lake with one vial each and left the unstable shelf alone.

paragraphs: A floating coral nursery came loose from its moorings before a tropical squall. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew reached the platform by launch; {{otherPlayer}}’s shore team waited with a towline and a narrow window before the tide turned. Underwater, the nursery dragged a heavy chain across living reef.

{{hero}} went below the platform and worked the chain free from the coral without breaking its anchor pin. The specialist surfaced to call for slack while the towline tightened above. In the pause between waves, a diver saw new coral growing along a metal plate hidden under the nursery.

The squall arrived as the platform swung clear of the reef. Both crews helped guide it into sheltered water, keeping the plate submerged. No inventory listed that plate; someone had installed it long enough ago for a living colony to take hold.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew moored the nursery in shelter and saved the growing colony beneath it.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s shore team took the tow and chose where the platform would be anchored.
endings.draw: The nursery reached sheltered water, and both crews agreed to leave the unknown plate in place.

paragraphs: A harvest conveyor carried crates from hillside greenhouses to the market until a sealed box appeared among the produce. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspection crew recognized a mark from a crop lost years earlier; {{otherPlayer}}’s growers demanded the line keep moving before their harvest spoiled. The box was already approaching the open bridge.

{{hero}} covered the bridge while an inspector stopped the conveyor and opened the box. A figure reached for its latch from the opposite bank, but the fighter kept the inspector clear long enough to lift out paper packets of seed. Each packet bore a date later than the crop’s disappearance.

The machinery started again, and the growers sent their crates to market. The inspector carried the packets uphill toward a greenhouse with empty benches. Beneath the last layer of paper lay a photograph of the field that had supposedly gone barren, its irrigation lines newly repaired.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the seed and reopened the conveyor under their watch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s growers reclaimed the bridge and took charge of the box.
endings.draw: The harvest reached market; both crews witnessed the seeds being sealed for testing.

paragraphs: At a district tribunal, a submission box filled with petitions to preserve a walled garden. {{heroPlayer}}’s clerks came to file them before the hearing; {{otherPlayer}}’s maintenance crew was there to inspect a leaking wall. The garden’s owner said the water line ended at the street.

{{hero}} opened the jammed box and sorted the petitions by address. One child had drawn a channel beneath the garden instead of signing a page. The specialist took the drawing to the wall, where a trickle escaped between bricks, and called the maintenance crew to look.

The hearing began with damp petitions spread across the table. A worker lifted the loose brick and found a small water gate behind it, still turning under a careful hand. From the garden came the sound of a fountain no one in the chamber had known was there.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s clerks entered the petitions and the hidden channel into the tribunal record.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew kept control of the wall and closed the garden pending its inspection.
endings.draw: The tribunal heard the petitions while both parties watched water run through the reopened gate.

paragraphs: An emergency armory stored the drills and breathing sets needed after a collapse at the old mine. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue team arrived for the gear; {{otherPlayer}}’s depot guards reported that an unfamiliar person was carrying a charge toward the only bridge. Families of the trapped miners waited on the far bank.

{{hero}} took position beside the bridge and forced the person with the charge away from its supports. The fighter kept the crossing clear while the rescuers wheeled a drill over the planks. A worker recognized the charge as a blasting tool from the mine, with its warning tag still attached.

The rescuers reached the tunnel mouth with their equipment intact. Inside, faint tapping answered a hammer struck against the rock. The families counted each tap in silence, then watched an empty breathing set disappear into the opening ahead of the first rescuer.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers carried the gear into the mine and kept the bridge open for evacuation.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards retained the depot and controlled the crossing while the rescue plan was revised.
endings.draw: The equipment crossed safely, and both teams worked beside the families at the mine entrance.

paragraphs: A mountain tea terrace concealed the only working repeater between two stormbound villages. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew came for its battery; {{otherPlayer}}’s growers feared losing the warning it carried. A bell inside the repeater hut began ringing although the wind had dropped.

{{hero}} climbed the wet service stairs and found a stranger prying at the battery housing. The fighter closed the distance where a shot might strike the cables, wrested the tool away, and held the doorway until a technician could cut the current. On the repeater screen, every weather alert showed the same impossible timestamp.

Below the hut, the growers lit small lamps along the terraces to guide the technician home. The bell rang once more when the new battery was fitted, then gave way to a voice reporting clear skies from the village beyond the storm.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the repeater working and sent the warning to both villages.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s growers held the hut and took charge of its battery.
endings.draw: The repeater stayed in service while the crew and growers shared its weather reports.

paragraphs: An old seismology bunker stood beneath a field of tall, silver grass. {{heroPlayer}}’s field scientists followed a fresh tremor there; {{otherPlayer}}’s agronomists wanted the doors sealed before their irrigation began. The recorder inside had drawn a straight line through the last shaking.

{{hero}} opened the recorder cabinet and discovered its paper tangled around a spool. The specialist freed the strip and threaded it past a cracked ink roller. Instead of a straight line, the hidden section showed repeated, evenly spaced pulses coming from a point beneath the grass.

Outside, the irrigation channels were filling. The scientists laid the strip on the bunker step and counted the pulses beside the ticking pump. When the pump stopped, the pattern continued. A grass stem above the buried point quivered in still air.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scientists secured the bunker and began a careful survey of the buried source.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s agronomists closed the bunker and resumed work in the field.
endings.draw: The recorder remained open for observation as both teams marked the same point on their maps.

paragraphs: A glassworks was being cleared for a new road, but its furnace still held the last molds from a vanished workshop. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvagers arrived with a handcart; {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew had brought a crane to move the chimney. No one knew how fragile the furnace floor had become.

{{hero}} caught the crane operator at the doorway as the chimney began to shift. The fighter pulled the operator clear of a falling lintel and held the release lever down while the salvagers rolled the molds out. A copper plaque slipped from the lintel, warm despite the cold building.

In the daylight, the salvagers turned the plaque over. It carried the names of apprentices, each beside a tiny fingerprint pressed into the metal. The road crew set the chimney down gently and waited while the oldest worker searched the list for a family name.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s salvagers took the molds and plaque to the town archive.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew retained the glassworks and scheduled another guarded salvage visit.
endings.draw: Both crews helped move the molds before the chimney was lifted again.

paragraphs: Floodwater reached the old railway junction just as a relief train approached. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort needed its signal tower; {{otherPlayer}}’s maintenance team had found the points locked against the train. A lamp flashed from the tower window, though its operator had gone missing at dawn.

{{hero}} covered the narrow gantry while a mechanic reached the point switch. Someone behind the signal glass raised a weapon, and the fighter kept the gantry clear long enough for the mechanic to throw the lever. The flashing lamp continued, three short pulses followed by one long.

The relief train slowed into the dry siding. The mechanic climbed the tower and found its door locked from outside, with a second lamp blinking on the floor beneath it. He lifted the lamp and read a penciled note directing him toward a service room below the flooded tracks.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the junction and guided the relief train into the safe siding.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team retained the signal tower and controlled the train’s approach.
endings.draw: The train stopped safely, and both teams searched the service room together.

paragraphs: A returning survey capsule dropped into a grazing field with its beacon still announcing an orbital descent. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew followed the signal; {{otherPlayer}}’s herders were moving animals away from a ribbon of spilled coolant. The capsule’s hatch bore two different return addresses.

{{hero}} traced the coolant line to a damaged valve and closed it before the herd reached the ditch. The specialist then found a shipping cylinder inside the capsule, padded with loose straw rather than the foam listed on its manifest. Something inside the cylinder answered the tapping of a tool.

The herders watched from the fence as the crew carried the cylinder into a clean tent. When its lid was opened, a little brass music box played four notes and stopped. Scratched underneath was a request to send it home to whichever address still existed.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew contained the spill and recovered the cylinder for its intended recipient.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s herders kept the field closed until the capsule could be removed safely.
endings.draw: The animals returned to the pasture, and both parties signed the cylinder into joint custody.

paragraphs: A remote observatory kept a telescope aimed at a hillside instead of the sky. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to ask why; {{otherPlayer}}’s survey party had planted stakes around the same slope. Through the eyepiece, the hill showed a pale circle that could not be seen with bare eyes.

{{hero}} held the observatory path while a technician steadied the telescope and copied its coordinates. A shot cracked against the railing, and the fighter pushed the technician below the parapet before answering from cover. In the eyepiece, the pale circle slid across the slope as if something beneath it were moving.

By sunset, the survey stakes outlined empty ground far below the telescope’s mark. The patrol reached the new point and found a shallow pit of glassy earth, still warm. From the observatory window, the circle had already moved again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol kept the observatory open and followed the next set of coordinates.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors secured the hill and closed the path to the telescope.
endings.draw: The telescope stayed trained on the slope while both crews plotted the moving circle.

paragraphs: A hydroelectric dam had a narrow fish ladder that no one had used in years. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers followed fresh chalk marks along its railing; {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers had orders to close the intake before silt reached the turbines. The marks were at the height of a child’s hand.

{{hero}} found a jammed inspection hatch beside the ladder and pulled it open as water rose around the hinges. A stranger tried to shove it shut from the far side, and the fighter held the gap while a ranger slipped through. Beyond it sat a small rowboat with a blanket and a dry pair of shoes.

The engineers shut the intake and waited for the water to fall. From under the boat came a quiet voice asking whether the fish could still get upstream. The chalk marks stopped at the hatch, but wet footprints led onward toward the high bank.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers secured the hatch and helped the hidden traveler reach the bank.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers controlled the intake and continued their search under dam safety rules.
endings.draw: The intake stayed closed while rangers and engineers searched the dry side of the ladder together.

paragraphs: A clinic greenhouse lost its cooling system during a heat wave. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team came for the plants used in an experimental treatment; {{otherPlayer}}’s groundskeepers had been told to clear the beds for repairs. One tray carried a handwritten name that did not appear on the inventory.

{{hero}} traced the faulty cooling circuit beneath the tray and found its valve deliberately locked half open. The specialist freed it, then moved the named plants into the shaded recovery room before their leaves could wilt. Under the tray lay a stack of letters from patients describing the same unmistakable scent.

As the temperature fell, the groundskeepers opened the greenhouse vents. The room filled with the scent the letters described, and an elderly patient at the clinic door recognized it before anyone showed her the label. She asked who had cared for the plants all these years.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team kept the greenhouse operating and preserved the named plants.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s groundskeepers retained the greenhouse and moved the plants for repairs.
endings.draw: The plants survived the heat, and both crews helped document the forgotten tray.

paragraphs: A bookbinder beneath the salt market claimed to have repaired a ledger everyone else believed destroyed. {{heroPlayer}}’s courier came to collect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors wanted the market evacuated before a leaking roof spread brine into the workshop. The courier could hear pages turning behind the locked door.

{{hero}} watched the stair while the bookbinder passed a wrapped volume to the courier. A figure appeared at the upper landing and tried to block the way out; the fighter held that narrow line until the courier reached the street. The wrapper left a faint outline of salt across the courier’s sleeve.

At a dry table, the courier opened the ledger and found no accounts, only a record of houses beneath the market that had disappeared from public maps. One address had been crossed out that morning. Through the open window came the sound of workers repairing the roof above it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s courier kept the ledger dry and brought its addresses to the people living nearby.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors sealed the market and took charge of the damaged workshop.
endings.draw: The workshop was evacuated, and both parties recorded the ledger before the roof was repaired.

paragraphs: A harbor customs scale began registering cargo weight when no ship was berthed. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock crew followed its reading to a chain beneath the water; {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors were marking the pier for demolition. An abandoned buoy pulled steadily against its mooring as the tide went out.

{{hero}} stepped onto the slippery lower platform and seized the chain where it crossed a rusted winch. Another person reached for the release handle; the fighter wrested it free and held the chain while the dock crew raised the buoy. A small tin compartment inside was packed with sealed receipts.

The scale fell to zero as the last receipt came ashore. Each document listed a shipment that had never entered the harbor register, yet several bore the signature of the pier’s original builder. The surveyors put away their demolition flags until the harbor office could read them.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew retained the pier and delivered the receipts to the harbor office.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors controlled the pier and suspended work pending an inspection.
endings.draw: The buoy was lifted intact, and both teams witnessed the opening of its compartment.

paragraphs: Pilgrims on a desert road relied on a hilltop refuge whose fog bell had fallen silent. {{heroPlayer}}’s care workers came with fresh water; {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew wanted the building closed after finding blue dye in its cistern. The refuge keeper insisted no dye had been stored there.

{{hero}} traced the cistern feed through the courtyard and found a cracked branch leading to an old signal pipe. The specialist isolated it, then opened the bell housing to see where the pipe ended. Inside hung a blue-stained cloth wrapped around the bell’s clapper, knotted in a pattern the keeper recognized.

The keeper unfolded the cloth beside the road crew. It was a child’s scarf, lost during a sandstorm years earlier; the dye had washed into the water whenever the fog machinery ran. After the cistern was drained, the bell sounded across the road again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s workers reopened the refuge with clean water and a working warning bell.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew kept the refuge closed while its supply was replaced.
endings.draw: The pilgrims received water outside, and both teams helped clean the cistern before reopening.

paragraphs: An unused amusement dome began projecting a rising sea across its walls, convincing nearby residents that the flood barriers had failed. {{heroPlayer}}’s repair team entered to shut off the display; {{otherPlayer}}’s neighborhood wardens kept people back. The dome’s air pressure was falling for real.

{{hero}} covered the projection room while a technician reached the ventilation controls. A figure stepped out of the dark seating and leveled a weapon at the console; the fighter drew that attention away, giving the technician time to restore pressure. The painted water vanished, leaving a small handwritten sign on the wall.

The sign gave instructions for finding a child’s lost coat beneath the rear seats. A warden brought it out, dusty and much too small for its present owner. In its pocket was a ticket for the dome’s final show, dated the day the venue closed.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team held the dome and repaired its ventilation before the residents returned.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took control of the building and restricted entry for repairs.
endings.draw: The false flood ended, and both groups checked the dome before allowing anyone back inside.

paragraphs: A walking bridge inside a habitat’s low-gravity animal house stopped halfway across its enclosure. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers needed to reach a stranded juvenile; {{otherPlayer}}’s safety crew had disconnected the motor after spotting damaged supports. A paper bird drifted above the bridge with a child’s name on it.

{{hero}} secured a tether to the nearest sound beam and crossed by hand, keeping away from the loose railing. The specialist coaxed the juvenile into a carrier and found more paper birds folded into a gap above its nest. Each carried a different name and a wish for the animal to come home.

Back at the entrance, children pressed against the glass to watch the carrier pass. One recognized her bird and explained that they had made them for a keeper who had been away too long. The keeper arrived as the juvenile was returned to its enclosure.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers rescued the juvenile and secured the bridge for repair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s safety crew retained the enclosure and directed the recovery from outside.
endings.draw: The juvenile returned safely, and both teams left the bridge closed until its supports could be replaced.

paragraphs: An archival cold room stored film reels beneath a freight elevator whose cable had begun to fray. {{heroPlayer}}’s retrieval crew came for a single reel; {{otherPlayer}}’s building stewards wanted the lower level evacuated. From the elevator shaft came music that stopped whenever its inspection lamp turned on.

{{hero}} reached the lower landing as a stranger tried to force the elevator door against a trapped technician. The fighter held the door open, pulled the technician through, and stayed at the threshold while the crew carried out the reel. In the open shaft, the music started again from a tiny speaker tied to the cable.

The reel showed a community orchestra playing in the same building before it was converted into storage. The technician recognized the tune from the shaft: an unfinished piece, played here only once. Someone had tied the speaker there so it would be heard whenever the elevator moved.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew recovered the reel and kept the cold room accessible for inspection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s stewards closed the lower level and took charge of the archive.
endings.draw: The reel and technician came out safely, and both crews agreed to leave the elevator idle.

paragraphs: A rooftop antenna began broadcasting street names that had been removed from the city map. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal analysts climbed the roof to locate the source; {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal crews came to cut power before the broadcast confused emergency calls. Small weather vanes around the antenna turned against the wind.

{{hero}} watched the narrow access stair while an analyst traced the signal through a box of analog wires.
