endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors retained the records and scheduled the visits.
endings.draw: The house appeared on both lists, and the teams conducted the survey together.

paragraphs: An emergency communications tower stood above a temporary village built after the floods. {{heroPlayer}}’s protection detail came with a repairer; {{otherPlayer}}’s civil workers were waiting for word that a missing family had been found. The tower kept transmitting half a sentence, then falling silent.

{{hero}} covered the base while the repairer climbed to replace a damaged relay. A figure moved toward the power junction and raised a weapon, and the fighter held them off until the aerial steadied. The full message named a shelter on the far bank where the family had checked in.

Workers in the village relayed the news from door to door, until it reached the family’s neighbor. She saved a place at the common table and set out a cup for each person expected back. The tower’s next message arrived without interruption.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail secured the tower and restored the emergency link.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the tower and passed messages by ground courier.
endings.draw: The missing family was located, and both groups kept the link open for their return.

paragraphs: An ancestral teahouse stood above stepped fields where irrigation water had begun running through the guest room. {{heroPlayer}}’s protectors brought a mason to inspect the floor; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers were moving family keepsakes upstairs. A young visitor found a door beneath the wet floorboards.

{{hero}} reached the hidden door as a stranger tried to force it shut on the mason’s hand. The fighter pulled them away and held it open while the mason traced a narrow water channel underneath. A blocked outlet sent water into the house instead of the fields.

The caretakers cleared the outlet and watched water resume its old route downhill. In the drying guest room, the visitor uncovered a painted plan of the fields behind the door. A grandparent recognized the path they had walked to school long before the teahouse was built.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s protectors secured the teahouse and restored the fields’ water route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers retained the house and completed the repairs.
endings.draw: The guest room dried, and both teams preserved the field plan.

paragraphs: A wilderness fire tower carried a hand-painted trail board for visitors who preferred paper maps. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers arrived after wind tore it loose; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors were searching for hikers who had followed its missing arrows. From the tower, a line of colored ribbons could be seen between trees.

{{hero}} followed the ribbons to a collapsed footbridge and found the hikers sheltering on the near bank. The specialist fixed a temporary arrow at the safe detour and radioed the inspectors, who met the group before dusk. The torn board lay in the stream, caught against a branch.

Back at the tower, a ranger spread the board to dry. Its arrows had been painted by one of the hikers’ grandparents, who knew every bend of the trail. The hiker helped repaint the missing turn, using the same color as the ribbons that had led them home.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers secured the tower and marked the safe detour.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors retained the trail and closed it for bridge repairs.
endings.draw: The hikers returned, and both groups restored the trail board together.

paragraphs: A riverside forge held a mold for the community bell, scheduled to be cast that morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came with the bell metal; {{otherPlayer}}’s foundry workers were lifting their tools above a sudden flood. The heavy mold remained on a low bench beside the open door.

{{hero}} reached the bench as a stranger tried to tip the mold into the water. The fighter grappled them away and held its frame while workers hoisted it onto dry bricks. Beneath the mold lay a handwritten list of neighbors who had donated small pieces of metal for the casting.

The flood fell by afternoon, and the foundry workers read each name before pouring the metal. No single piece survived visibly in the bell, but the list was kept beside it. When it first rang, families on both banks came to the forge to hear it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts saved the mold and secured the forge for the casting.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the forge and postponed the pour.
endings.draw: The mold stayed dry, and both groups witnessed the bell’s first ringing.

paragraphs: An electric tram lost power beneath a rail bridge while carrying workers home from an evening shift. {{heroPlayer}}’s rapid response team brought an electrician; {{otherPlayer}}’s bridge staff were checking a loose overhead cable. Through the tram windows, passengers held up their phone lights in a neat row.

{{hero}} covered the bridge stair while the electrician isolated the broken cable. A figure reached for the supply switch with the repair unfinished, and the fighter held them clear until the electrician gave the signal. The tram lights came back, revealing a passenger’s birthday cake still upright on a seat.

The tram rolled into the next stop, where relatives were waiting beside a small gathering of candles. The passenger carried out the cake and apologized for being late. A bridge worker said the lights in the windows had told them everyone aboard was still calm.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the cable and brought the tram into the station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s bridge staff retained the crossing and directed the repair.
endings.draw: The passengers reached their stop, and both crews checked the line before the next tram.

paragraphs: A weather balloon from an orbital survey descended into a city courtyard with its sensors still reporting a storm overhead. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery specialists came for the instruments; {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal officers kept children back from the trailing cable. The sky above the courtyard was perfectly clear.

{{hero}} reeled in the cable and discovered a pocket of ash trapped around the balloon’s upper sensor. The specialist cleaned it and watched the false storm warning disappear. In the remaining data was a genuine wind shift approaching the far side of the city, still hours away.

The officers sent the corrected warning to the neighborhoods in its path. A child who had watched the balloon land drew a black cloud on a clear blue page, then added the direction it would travel. When the breeze arrived, the drawing was already pinned to the courtyard wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s specialists secured the instruments and issued the corrected forecast.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers retained the courtyard and sent their own weather warning.
endings.draw: The balloon was recovered, and both groups shared the new wind data.

paragraphs: A forest lookout began flashing amber along a migration path just as a herd approached the narrow valley below. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol climbed to find the cause; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens were holding a road convoy outside the valley. The amber flashes followed the rhythm of something tapping inside the tower.

{{hero}} covered the lookout stairs while a warden checked the beacon. A figure appeared at the upper landing with a weapon, and the fighter held the approach until the beacon was made safe. Inside its housing sat a woodpecker, trapped beside a loose contact that blinked whenever it pecked.

The wardens released the bird into the trees and kept the road closed until the herd passed. As the last animal entered the far woods, the woodpecker began tapping on a pine outside the tower. This time the beacon stayed dark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol secured the lookout and protected the migration path.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens retained the road and delayed the convoy.
endings.draw: The herd crossed safely, and both groups repaired the amber beacon.

paragraphs: A municipal wildlife gate had closed on the migration route outside a crowded district. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers arrived before dusk; {{otherPlayer}}’s street inspectors worried that opening it would send animals through the bus depot. On the far side, a small herd waited with a calf pressing its nose to the fence.

{{hero}} walked the fence and found an older service lane behind the depot, still blocked by fallen branches. The specialist cleared it and opened the gate just wide enough to guide the herd toward the trees. The calf passed last, stopping to look at its reflection in a depot window.

Bus drivers watched the animals disappear beyond the service lane. One driver said the route had been there before the depot and asked for it to remain marked. The rangers painted a small sign before they left, pointing away from the buses and toward the woods.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers secured the gate and guided the herd to woodland.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors retained the depot and delayed the crossing.
endings.draw: The herd passed safely, and both groups marked the old lane for future migrations.

paragraphs: A clinic courtyard held a mural painted by patients over many years. {{heroPlayer}}’s care team came to preserve it before a cracked irrigation channel washed the wall; {{otherPlayer}}’s building inspectors had marked the courtyard for closure. Water was already spreading toward the lowest painted row.

{{hero}} found the channel’s break beneath a planter and turned its flow into a dry catch basin. The specialist worked around the plants while the inspectors braced the wall. Once the water stopped, a painted date emerged beneath the muddy edge, older than anyone had guessed.

A former patient recognized the date as the day the clinic first opened and pointed out a tiny portrait of its first caretaker beside it. Staff brought out chairs so people could look without stepping on the wet ground. The channel was repaired while the mural dried.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the courtyard and preserved the mural.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors retained the building and closed the garden for repair.
endings.draw: The wall survived, and both parties documented its newly visible date.

paragraphs: A narrow archive beneath the old courthouse held witness statements from a dispute resolved decades ago. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers came to recover a sealed packet before the room flooded; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers were carrying boxes upstairs. A whistle sounded from the locked records stair.

{{hero}} covered the stair while a courier opened the packet room. A figure appeared behind the boxes and raised a weapon, and the fighter held them away until the packet was carried out. The whistle continued from a small brass timer left to warn when the flood pump stopped.

The caretakers restarted the pump and opened the packet with its designated recipient present. Inside was a letter from a witness who had asked that it be read only if the courthouse was ever threatened. It urged the city to preserve the room where neighbors had finally listened to one another.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers secured the packet and brought it upstairs dry.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers retained the archive and managed the flood response.
endings.draw: The room was pumped out, and both groups preserved the letter and its original packet.

paragraphs: A customs shed held a carved door meant for a rebuilt seaside school. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts arrived to move it; {{otherPlayer}}’s shipping clerks had discovered its pallet shifting toward an open loading edge. Children outside waited to see the painted panels for the first time.

{{hero}} reached the pallet as a stranger tried to release its retaining strap. The fighter grabbed the strap, pushed the person clear, and held the load until movers set the pallet flat. The door’s panels showed fish, boats, and a row of children standing together beneath a painted roof.

The shipping clerks brought the door into the light where the waiting children could see it. One child asked why the artist had left a blank face in the row. A mover said it was for whoever entered the school next, and the children began naming one another.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the shed and delivered the school door.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s clerks retained the pallet and scheduled a safer loading crew.
endings.draw: The door remained intact, and both groups let the children see its painting before delivery.

paragraphs: A mobile care station stopped beside a school during a power outage, drawing families to its shaded courtyard. {{heroPlayer}}’s staff needed its generator; {{otherPlayer}}’s district workers found the cable stretched across the only accessible entrance. A parent pushing a chair waited at the far curb.

{{hero}} rerouted the cable overhead through the station’s raised support hooks and tested a clear path into the courtyard. The specialist brought the parent and child across while the workers guarded the newly suspended line. Inside, the child spotted a classroom art display visible through an open window.

After the station reopened, the child added a drawing of the care vehicle to that display. The parent returned to see it beside the other pictures, all hung low enough to read from the chair. The generator ran until the school lights came back.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s staff secured the station and kept the accessible entrance open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the courtyard and moved the station to a safer position.
endings.draw: Families reached the station safely, and both teams kept the cable above the path.

paragraphs: A rooftop transmitter stopped sending the neighborhood’s evening announcements just before a storm. {{heroPlayer}}’s technical crew climbed to repair it; {{otherPlayer}}’s city staff were preparing a community hall below. On the silent screen, one announcement remained queued: a request to bring spare blankets.

{{hero}} covered the rooftop stair while a technician connected a replacement aerial lead. A figure emerged from behind the cooling unit with a weapon, and the fighter held them back until the technician finished. The blanket request went out with the updated shelter address while the first rain struck the roof.

People arrived at the hall carrying more blankets than anyone had asked for. A child picked a bright one and spread it across two empty chairs for neighbors still on the way. The rooftop screen displayed the next announcement: all arrivals accounted for.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the transmitter and restored the shelter announcements.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the roof and organized the hall without the broadcast.
endings.draw: The hall filled safely, and both teams kept the announcements running through the storm.

paragraphs: A temporary aerial stage hung over a civic plaza for its annual night performance. {{heroPlayer}}’s performers arrived to test the rig; {{otherPlayer}}’s safety crew had seen one tether slacken above the audience seats. A young acrobat waited at the edge with a length of silver ribbon.

{{hero}} reached the tether as someone tried to pull its anchor free. The fighter wrestled them away and held the anchor while a rigger set a new lock. The acrobat crossed only after the safety crew gave the signal, her ribbon tracing a bright loop in the air.

The audience below saw the loop but never the repair behind it. Afterward, the acrobat left the ribbon tied to the safe anchor for the next rehearsal. A rigger kept it there until morning as a visible reminder to check the lock again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s performers secured the rig and completed the night show.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the plaza and suspended the aerial act.
endings.draw: The performance finished safely, and both groups inspected every tether afterward.

paragraphs: A workers’ dormitory shared one air recycler between its oldest and newest wings. {{heroPlayer}}’s maintenance crew arrived when the old rooms grew stuffy; {{otherPlayer}}’s building officers had already posted a notice asking residents to leave. One resident refused to go without a box of family photographs.

{{hero}} traced the airflow to a damper left closed after the new wing opened. The specialist freed its hinge and measured fresh air in both corridors while the officers guided residents outside. When it was safe to return, the resident carried the photograph box back into the oldest room.

The first picture unpacked showed the dormitory before its newest wing was built, with a garden in the space now occupied by a hall. A younger worker proposed putting plants in that hall. By evening, a few pots had appeared beneath its bright windows.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored air to both wings and reopened the dormitory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers retained the building and kept residents out for inspection.
endings.draw: The air stayed clear, and both parties welcomed the residents back.

paragraphs: A public scoreboard began counting fewer participants than the charity walk could see gathering in the square. {{heroPlayer}}’s data team came to fix its registration terminal; {{otherPlayer}}’s organizers were handing out paper numbers. A child had joined the walk without a device or a number.

{{hero}} found that the terminal skipped registrations made at the accessible entrance. The specialist merged the missing entries from the paper sheet while the organizers made space for everyone at the starting line. The count rose to include the child, who asked to have number one for a friend unable to attend.

The organizers pinned an extra number to an empty chair at the finish. When the walkers returned, the child left a small ribbon on that chair. The scoreboard showed the full count, including the registrations no device had recorded.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team repaired the terminal and recorded every walker.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s organizers retained registration and used paper numbers.
endings.draw: The walk began together, and both groups kept the full count on display.

paragraphs: An abandoned listening post began playing a low call that drew migrating birds down to its empty courtyard. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts escorted a researcher inside; {{otherPlayer}}’s district staff feared the birds would strike the glass tower nearby. The call sounded like a sea creature heard far from any shore.

{{hero}} held the listening room doorway while the researcher traced the sound to a looped old recording. A figure appeared behind the relay cabinet with a weapon, and the fighter kept them from the switch until the recording was saved and silenced. Outside, the birds rose together above the courtyard.

The researcher identified the call as one made by an animal recorded before the district existed. A staff member remembered hearing it on a classroom tape years earlier. They played a few seconds at low volume once more, this time with the tower windows covered.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts secured the post and protected the migrating birds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the courtyard and closed the tower approach.
endings.draw: The recording was preserved, and both teams watched the birds continue their flight.

paragraphs: A market freight scale sank under a stack of relief crates, blocking the station platform as a train approached. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to shift the load; {{otherPlayer}}’s station workers were holding passengers at the far stair. A small parcel slid from the top and landed beside the tracks.

{{hero}} reached the scale as a stranger tried to release its broken catch toward the train. The fighter seized the handle and held the stack while workers lifted crates to level ground. A worker retrieved the parcel from the rail bed before the train rounded the bend.

The parcel held a pair of worn shoes, sent from a parent to a child learning to run. It was handed to the family waiting at the station after the train stopped. The child put the shoes on before anyone could ask whether they fit.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the platform and cleared the freight scale.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the station and delayed the train.
endings.draw: The train arrived safely, and both teams carried the crates away from the tracks.

paragraphs: Tiny maintenance robots tended an urban aqueduct whose rain gutters watered a rooftop nursery. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians arrived when the robots began circling one dry junction; {{otherPlayer}}’s gardeners carried seedlings toward the roof. A single robot had found a gap too narrow for the others.

{{hero}} widened the inspection cover and found a tile wedged across the gutter. The specialist cleared it, then guided the robots through the restored channel without trapping the one beyond. Water reached the nursery as the gardeners set down their last tray of seedlings.

The smallest robot returned with a piece of the tile balanced on its body. It carried a painted green leaf, a fragment from an old roof sign. The gardeners set it beside the new seedlings while the robots resumed their quiet rounds.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians secured the aqueduct and restored the nursery supply.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s gardeners retained the roof and watered the seedlings by hand.
endings.draw: The water returned, and both groups watched the robots clear the junction.

paragraphs: A crater settlement used a slow-turning sky wheel to tell its night workers when dawn would reach the rim. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey team came after the wheel stopped; {{otherPlayer}}’s settlement crew feared the jam would leave a remote shift waiting in darkness. A narrow strip of reflected light remained fixed on a doorway.

{{hero}} cleared dust from the wheel’s bearings and found a small folded map beneath its housing. The specialist reset the mirror to send a dawn signal toward the remote shift, then opened the map. It showed the same doorway, with a handwritten note marking where hot drinks could be collected.

The waiting workers followed the returning beam to the settlement and found warm cups set out beside the door. One said the map had been drawn for their first winter there, when everyone got lost after dark. The wheel turned until sunlight replaced its signal.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors secured the sky wheel and guided the remote shift home.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the mechanism and sent guides out on foot.
endings.draw: The workers returned safely, and both groups kept the folded map beside the wheel.

paragraphs: A natural-history museum built a mirrored passage to show visitors how a habitat looked from an animal’s height. {{heroPlayer}}’s guides came to clear it after an alarm; {{otherPlayer}}’s curators had counted one fewer visitor leaving than entering. Footsteps echoed from behind a panel that appeared to be a wall.

{{hero}} reached the panel as a stranger tried to wedge it shut. The fighter pulled the wedge free and held the hidden door while a guide led the missing visitor through. The visitor carried a sketchbook full of drawings of the passage, each mirror marked with the exit it reflected.

The curators used the sketches to place visible arrows at eye level for younger visitors. Before leaving, the artist drew one more picture: the hidden door open, with every guide and curator reflected together in its glass.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guides secured the passage and found the missing visitor.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s curators retained the museum and closed the exhibit for repairs.
endings.draw: The visitor returned safely, and both groups added clearer exit signs.

paragraphs: At a spring kite festival, an automated wind board predicted that every kite would tangle over the same street. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts came to check its sensors; {{otherPlayer}}’s festival stewards were already moving families away. One little kite had risen smoothly where the board showed the strongest gust.

{{hero}} compared the board with the kite’s line and discovered the sensor had been mounted in the lee of a new rooftop canopy. The specialist moved it into clear air and revised the safe launch area. The stewards shifted the festival to a broad field, where the children lifted their kites one by one.

From the field, the board’s old predicted tangle looked like a cluster of roofs with no wind above them. A child sent the little kite toward the open sky and laughed as its line stayed clear of every other one.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts secured the board and found a safe launch field.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s stewards retained the festival and grounded the kites for the day.
endings.draw: The kites flew safely, and both teams kept the corrected wind readings on display.

paragraphs: A district archive began playing an unfinished oral-history recording over its public address system. {{heroPlayer}}’s security escort accompanied an archivist to the console; {{otherPlayer}}’s librarians moved visitors into a quiet reading room. The voice stopped just before naming the place where a garden had once stood.

{{hero}} covered the console corridor while the archivist recovered the damaged final spool. A figure moved behind the shelving with a weapon, and the fighter held the passage until the spool was safe. Replayed carefully, the voice named a courtyard hidden behind the archive’s newer wall.

The librarians opened a rear door and found the courtyard overgrown but still catching afternoon light. A visitor recognized the speaker as a relative who had planted its first tree. They listened to the recording again beneath that tree, now taller than the wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort secured the archive and preserved the full recording.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s librarians retained the console and closed the rear passage.
endings.draw: The voice was restored, and both groups visited the courtyard it described.

paragraphs: A public training arena had been turned into a temporary relief depot after a storm. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to secure its upper tier; {{otherPlayer}}’s depot workers were passing supplies through the old athletes’ entrance. A young runner had gone back for an elderly spectator left above.

{{hero}} reached the stair as a stranger tried to drop its barrier across the runner’s path. The fighter forced it open and held the landing while the runner helped the spectator down. Behind them, rainwater flowed over the tier where spectators had once painted names for every competitor.

The runner found their own name almost washed away and traced it with a finger before leaving. At the depot entrance, the elderly spectator offered the runner a dry blanket. Supplies kept moving through the arena while the storm passed beyond its open roof.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the upper tier and cleared the arena safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the depot and closed the unsafe stairs.
endings.draw: The runner and spectator came down, and both teams kept supplies moving.

paragraphs: A neighborhood planetarium closed during a school visit after a ceiling projector began showing two skies at once. {{heroPlayer}}’s public-safety team came to inspect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s school staff kept children beside the exit. One student insisted the second sky contained a star missing from the first.

{{hero}} opened the projection housing and found a second glass slide left in the lamp path. The specialist separated it from the current map and projected each sky in turn. The older slide showed a star chart drawn for the planetarium’s opening, complete with a handwritten dedication on its edge.

A teacher read the dedication to the children. It was addressed to anyone who found a new place in the sky to look. The student pointed again to the missing star, and the class drew their own chart before the projector was turned off.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the planetarium and restored the correct sky map.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s school staff retained the room and postponed the visit.
endings.draw: Both slides were saved, and the children finished their new chart together.

paragraphs: A rescue glider hung outside an orbital station’s docking ring with its pilot signaling through a frosted canopy. {{heroPlayer}}’s watch escorted a mechanic to the release controls; {{otherPlayer}}’s station operators warned that the ring was rotating out of alignment. The pilot’s last signal was a small circle drawn in condensation.

{{hero}} covered the access gantry while the mechanic adjusted the ring. A figure at the far controls raised a weapon, and the fighter held the approach until the glider could be drawn into the bay. Its canopy opened to reveal the pilot pointing toward a crack in the ring’s outer seal.

Operators repaired the seal before the next docking cycle. The pilot explained that the circle had meant the ring was turning around a damaged point, not that the glider was drifting. On a station window, a mechanic traced the same circle to teach the next watch where to look.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch secured the ring and brought the glider into the bay.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s operators retained the controls and delayed recovery until rotation stopped.
endings.draw: The pilot returned safely, and both groups repaired the cracked seal.

paragraphs: An underground library kept a small mushroom garden to clean the air in its deepest reading room. {{heroPlayer}}’s tunnel crew came after its ventilation fan slowed; {{otherPlayer}}’s librarians were guiding readers upward. The mushrooms had begun bending toward a thin shaft of light beneath the shelf.

{{hero}} traced the light to a forgotten service hatch and found its fan belt caught on a loose page of an old catalog. The specialist freed the belt and secured the page without tearing it. Air moved again, carrying the smell of damp earth through the reading room.

The recovered page described the garden when it was first planted, with notes from readers who had helped tend it. A librarian added the names of the tunnel crew to a new page. Readers returned to find the mushrooms upright beneath their shelf.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored ventilation and secured the library’s deepest room.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s librarians retained the room and closed it for repair.
endings.draw: The air cleared, and both groups kept the recovered catalog page with the garden records.

paragraphs: The last train had left the municipal depot, but its departure board kept printing a platform that no longer existed. {{heroPlayer}}’s people came for the route plans locked behind the board; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors were sealing the depot from the street. Beneath the tracks, a second train could be heard moving in darkness.

{{hero}} pushed through the service corridor as an opponent tried to close its steel gate. The fighter caught the gate, drove the opponent back, and reached the old signal room. There was no hidden train: a freight car had broken loose and was rolling toward the sealed underground platform.

The route plans lay within reach, but the signal lever would only stop the car if someone stayed to hold it. Above, the inspectors began forcing the corridor door. The car grew louder behind the wall, and the fighter had time to take either the plans or the lever first.

endings.heroWins: {{hero}} held the lever until {{heroPlayer}}’s people recovered the plans and cleared the platform.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the signal room and stopped the car while the plans remained sealed.
endings.draw: The car stopped short; each side escaped with a different page from the route plan.

paragraphs: The walled reservoir should have been empty. Instead its surface glowed green under the midnight lamps, and every gate into the adjoining orchard stood open. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey crew reached the intake from the hills; {{otherPlayer}}’s officers held the pump house. A downstream neighborhood had already reported green water in its taps.

{{hero}} slipped along the spillway to inspect the intake valve. The specialist found a dye capsule crushed against the grate and a second, unbroken capsule lodged inside the emergency bypass. Cutting the bypass would stop the color but leave the orchard without water until morning.

A warning horn sounded from the neighborhood as the officers crossed the pump house bridge. The intact capsule began to move in the current. The specialist braced a tool against the grate, knowing that opening it would release water and the capsule together unless the bypass could be shut first.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew shut the bypass, captured the capsule, and kept the reservoir under watch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers took the pump house and isolated the orchard before the capsule moved farther.
endings.draw: The capsule was trapped between closed gates, leaving both crews on opposite banks until daylight.

paragraphs: A neighborhood recording studio was sending a live evacuation warning when the signal cut to a single note. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort climbed the sound tower to restore the feed; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail had taken the street below. Inside the studio, an announcer continued speaking into a dead microphone.

{{hero}} covered the tower stair while a sound engineer traced the severed cable. Shapes moved behind the window opposite them; the fighter kept their heads down with measured fire, giving the engineer time to pull a spare lead through the wall. The speaker outside crackled, then returned with the announcer’s voice.

The first warning named a safe route through the market. The second named a shelter that the announcer suddenly realized was locked. Below, the opposing detail was already moving toward that building. The engineer could keep the broadcast open or leave with the escort to unlock it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the tower long enough to broadcast the corrected shelter route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail seized the street and silenced the tower before the second warning.
endings.draw: The broadcast reached the market, but each side controlled one end of the route to shelter.

paragraphs: A living relay tree rose through a rooftop observatory, its pale leaves flashing messages from a distant research camp. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers arrived to read a new sequence; {{otherPlayer}}’s guards were already cutting the stair access. The tree’s roots reached a cistern that had begun to drain.

{{hero}} climbed the exterior lattice with a portable reader and caught the sequence before the leaves dimmed. The specialist found the cistern outlet forced open beneath the roof. Restoring the water would keep the tree alive, but the reader needed power from the same pump to send a reply.

The message said the distant camp had lost its own relay and could see the rooftop flashes only until dawn. Water rattled down the open outlet; footsteps sounded on the observatory stairs. The specialist held the pump cable in one hand and the reader in the other.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers saved the tree and sent a reply before dawn.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the observatory and cut the message short.
endings.draw: The tree survived on a trickle, while the distant camp received only part of the reply.

paragraphs: An auction hall was empty except for a revolving stage and a crate marked for collection before sunrise. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors had been hired to retrieve the crate; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators had locked down the hall. Someone restarted the stage, carrying the crate toward a trapdoor in the floor.

{{hero}} leapt onto the moving platform and collided with a defender beside the crate. The fighter forced the defender away from the latch, then saw that the crate held a reel of testimony rather than any valuable object. Under the platform, a conveyor was already pulling at its trailing strap.

The trapdoor opened a handspan. There was room to grab the crate, or to seize the stage brake before everyone standing on it dropped into the machinery. Across the hall, the investigators broke through the locked entrance, their lights sweeping over the turning floor.

endings.heroWins: {{hero}} stopped the stage and {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors carried out the reel.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the crate as the contractors escaped the machinery.
endings.draw: The stage stopped, but the reel came loose; both sides left with fragments of its testimony.

paragraphs: A customs barge lay moored under a river bridge with one refrigerated container still aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards were hired to deliver it to a field clinic; {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors had marked it for seizure. As the tide rose, the bridge began pressing against the container’s lifting rig.

{{hero}} took position behind the barge wheelhouse while a crane operator tried to lower the rig. A defender fired from the far bank; the fighter answered through a gap in the rail, protecting the operator as the cable came taut. The container shifted free, but its temperature warning started blinking.

The operator had one lift left before the bridge trapped the rig. The clinic waited downstream with its lights on; the inspectors had a truck at the nearer bank. The fighter could see both routes from the wheelhouse and heard the warning beep accelerate inside the container.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards got the container onto the clinic boat before its cooling failed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors took custody on the nearer bank and held the cargo for examination.
endings.draw: The container reached shore, but both parties had to share its dwindling cooling supply.

paragraphs: A foundry was casting the final gear for a floodgate that protected the workers’ quarter. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired crew came to collect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal team had secured the casting floor. The first test fit was due at dawn, and rain had already reached the lower streets.

{{hero}} crossed the hot floor as a defender tried to close the cooling pit over the fresh gear. The fighter drove them off the handle and held the cover open while a worker hooked the casting. Its teeth were still hot enough to burn through the carrying straps.

A second set of straps hung on the far wall, beyond a line of workers sheltering from flying sparks. The rain hammered harder on the roof. If the casting cooled in the pit, it might crack; if moved too early, it might tear free before it reached the gate.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew carried the gear to the floodgate in time for the rising water.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team retained the foundry and fitted the gear under its own supervision.
endings.draw: The gear reached the gate, but neither side could claim it before the flood receded.

paragraphs: A solar balloon above the civic square carried the only working signal between the district and its outer farms. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to retrieve its data capsule; {{otherPlayer}}’s officers ordered the tether cut after its shadow fell across the emergency landing pad. A farm vehicle was already approaching the pad.

{{hero}} climbed the balloon mast and found the capsule locked beneath a panel that had warped in the sun. The specialist freed it, then saw a second tether running toward the landing lights. Cutting the balloon loose would clear the pad but take the capsule out of reach.

The vehicle’s approach light appeared over the rooftops. The officers began pulling on the emergency cable below while the technicians called for one more minute. From the mast, the specialist could feel the balloon tugging against both tethers as the sun slipped behind cloud.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew recovered the capsule and cleared the pad before the vehicle landed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers cut the balloon free and kept the landing lane open.
endings.draw: The vehicle landed, but the capsule fell into the square between the two waiting groups.

paragraphs: On a ridge of wind turbines, the district’s water pumps depended on one turning generator. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort brought a mechanic to repair its damaged brake; {{otherPlayer}}’s security detail held the service road. In the valley, a line of empty water carts was forming at the pump station.

{{hero}} held the tower platform while the mechanic crawled into the brake housing. Shots struck the railing from the road, and the fighter fired back to keep the mechanic beneath cover. The turbine began turning again, but a loosened blade bolt knocked against its hub on every rotation.

The mechanic could stop the machine to tighten the bolt, risking another stall, or leave it spinning long enough to fill the waiting carts. The noise became louder as the opposing detail reached the tower stairs. From the valley came the first faint sound of water entering a cart.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the tower while the pumps filled the waiting carts.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail secured the turbine and shut it down for repair.
endings.draw: A few carts filled before the turbine stopped; both sides guarded the tower until the blade was safe.

paragraphs: Two recovery teams reached opposite airlocks of the same drifting refinery, each carrying orders to secure its emergency reactor. {{heroPlayer}}’s people came from the service craft; {{otherPlayer}}’s arrived along the outer truss. Between them, the refinery’s rotation pulled a loose cargo net across the only passage.

{{hero}} entered the central control room as the net struck its window. The specialist found two shutdown controls: one would stabilize the refinery but seal the outer airlock, while the other would keep both exits open and let the reactor run hotter. A second team’s lights appeared at the far door.

A voice over the intercom called that a worker remained outside on the truss. The reactor gauge climbed. The specialist had a hand on each control and no way to see whether the worker was nearer the service craft or the outer airlock.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team stabilized the refinery and pulled the worker through the service hatch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team took the control room and rescued the worker through the outer airlock.
endings.draw: Both exits stayed open just long enough for the worker to cross, leaving the reactor under shared watch.

paragraphs: Snow had buried the pass markers, leaving a medical convoy stalled above a steep ravine. {{heroPlayer}}’s climbers followed a rope toward the old beacon hut; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored escorts had secured the road below. A second rope, newly cut, dangled from the hut’s upper window.

{{hero}} climbed the exposed ladder as a defender leaned out to push it loose. The fighter caught the defender at the sill and forced a way inside. The hut’s beacon battery was missing, but the convoy’s lead vehicle still had enough power to run it through a long cable.

The cable had to be stretched across the ravine in full view of the escorts. Somewhere behind the snowfall, an engine started and the convoy began to move without its markers. The fighter held the empty battery socket while the climbers carried the cable into the white air.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s climbers relit the beacon and guided the convoy along the safe edge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s escorts took the hut and directed the convoy down their road.
endings.draw: The beacon flashed once, enough for both groups to stop the convoy before the ravine.

paragraphs: A forest communications bunker held the last working map of a firebreak that had vanished beneath new growth. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers entered to recover it; {{otherPlayer}}’s advance guard watched the ridge above. Smoke from a distant brushfire threaded through the ventilation grille, carrying the scent of wet pine.

{{hero}} found the map sealed inside a waterproof tube beneath the bunker floor. The specialist unrolled it and saw a hand-drawn shortcut around the ridge, but the ink had run where someone had marked a new water source. Outside, the advance guard began descending toward the bunker entrance.

The rangers could follow the old firebreak, whose trees had grown back, or gamble on the shortcut and search for the lost water source. The smoke thickened while the specialist traced both lines with a gloved finger. A whistle sounded once from the ridge and was not answered.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers found the hidden water source and cut a new line around the fire.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard secured the bunker and controlled the only usable map.
endings.draw: Both groups followed different paths to the same stream and held opposite banks through the night.

paragraphs: A stone quarry served as the emergency loading yard for a hillside town. {{heroPlayer}}’s protection detail came for a stack of flood barriers; {{otherPlayer}}’s laborers were already hauling them toward a different gate. On the ridge, a section of drainage wall had begun to crack.

{{hero}} held the quarry ramp while a loader carried the first barrier uphill. Gunfire struck the rail beside the machine, and the fighter returned fire from behind a stone block, keeping the driver moving. The cracked wall split wider, pouring water into the lower lane between both gates.

There were enough barriers to close one gate before the water reached it, but the second would remain exposed. The loader stopped where the road divided. Over the engine’s noise, a bell sounded from the neighborhood below one gate; no one could tell whether the other neighborhood had a warning.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail secured the barriers and protected the first threatened street.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s laborers took the barriers to their gate before the lane flooded.
endings.draw: The load was split between the gates, leaving both neighborhoods with a narrow but uncertain defense.

paragraphs: A relief train stopped on a viaduct after its far signal switched to red. {{heroPlayer}}’s rapid response crew arrived along the maintenance walk; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries held the station at the far end. Below the bridge, floodwater carried a broken signal pole toward a support.

{{hero}} opened the trackside control box and found a loose wire making the signal flash at random. The specialist could lock the points for the train, but doing so would trap a maintenance trolley still approaching from behind. The trolley’s lamp appeared through the rain before its driver could hear the warning.

The train’s passengers began to move toward the doors as the water struck the support below. The specialist needed the trolley stopped and the far station cleared before the train could cross. Across the viaduct, the sentries switched on their own signal, a green light that did not explain the red one.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew stopped the trolley and brought the relief train through.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries secured the station and held the train on the viaduct.
endings.draw: The train and trolley both stopped safely, one at each end of the damaged points.

paragraphs: A landing capsule fell into a mountain radio array, snapping the dish away from the villages it served. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew followed the impact trail; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored patrol had reached the station from the road. A voice transmitted from the capsule, counting down the minutes of its remaining air.

{{hero}} reached the dish controls and found the damaged arm could be turned toward either the capsule or the valley, but the motor would survive only one more movement. The specialist sent a short signal to the capsule; its pilot answered with a location beyond the visible wreckage.

Snow began to fall over the array. A rescue team needed the dish aimed at the pilot to locate the hidden compartment, while the villages needed it pointed outward for weather warnings. The armored patrol climbed the station steps as the last minute of air was called.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew found the pilot and repaired the array before the next weather report.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol kept the dish aimed at the valley and secured the wreck for later recovery.
endings.draw: The pilot’s last signal was heard in both directions; each side searched from a different path.

paragraphs: A winter fuel depot was the last heated building between two isolated towns. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to protect its tanks; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored column had reached the service road. The depot keeper said a single tanker could still move, but its engine would start only if the generator stayed on.

{{hero}} covered the loading ramp while the keeper connected the tanker. Shots broke the glass of the control booth, and the fighter answered from behind a snowplow, keeping the hose crew working. The generator caught, the tanker started, and a gauge on the largest tank dropped toward empty.

Fuel was already flowing into the vehicle, enough for one town if it left now. The other town’s message flashed across the booth screen asking whether a second load was possible. The column advanced through the snow as the keeper reached for the valve that would decide.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol got the tanker away and kept the depot running for a second load.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s column secured the tanks and chose the first destination.
endings.draw: The tanker left half full while both sides guarded the fuel needed for the second town.

paragraphs: At a prairie grain silo, maintenance drones began circling overhead instead of sealing its roof before rain. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers came for the stored harvest; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored scouts held the approach road. The silo manager had already sent families to stack empty sacks beneath the dripping seam.

{{hero}} reached the drone station and found its guidance marker torn from the roof hatch. The specialist held a replacement marker against the wind until the first drone returned to the seam. Its welding arm sparked; the rain quickened, and grain shifted against the wall inside.

The drones could finish the roof only if the station remained powered, but its cable crossed the road where the scouts were advancing. The manager started loading dry grain onto a wagon as insurance. Each spark above him disappeared in the rain before anyone could tell whether it held.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers kept the drones working and saved the stored harvest.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the station while the manager moved what grain remained dry.
endings.draw: The roof held in patches; both groups carried sacks out before the next storm.

paragraphs: A border care station had sealed its supply room during a dust storm, leaving travelers waiting outside with no way to reach their packed provisions. {{heroPlayer}}’s aid crew arrived from the inland road; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored guards controlled the courtyard. A generator inside the room kept running although its door was locked.

{{hero}} followed the generator’s exhaust to a small maintenance opening and found a release cable hidden beneath the wall. The specialist pulled it, but the latch only lifted halfway. There was enough room to pass provisions through, one package at a time, while sand gathered around the opening.

The travelers called out the name of a child missing from their group. Behind the supply shelves came a muffled answer. The crew could widen the opening by cutting its frame, risking the air seal, or wait for the guards to bring the proper key through the storm.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew opened the room and brought the child and supplies into shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the room and controlled its opening after the storm.
endings.draw: The child answered through the gap as both groups passed supplies to the waiting travelers.

paragraphs: A night dispatch office held a strip of coded rail orders that could divert a relief train from a blocked tunnel. {{heroPlayer}}’s courier entered through the roof hatch; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored sentries guarded the station concourse. The dispatch printer was still feeding paper into a bin already half full.

{{hero}} watched the office stairs while the courier searched for the newest strip. A sentry pushed through the lower door, and the fighter fired to hold the landing as the courier found the correct order. Its code matched the tunnel warning, but the route change had not reached the train.

The station radio was beside the lower door, in sight of the sentries. The train’s headlight appeared beyond the curve as the printer fed out another copy, already marked obsolete. The courier held the true strip and looked at the fighter, waiting for a path to the transmitter.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s courier reached the radio and diverted the train before the tunnel.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries secured the office and sent their own instructions.
endings.draw: The train stopped at the junction while both sides argued over the coded route.

paragraphs: A dry dock filled unexpectedly as its floodgate opened under an unfinished rescue boat. {{heroPlayer}}’s dockhands came for the boat; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored crew held the gate machinery. A worker remained under the hull, fastening its last support with water rising around the cradle.

{{hero}} reached the gate wheel as a defender tried to turn it wider. The fighter pulled the defender from the handle and held the wheel against the flood while dockhands called to the worker below. The cradle began to shift; water forced a narrow channel between the boat and the wall.

Closing the gate completely would strand the unfinished boat high above the worker. Leaving it open would float the hull before its supports were ready. The worker shouted that the final fastening was nearly done, but their voice disappeared beneath the sound of the rising water.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s dockhands saved the worker and launched the rescue boat intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew took the gate and lifted the worker out while the boat stayed in the dock.
endings.draw: The worker escaped, and the boat floated loose between the opposing crews.

paragraphs: The care depot at the edge of the desert was cooling boxes for three towns when the electricity failed. {{heroPlayer}}’s field team came through the service entrance; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored detachment held the loading bay. A line of drivers waited outside, each claiming their town needed the first box.

{{hero}} reached the backup generator and found its fuel line pierced. The specialist clamped the leak and brought it back to life, but the cooling room had already warmed. The log showed that only one box could be sent immediately without a new inspection.

A runner arrived with word that the road to one town would close at dusk. The drivers stepped forward together, their headlights already on. The specialist could hear the armored detachment at the bay door as the cooling unit steadied and the first box was pulled toward the light.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s field team secured the depot and dispatched the boxes along safe routes.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detachment took the loading bay and controlled the first shipment.
endings.draw: One box left before dusk; both sides held the remaining cargo under cooling overnight.

paragraphs: A habitat’s central gravity junction failed during an evacuation drill, sending loose equipment drifting through the corridor. {{heroPlayer}}’s mechanics came to restore it; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored escort had sealed the only route to the lower shelter. People waited at the doors holding their children by the wrists.

{{hero}} floated behind a service bulkhead while a mechanic reached the junction panel. Shots sparked against the handrails, and the fighter fired from the bulkhead to keep the mechanic clear. The panel lit up, but its readout showed two conflicting gravity vectors, one pulling toward the sealed doors.

The first child slipped from a parent’s grip and began drifting toward the junction. The mechanic could select one vector blindly or wait for the sensor to recalibrate; the fighter had to leave cover to catch the child. A warning klaxon began counting down to the next automatic reset.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s mechanics restored the corridor and brought the evacuees to shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s escort secured the junction and rerouted the evacuation.
endings.draw: The child reached safety, but both crews held the corridor while gravity steadied.

paragraphs: A suspended walkway linked a gallery of illuminated sculptures to the district’s emergency tower. {{heroPlayer}}’s performers were clearing the gallery for a storm; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored guard occupied the tower. One sculpture kept swinging against the walkway cable, flashing red with every impact.

{{hero}} stepped onto the swaying bridge as a defender reached for its anchor pin. The fighter shoved them back and held the pin in place while a rigger caught the swinging sculpture with a safety line. The red flashes stopped, revealing a steady light aimed at the tower window.

Someone inside the tower answered with two brief flashes. The storm had disabled its radio, and the signal was the only reply the performers had received. The rigger could secure the sculpture or swing it deliberately to send a message while the bridge strained beneath them.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s performers kept the bridge intact and signaled the people in the tower.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard secured the tower and closed the walkway.
endings.draw: Both sides exchanged a brief signal before the sculpture was lowered out of the wind.

paragraphs: A cargo port’s pressure gate was stuck open while a salvage shuttle approached with a damaged seal. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock crew came to close the gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored technicians had taken the control booth. Behind the shuttle, a trail of loose containers was drifting into the docking lane.

{{hero}} reached the manual wheel and discovered that closing it would trap the shuttle outside until the damaged seal was repaired. The specialist set a temporary catch and called for the pilot to slow, while a dockhand pulled a container out of the lane with a tether.

The shuttle’s oxygen indicator flashed low. A second container struck the outer gate, knocking the catch loose. The specialist had one hand on the wheel and the other on a release cord that could pull the shuttle inside, provided the control booth did not override the lock first.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew brought the shuttle into a sealed berth and cleared the containers.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians took the gate controls and ordered the shuttle to hold outside.
endings.draw: The shuttle sheltered at the threshold while both crews fought to keep the gate from closing.

paragraphs: A records vault began erasing the identity files of everyone registered at the district shelter. {{heroPlayer}}’s data specialists entered from the municipal side; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored detail guarded the server floor. Outside, evacuees waited for the files they needed to cross the next checkpoint.

{{hero}} found the erasure coming from a failing backup drive, not an instruction sent by a person. The specialist copied the intact names to a portable unit, but the recovery key remained behind a locked server cage. The armored detail’s footsteps sounded on the stair above it.

The checkpoint announced it would close in ten minutes. The copied files could get most people through, while the missing key would restore the few names already lost. The specialist held the portable unit and looked at the cage as a final drive light went dark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s specialists recovered the key and brought the full roster to the checkpoint.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the vault and issued its own verified roster.
endings.draw: Most evacuees crossed, while both sides searched for the names still missing from the drive.

paragraphs: A geological scanner above an abandoned mine began drawing shapes that looked like rooms beneath the rock. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party came to preserve its readings; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored scouts were approaching along the tram tracks. From the mine entrance came a brief light, although its power had been cut for years.

{{hero}} covered the scanner deck while a geologist transferred its data. A burst of fire struck the gantry; the fighter answered from behind the scanner housing, buying time for the transfer. The final reading showed a narrow shaft connecting the buried rooms to the dark mine entrance.

The light flashed again, twice this time. The geologist could carry the data away or use the shaft coordinates to find whoever was below. The armored scouts reached the last bend of track, and the scanner’s display began to fade under a rising charge warning.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors found the shaft and escaped with the readings intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the scanner and closed the mine entrance.
endings.draw: Both sides left with a partial map, while the light beneath the rock continued to flash.

paragraphs: A cliffside pump drew drinking water through a stone amphitheater used as an emergency gathering place. {{heroPlayer}}’s assault party reached its lower steps; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored defenders held the control terrace. Below them, families waited with empty containers as a warning light blinked on the pump.

{{hero}} drove into a defender at the terrace rail and pulled them away from the manual cutoff. The fighter held the narrow landing while a technician opened the pump casing. Inside, the pressure seal had torn, and water was draining back into the cliff faster than it could reach the taps.

A replacement seal sat in a crate beside the defenders’ position. The technician waved for it while the fighter heard people calling from the steps below. Without the seal, the pump might run dry before dawn; crossing the terrace for the crate would leave the cutoff unguarded.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party secured the seal and kept water flowing to the gathering place.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s defenders held the terrace and repaired the pump themselves.
endings.draw: The pump delivered a small reserve while both groups held opposite sides of the terrace.

paragraphs: A living filter beneath the commuter tunnels had stopped cleansing the station’s water. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers entered its maintenance chamber; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored guards controlled the main stair. On the filter’s glass wall, a pattern of dark spots was spreading toward the outlet.

{{hero}} checked the nutrient lines and found one feeding the wrong side of the filter. The specialist corrected the flow, and pale color returned to part of the living membrane. The rest stayed dark. A sample taken from the outlet showed the change had reached the water already stored upstairs.

The station could close its taps immediately, leaving waiting travelers without a supply, or keep them open while the membrane recovered. Footsteps descended the guarded stair as the specialist raised the alarm. Inside the chamber, the pale patch grew, too slowly to settle the choice.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers isolated the stored water and restored the filter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the chamber and closed the station taps.
endings.draw: The taps stayed closed through the night while both groups watched the membrane recover.

paragraphs: A lunar mirror array carried daylight to a settlement cut into the crater wall. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians reached its hub after one mirror began turning toward an unused shaft; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored patrol stood between the hub and the settlement’s power room. A child’s voice reported darkness inside the school.

{{hero}} climbed the hub and found the control wheel split along an old repair seam. The specialist held the damaged mirror in place with a temporary brace, restoring light to one classroom. The rest of the array would follow only if the main motor could be restarted from the guarded power room.

The brace creaked as the sun moved across the crater. On the radio, the child said the light was sliding slowly off the desks. A technician offered to hold the mirror by hand while the specialist crossed to the motor, but the hub had no second safety line.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians restarted the array and filled the school with daylight.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the motor and directed the mirrors toward the settlement.
endings.draw: One classroom stayed lit while both parties worked from opposite ends of the damaged array.

paragraphs: An enclosed research garden locked its doors as a fast-growing vine crossed the ventilation shaft. {{heroPlayer}}’s infiltrators came through the lower service route; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored custodians held the public entrance. A researcher remained inside, visible through the fogged glass with a sealed specimen in hand.

{{hero}} met a defender at the service hatch and wrestled them away from its closing wheel. The fighter held the hatch open while a teammate pulled the researcher through. The specimen case caught on the sill; on its label, the researcher had written a warning about the vine’s rapid spread.

The custodians started sealing the ventilation shaft above them. The researcher could carry the case clear, or open it to confirm whether the warning described a harmless growth phase. The vine pressed against the vent grille as the hatch wheel began to turn again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team recovered the specimen and got the researcher out before the shaft sealed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s custodians held the garden and kept the specimen inside for inspection.
endings.draw: The researcher reached the service passage while the sealed case remained between the two crews.

paragraphs: A city evacuation map predicted a safe crossing over a canal that no longer had a bridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts reached the traffic center as residents began moving toward the missing span; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored responders held the control floor. On the map, the bridge remained drawn in bright green.

{{hero}} traced the bad route to a survey image copied before the bridge was removed. The specialist deleted the false crossing and found two real ones, each too narrow for the full crowd. Traffic lights could divide the evacuees, but their power depended on a failing battery bank.

A camera showed the first families already turning down the dead-end street. The battery warning flashed as the armored responders approached the controls. The specialist held a hand over the route switch, needing to choose which crossing should receive the first green lights.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts split the crowd safely between the two real bridges.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s responders seized the center and directed people by ground patrol.
endings.draw: The false route vanished, but each side guided a separate line across the canal.

paragraphs: An encrypted transmitter in a hillside tunnel carried the only contact with a trapped excavation crew. {{heroPlayer}}’s operators came for its key module; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored team held the main access shaft. The voices underground had fallen from three to two during the last transmission.

{{hero}} covered the transmitter alcove while an operator removed the failing module. Fire struck the tunnel mouth; the fighter held the angle and kept the operator beneath the alcove’s concrete lip. A fresh key came online, but the next voice reported that rising water had reached the crew’s equipment.

A rescue winch stood beyond the shaft held by the armored team. The operator could stay to guide the crew by radio or carry the module to the winch and risk losing contact in transit. Water dripped from the ceiling as the third voice finally answered with a weak tap.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s operators held the transmitter and guided all three workers to the winch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team took the shaft and ran the rescue through its own line.
endings.draw: Two workers emerged while both sides searched the flooded passage for the third.

paragraphs: The memorial arena’s water tower had been filled for an approaching fire, but its lower supports were cracking under the weight. {{heroPlayer}}’s fighters crossed the arena to reach the release valve; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored unit held the platform. Families waiting outside needed the water carried to the fire line.

{{hero}} climbed the tower stair and met a defender beside the valve. The fighter drove them into the railing and held the platform while a volunteer opened the release. Water rushed into the waiting hoses, but a support beam split and dropped onto the stair behind them.

The volunteer could close the valve and save the tower, leaving hoses half full, or keep it open until the tank drained and risk trapping everyone on the platform. The fire appeared over the arena wall as the fighter tested the broken stair with one foot.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s fighters kept the water flowing and brought the volunteer down safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s unit secured the tower and rationed the water for the fire line.
endings.draw: The hoses filled partway before the valve closed, leaving both teams to hold the tower together.

paragraphs: A temporary tribunal had been built around the only copy of a missing-persons registry after the floods. {{heroPlayer}}’s record keepers came to secure it; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored officers were clearing the hall for an evacuation. The registry’s final pages had been left on a table beside an open window.

{{hero}} gathered the loose pages and matched them to their binding marks while rain blew through the room. The specialist found one page written in a different hand, listing people still waiting at a shelter outside the evacuation zone. Their names had never been entered into the official count.

An officer called that the transport would leave in minutes. The specialist could carry the complete registry onto it or send someone to the uncounted shelter with the newly discovered page. At the open window, rain began to erase the address written in the margin.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s keepers saved the registry and brought the uncounted people onto transport.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers evacuated the hall with the registry under their custody.
endings.draw: The registry survived, but both sides went separately to check the uncounted shelter.

paragraphs: A service craft hung from the outer docking ring of a station, its cable snagged on a broken antenna. {{heroPlayer}}’s watch moved to recover the craft; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored unit controlled the inside hatch. A worker in the craft held up a hand with four fingers, showing the minutes left on their air display.

{{hero}} took cover behind the ring’s maintenance rail while a mechanic crawled out on a tether. Shots struck the rail, and the fighter returned fire to keep the mechanic moving. The antenna tore free, but the craft swung toward an unlit docking port whose seal had not been tested.

The mechanic could tow the craft into that port immediately or pull it around the ring toward a certified hatch that was farther away. The worker held up three fingers. Inside, the armored unit began cycling the inner hatch, and the mechanic’s tether tightened against the station wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch brought the worker through the certified hatch with air to spare.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s unit took the docking controls and recovered the craft at the near port.
endings.draw: The craft reached the ring as both sides worked together to test the unlit port seal.

paragraphs: An underground waystation kept the tunnel air moving with a fan cut into the rock. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue crew arrived after travelers reported smoke near the lower exit; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored column had stopped at the upper gate. Inside, the fan was turning backward, pushing smoke toward the occupied sleeping rooms.

{{hero}} opened the fan housing and found the direction switch jammed by a piece of melted insulation. The specialist freed it and restored the draft, but a sensor showed fresh smoke entering from a second passage. A family behind the sleeping-room door began knocking for help.

Turning the fan faster might clear the rooms while drawing the new smoke deeper into the station. Shutting it down would buy time to reach the family but leave the tunnel air still. The armored column started opening the upper gate as the specialist held the switch between its two settings.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew cleared the rooms and brought the family out through clean air.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s column took the station and opened a different escape shaft.
endings.draw: The family reached the corridor, but both sides kept the fan at low speed while searching for the smoke.

paragraphs: A narrow timber bridge carried the annual remembrance procession across a mountain stream. {{heroPlayer}}’s procession guards reached it with lanterns; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored unit held the far bank. Beneath the planks, floodwater had taken the central support while people were still walking onto the bridge.

{{hero}} met a defender at the entrance and pulled them away from the barricade, making room for the procession to retreat. The fighter then caught a fallen beam against the remaining post while a carpenter secured a rope across the gap. On the far side, someone raised a lantern in reply.

The bridge could hold only a few people at a time, and the procession carried more lanterns than there were hands to spare. Rain swelled the stream as the carpenter called for the first crossing. The fighter felt the beam shift under its weight and saw the far-bank lantern go dark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards brought the procession across and kept the bridge standing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s unit secured the far bank and redirected the procession upstream.
endings.draw: The people crossed in small groups, leaving both sides holding the rope until the last lantern passed.

paragraphs: A hillside shrine had kept a water clock running through generations of drought. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came when its bowls emptied before dawn; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored watch controlled the terrace above. The clock’s last drop fell just as a bell below announced the opening of the village wells.

{{hero}} followed the supply channel beneath the shrine and found a fresh diversion feeding an unused upper cistern. The specialist closed it and sent a trickle back toward the clock. At the village, however, a second bell began to ring: the wells were running low too.

There was enough water to restart the clock or fill the village’s morning reserve first. A caretaker said the clock could wait, but its mechanism held the only record of how the channels had been divided in earlier droughts. Footsteps crossed the terrace overhead as light reached the first bowl.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers recovered the channel records and sent water to the village wells.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch secured the cistern and rationed its supply.
endings.draw: The clock stayed silent while both sides measured what remained for the village.

paragraphs: A dispatch office above the express line lost contact with the train carrying emergency bridge parts. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal escort entered from the east stair; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored guards held the platforms below. Through the window, the train was visible but approaching a switch set toward a closed tunnel.

{{hero}} covered the signaler as they reached the manual lever. A burst of fire hit the stair rail, and the fighter answered from behind the dispatch desk, holding the upper floor. The lever moved halfway before its cable snapped, leaving the switch pointed between both routes.

A ground signaler could finish the change at the track, but the office radio was the only way to warn them. The train’s horn sounded beneath the window as the fighter watched the stairs and the signaler tried to raise a voice through a damaged microphone.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the office and steered the train onto the safe track.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the platforms and stopped the train before the switch.
endings.draw: The train halted between signals while both parties repaired their half of the line.

paragraphs: A canopy archive stored its history in living leaf patterns high above a border settlement. {{heroPlayer}}’s readers came to copy a new pattern; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored patrol controlled the path beneath the trees. A spreading gray mark had already erased part of the lowest branch.

{{hero}} climbed through the canopy and found dry sap where a water line should have fed the branch. The specialist restored the line and photographed the remaining pattern. The gray mark slowed, but the newest leaves began changing shape, as though the archive had been writing through the damage.

The copied image showed a warning about the settlement’s old boundary trail, now used by children returning from school. The trail could be closed before anyone read the full pattern, or the reader could stay until the last leaves opened. Below, the patrol began cutting through the undergrowth toward the path.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s readers completed the warning and guided the children along a safe route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the trail and closed the canopy archive.
endings.draw: The children turned back while both sides waited for the new leaves to finish opening.

paragraphs: A warehouse by the old canal had become the only dry store for a neighborhood’s winter food. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors were hired to bring out the crates; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored patrol had locked the street entrance. Beneath the warehouse, a disused loading tunnel was filling with canal water.

{{hero}} came through the tunnel and met a defender beside the freight lift. The fighter drove them back from its release chain and held the platform while workers pushed a crate aboard. The lift groaned upward, but the water beneath it carried a second chain toward the gears.
