There was time to send one load to street level before the chain fouled the lift. Outside, the patrol’s engine started; below, a worker shouted that more food remained in the dark. The fighter held the release chain, weighing the load already rising against the people still underground.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew cleared the tunnel and carried the winter food out before the lift failed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the warehouse and controlled distribution from the street.
endings.draw: One load escaped as the lift stopped, leaving both groups to retrieve the rest by hand.

paragraphs: A crater observatory held a sealed sample from the first meteor survey of the region. {{heroPlayer}}’s security team had orders to escort it to a laboratory; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored detachment took the access road. The observatory’s dome had stopped turning, leaving its one open slit aimed at the rising sun.

{{hero}} covered the sample room while a researcher prepared the container for travel. Shots broke the upper glass, and the fighter answered from beneath the dome frame, keeping the researcher away from the windows. The sample’s outer seal remained intact, but its insulated case began flashing a heat warning.

The road vehicle waited below the detachment’s position; a smaller service sled stood beside the dome. The researcher could carry the case to either one, but sunlight would reach the open slit first. The fighter watched the shadows shorten across the floor as another shot struck the frame.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team reached the laboratory with the sample still sealed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detachment secured the road and retained the sample at the observatory.
endings.draw: The case stayed cool in the service sled while both sides held opposite sides of the dome.

paragraphs: A refinery’s reserve fuel line ran beneath housing built for the people who worked there. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired crew came to isolate a leak; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored guards held the valve house. Families had gathered on a footbridge above the line, watching a dark patch spread through the gravel.

{{hero}} fought a defender away from the valve wheel while a technician clamped the damaged pipe. The fighter held the valve against the flow as the technician called for pressure to drop. Instead, a gauge rose: the backup pump had started somewhere beyond the guardhouse.

Closing the wheel would stop the leak but push pressure toward the footbridge supports. The technician could reach the backup switch only by crossing the guarded yard. Above, a parent began guiding the families away as the fighter felt the wheel turn harder beneath both hands.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew shut down the backup pump and protected the housing.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the valve house and cleared the bridge themselves.
endings.draw: The leak slowed, and both teams evacuated the bridge before isolating the last pump.

paragraphs: An old communications tower had begun transmitting two different distress locations on the same channel. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to identify the real call; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored scouts controlled the maintenance road. At the tower’s base, two families waited, each insisting the missing traveler belonged to them.

{{hero}} traced one transmission to a recently repaired repeater and the other to a battery hidden inside the stairwell. The specialist played the calls at half speed. One voice asked for rescue at a river crossing; the second repeated the same words with the breaths missing between them.

The repeater’s battery was nearly spent. The technician could send a reply to the live caller or preserve both recordings for the families, but there was power for only one more transmission. An armored vehicle stopped below as the two families listened for the next breath.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians reached the live caller and returned with the missing traveler.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the tower and sent their own rescue party.
endings.draw: Both calls were saved, and the families followed separate routes to the crossing.

paragraphs: The rail yard’s refrigeration wagon held seed stock for a valley struck by blight. {{heroPlayer}}’s security escort came to move it; {{otherPlayer}}’s armored troops had reached the switching station. The wagon’s cooling unit sputtered as workers tried to couple it to the only powered engine.

{{hero}} took cover beside a signal shed while the coupling crew crossed the open track. Fire struck the shed roof; the fighter answered, keeping the workers low until the connector locked. The engine pulled forward a handspan, then stopped at a switch set toward a collapsed bridge.

A manual lever stood between the opposing positions. The engine driver had no sight of the broken span; the cooling gauge was falling behind him. The fighter could hold the shed or break cover for the lever before the driver committed to the wrong track.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort threw the switch and delivered the chilled seed stock.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s troops secured the yard and took the wagon into custody.
endings.draw: The wagon stopped short of the broken bridge while both crews fought to keep its cooling unit alive.

paragraphs: Two mountain rescue teams reached a snowbound dam from opposite ridges, both carrying orders to keep its floodgate open. {{heroPlayer}}’s climbers found the control hut first; {{otherPlayer}}’s team had brought a warning that ice was blocking the spillway below. If the gate stayed open, water would rise behind the ice.

{{hero}} inspected the hut’s manual drive and discovered the gate could be raised in small steps while a sensor watched the spillway. The specialist lifted it once, then waited. The sensor showed a narrow channel forming beneath the ice, but a sharp crack came from the dam’s upper face.

The two teams called different readings over the same radio channel. One believed the crack was in the ice; the other had seen fresh stone fall from the wall. With the gate half raised, the specialist held the drive handle while water pressed harder against it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team cleared the spillway and brought the dam safely through the thaw.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team took the hut and lowered the gate to protect the upper wall.
endings.draw: Both teams held the gate halfway until the ice broke free without damaging the dam.

paragraphs: An old mountain barn had been converted into a shelter for travelers crossing the high road. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers arrived to restock it; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts had found smoke coming from the sealed loft. The shelter’s emergency ladder leaned against the wrong wall, too far from the smoke.

{{hero}} moved the ladder and climbed to the loft, where a faulty stove pipe had set its insulation smoldering. The specialist cut the draft and found a traveler sleeping beyond the partition, unaware of the smoke. A fresh gust pushed air through the broken pipe, feeding the heat again.

The traveler woke and said a second person had gone into the barn’s cellar for water. The rangers had only one mask left; the scouts below were already lifting the cellar door. The specialist held the loft hatch open as smoke rolled toward the stair.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers cleared the shelter and brought both travelers onto the road.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took control of the barn and completed the rescue.
endings.draw: The travelers emerged, while both sides kept watch until the stove pipe was replaced.

paragraphs: A hillside mill stored flour for the villages beyond the pass. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to collect the winter ration; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guards held the millrace. The wheel had jammed while sacks remained on an upper platform, leaving the only loading bridge suspended above the water.

{{hero}} reached the wheelhouse as a defender tried to release its brake with workers still on the platform. The fighter pulled them from the lever and held the brake while a miller lowered the bridge by hand. The sacks began to slide toward the exposed edge as the bridge moved.

The first workers crossed, but the last was trapped behind a stack too heavy to shift alone. The wheel groaned against the brake. Downstream, a village lantern flashed twice, the signal that its storehouse was empty, as the fighter felt the lever creeping forward.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts saved the worker and carried the flour over the pass.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the mill and distributed the ration from its own wagons.
endings.draw: The worker escaped, and both groups split the first dry sacks between the villages.

paragraphs: An avalanche lookout above the ski road flashed a red warning while the slope looked still. {{heroPlayer}}’s response team reached its cabin; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain patrol controlled the lift station below. The cabin’s paper log showed a tremor recorded after the instruments were switched off.

{{hero}} covered the cabin window while a geologist checked the sensor outside. Fire struck the railing from the lift station, and the fighter answered from behind a thick shutter, giving the geologist time to return. The sensor was warm despite the frozen air, and its cable led beneath the lookout floor.

The geologist found a second sensor in a sealed box, linked to a rescue beacon under the snowfield. It might belong to someone trapped there or to an old training device. Below, passengers began boarding the lift while the red warning continued to flash.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team stopped the lift and found the beacon’s source before the slope moved.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the lookout and set its own evacuation route.
endings.draw: The lift remained still while both sides searched the snowfield for the beacon.

paragraphs: A high-altitude radio farm tracked returning spacecraft across the mountain horizon. {{heroPlayer}}’s ground crew came to recover a lost signal; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge sentries were closing the aerials before a lightning storm. A returning pilot could still be heard, but each word arrived from a different antenna.

{{hero}} traced the broken array and found one dish locked onto a false reflection from the clouds. The specialist turned it toward the pilot’s real bearing while a storm warning sounded overhead. The voice became clear enough to report a damaged guidance unit and a landing site somewhere beyond the ridge.

The pilot needed one more bearing to avoid a narrow valley; the sentries wanted every dish grounded before lightning struck. The specialist held the dish’s manual wheel as a blue spark crossed the nearest mast and the pilot asked whether anyone could still hear.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew guided the pilot through the valley and secured the aerials before the storm.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries grounded the farm and launched a rescue from the last reported bearing.
endings.draw: The pilot received one bearing before the array fell silent, leaving both parties to search after the storm.

paragraphs: A mountain grain depot stood at the meeting of three narrow roads, its doors packed with ice. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to open the stores for an isolated settlement; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge fighters had taken the western road. Inside, a generator thudded unevenly beside the grain drying fans.

{{hero}} covered the depot door while workers broke away the ice. Shots struck the loading frame, and the fighter returned fire from behind a stack of empty pallets. When the door opened, warm air rushed out carrying smoke from the generator room rather than the smell of dry grain.

The workers could load the nearest sacks and leave, or shut down the fans to investigate the smoke before it reached the stored harvest. From the western road came the sound of an engine pulling closer. The fighter watched the generator-room light dim as a worker reached for its handle.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol saved the grain and sent supplies down all three roads.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge fighters secured the depot and controlled its distribution.
endings.draw: The generator stopped, and both sides carried dry sacks out before the smoke spread.

paragraphs: A ranger station above a narrow canyon controlled a cable crossing used by the spring wildlife survey. {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers arrived with a sedated animal that needed shelter; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain detail guarded the far landing. An empty survey cage hung halfway across, twisting in the wind.

{{hero}} took the cable controls and brought the empty cage back, then found a missing tooth in its drive wheel. The specialist seated a spare gear from the station stores, but the brake would hold only while someone kept pressure on the handle. The animal began stirring as the trackers prepared the crossing.

The far landing flashed a warning lamp: the detail had found the support anchor shifting in the wind. There was time for one quick transit before a full inspection. The specialist felt the handle tug toward release while the trackers debated whether to send the animal or a person first.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers crossed and brought the animal into safe shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the landing and stopped the cable until its anchor was repaired.
endings.draw: The empty cage crossed for a test, while both teams waited out the wind with the animal on the near side.

paragraphs: A mountain clinic depended on a small snowmelt reservoir whose water arrived cloudy that morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s care team came to inspect the filter; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland sentries occupied the reservoir path. The clinic’s waiting room filled while its kitchen taps remained shut.

{{hero}} reached the filter chamber through a side culvert and found fresh silt entering above its mesh. The specialist cleared the intake and traced the disturbance to a cracked bank near the footpath. Stabilizing it would take the spare mesh needed to keep the clinic supplied that day.

A storm crossed the ridge, sending new meltwater toward the crack. At the clinic, staff called to say they could manage until evening if the filter held. The sentries’ lights appeared along the path as the specialist lifted the one spare mesh from its case.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the bank and reopened the clinic’s clean-water supply.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries took the reservoir and redirected the clinic to a temporary source.
endings.draw: The filter ran at reduced flow as both groups worked to brace the bank.

paragraphs: A mountain meeting house kept a coded radio for travelers lost beyond the pass. {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers arrived to collect its last call; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol had already surrounded the doorway. The radio repeated a place name in an old local dialect that neither side’s map contained.

{{hero}} held the upstairs corridor while a courier copied the transmission. Fire broke the glass near the stair, and the fighter returned it from a stone window, giving the courier time to compare the code with a painted sign below. The sign’s faded letters matched the place name exactly.

The sign pointed to a footpath buried by a recent slide. The call sounded again, weaker this time, as footsteps reached the lower room. To find the traveler, the courier needed the original route marker outside; to keep the radio, they had to remain above the guarded stairs.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s couriers found the buried path and brought the traveler home.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the meeting house and took over the search.
endings.draw: Both groups followed separate clues toward the footpath while the radio fell silent.

paragraphs: A river port below the mountain sent vital freight uphill on a suspended cable car. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock escorts arrived with a load of bridge bolts; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland guards held the upper terminal. The car stalled above the torrent just as a worker heard its suspension pin begin to shift.

{{hero}} reached the lower winch and wrestled a defender away from its brake. The fighter held the mechanism still while a dockhand tied a safety line to the car. A second pin slipped above the river; the car tipped, scattering a few bolts into the water.

The bridge crew waited at the upper terminal with its own bolts running short. Bringing the car down would save the dockhand climbing toward it but lose the cargo’s chance of reaching the bridge by dusk. The fighter felt the brake shake as the safety line went taut.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts saved the car and sent the bolts uphill before dusk.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the upper terminal and lowered the car for repair.
endings.draw: The dockhand came back safely, and both groups carried the surviving bolts along the river road.

paragraphs: A mountain refuge received a stranded walking party as its heating loop began to freeze. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical support team approached from the old road; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries held the narrow yard. Inside, the refuge keeper was counting blankets while a child’s hands turned pale with cold.

{{hero}} opened the heater housing and found a frozen return pipe. The specialist warmed the joint with a portable unit and restored circulation to one room. A pressure alarm then sounded at the adjoining bunkhouse, where more travelers were sleeping without knowing their pipes had split.

The unit had enough charge to warm either the occupied room until dawn or the bunkhouse long enough to evacuate it. Outside, the sentries began moving toward the entrance. The refuge keeper put a blanket around the child and waited for the specialist to choose a door.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team warmed the refuge and brought the bunkhouse travelers to safety.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries secured the yard and organized the evacuation.
endings.draw: Both rooms emptied into a single warm shelter while the teams shared the remaining power.

paragraphs: A habitat’s mountain-themed garden lost artificial daylight during a gathering for residents who had never seen snow. {{heroPlayer}}’s mechanics reached the light controls; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch held the corridor outside. In darkness, a young resident reported that the garden’s viewing door had opened toward the unsealed service deck.

{{hero}} covered the service junction while a mechanic isolated the door actuator. Shots struck the rail behind them, and the fighter answered from a planter, buying time for the mechanic to close the outer door. Then a voice from the dark garden called that someone remained beyond it.

Reopening the door could bring the missing person into safety, but its damaged seal might not close again. The mechanic found an emergency tether and offered one end to the fighter. As the watch drew nearer, a hand pressed against the glass from the unlit deck.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s mechanics recovered the resident and restored light to the garden.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch secured the service deck and brought the resident inside.
endings.draw: The resident reached the tether, while both groups kept the damaged door closed by hand.

paragraphs: An interactive mural on a mountainside plaza changed color when people spoke to it. {{heroPlayer}}’s artists came when the mural began answering with a recorded voice they had never installed; {{otherPlayer}}’s security crew had closed the plaza. Below the painted surface, a maintenance crawlspace held the original sound archive.

{{hero}} opened the crawlspace and found a second recorder connected to the mural’s speaker. The specialist saved its file, then heard the voice say that a visitor was trapped under the stair, out of sight behind the crowd barriers. A weak knock answered from the other side of the wall.

The crawlspace door led to the trapped visitor, but opening it fully would cut power to the mural and erase the recorder’s unsaved final seconds. Security lights moved across the plaza above. The artist held the file transfer open while the knocking came again, much closer.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s artists saved the recording and freed the visitor.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s security crew took the crawlspace and completed the rescue.
endings.draw: The visitor emerged, but the recording’s final message remained lost behind the mural.

paragraphs: A cliffside freight cradle carried prefabricated homes up to a settlement rebuilt after a landslide. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers came to bring up the final wall panel; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guards held the top winch. The cradle hung below the ridge with a worker still fastening its load.

{{hero}} reached the winch by a narrow scaffold and grappled a defender reaching for the release catch. The fighter held them away while a rigger took the brake. From the cradle, the worker shouted that one panel strap had torn and the wall was shifting toward the cliff.

The winch could lift the load fast and risk losing the wall, or lower it toward a ledge too narrow for the worker to stand. Above them, the settlement’s lights appeared in new window frames that had no walls yet. The rigger waited for the fighter’s signal.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew saved the worker and delivered the last wall to the settlement.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the winch and lowered the cradle for repairs.
endings.draw: The worker reached the ridge, but the wall remained suspended between both crews.

paragraphs: A mountain weather cache stored years of avalanche maps, but its newest route file had been overwritten overnight. {{heroPlayer}}’s data specialists reached the cabin to restore it; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge patrol had already posted old trail markers. A supply convoy was due through the pass before morning.

{{hero}} recovered most of the file from a backup drive and found two conflicting locations for a fresh fracture in the snowpack. One matched the ridge patrol’s markers; the other matched a sensor that had stopped transmitting after the storm. The specialist could publish only one route to the convoy.

A test flare showed movement near the silent sensor. The patrol called that its route remained open, while the restored map placed the fracture beneath it. In the cabin, the convoy’s driver requested a bearing as the specialist watched snow fall across both possible paths.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s specialists verified the fracture and guided the convoy around it.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the cache and led the convoy along its marked route.
endings.draw: The convoy waited at the pass while both groups sent teams to check the silent sensor.

paragraphs: A glacier exposed the entrance to a chamber older than the mining road above it. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey escort went inside to retrieve its survey markers; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guards held the road. The chamber walls reflected lantern light into a tunnel that was not on the miners’ map.

{{hero}} covered the entrance while a surveyor photographed the new passage. Shots struck the ice outside, and the fighter returned fire from behind a stone pillar, keeping the surveyor in the chamber. In the photograph, another lantern appeared deep in the tunnel although none of the party had gone there.

The surveyor could follow that light or carry the image back to the road before the glacier shifted again. Ice cracked above the entrance, and the reflected lantern moved closer without a sound. The fighter held the pillar as the mountain guards’ lights came down the road.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party found the light’s source and escaped with the chamber survey.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards sealed the entrance and retained the road.
endings.draw: Both parties withdrew with different photographs of the tunnel, each showing the lantern in a different place.

paragraphs: A mountain freight winch carried winter fuel above a village built along the slope. {{heroPlayer}}’s assault party reached the lower engine room; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland defenders held the cable station above. The fuel car stopped halfway up, hanging over houses whose chimneys were already cold.

{{hero}} met a defender at the engine brake and drove them away from its release pin. The fighter held the brake as a worker checked the cable. Its outer strands were unraveling where they passed around the upper wheel, and restarting the engine would pull the damage directly into the mechanism.

A rescue line could lower the car into the village, but the cable station was still held from above. The worker offered to climb the damaged span to fit it. The fighter felt the brake handle jerk as the car swayed, and a house light came on directly below.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party recovered the fuel car and kept the village supplied.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s defenders secured the upper wheel and lowered the car under their control.
endings.draw: The car came down between the two crews, leaving both to carry fuel through the village.

paragraphs: A living flood sensor was planted along the riverbank below a mountain settlement. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers arrived when its leaves began turning black; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol was guarding the footbridge nearby. The river appeared low, yet the sensor had never warned without a rise upstream.

{{hero}} traced the sensor’s roots beneath the bank and found them wrapped around an old gauge whose needle was pinned at zero. The specialist freed the mechanism. Its pointer swung toward a level higher than the bridge’s deck, while the plant’s remaining leaves darkened in a wave.

The first villagers stepped onto the bridge carrying crates for market. A warning bell stood on the far bank, beyond the patrol’s position. The specialist could run for it or keep reading the gauge long enough to know whether the warning was real.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers sounded the warning and cleared the bridge before the flood.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the bridge and directed villagers to higher ground.
endings.draw: The bridge emptied, but both groups waited beside the sensor for the delayed water to arrive.

paragraphs: An array of mirrors above the crater village redirected a few hours of sunlight into homes beneath the rim. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came when one beam stopped; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain sentries held the access stairs. In the darkened homes, residents lit candles while a second beam began striking the empty road.

{{hero}} climbed the outer brace and discovered that a fastening pin had slipped from the leading mirror. The specialist reset its angle, bringing a strip of light back into the village. The pin, however, was too worn to hold through the next rotation of the array.

A replacement lay in the locked station above the sentries. The worn pin began creeping outward under the weight of the mirror as the village children cheered the returning light. The specialist kept one hand against the frame and watched the sun continue moving.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians replaced the pin and restored daylight to every home.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries secured the station and brought the mirrors back under control.
endings.draw: The first homes stayed lit while both sides braced the failing mirror through the afternoon.

paragraphs: A mountain conservatory was built around a single tree whose branches held an archive of weather ribbons. {{heroPlayer}}’s entry team came for the newest ribbon; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland guards sealed the glass corridor. A missing caretaker’s lantern burned near the tree, though no one was visible inside.

{{hero}} forced past a defender at the corridor lock and held it open while a teammate crossed the threshold. The caretaker emerged from beneath the branches with the ribbon in hand, warning that a vent above the tree had opened to freezing air. The lock began closing under automatic pressure.

The team could bring the caretaker through before the lock shut, or reach the vent first to protect the tree and its hanging archive. Frost was already gathering on the oldest ribbons. The defender pushed against the fighter at the doorway as the lantern went out.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team saved the caretaker and carried out the newest ribbon.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards took the conservatory and sealed its damaged vent.
endings.draw: The caretaker reached the corridor while both groups worked to keep the archive from freezing.

paragraphs: A route planner at the mountain transit hub predicted that the morning shuttles would meet an avalanche on the east road. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts reached its console; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol had already directed the first shuttle toward a western detour. The planner then marked the detour as unsafe too.

{{hero}} compared the prediction against a live snow sensor and found that its clock lagged the hub by an hour. Correcting it erased the western warning but left the east road red. The first shuttle was now between the two roads, its driver asking which sign to trust.

The patrol’s lights appeared at the road junction as snow began falling faster. The corrected plan could guide the driver west, but another update was still loading from a sensor high above that route. The specialist held the transmission open while the shuttle slowed beneath both signs.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts verified the detour and guided every shuttle safely west.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the junction and led the shuttles along its marked route.
endings.draw: The shuttles waited at the junction while both parties checked the high sensor.

paragraphs: An observatory above a mountain town received a narrow-band call from a climber stranded on the far ridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s operators reached the dish; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland patrol held the lower path. The climber could hear the town bells but could not see their lights through the cloud.

{{hero}} covered the dish platform while an operator aligned the receiver. Shots struck the housing, and the fighter returned fire to keep the operator at the controls. The climber’s voice cleared long enough to describe a red marker post and the sound of running water beneath the snow.

The nearest rescue team was waiting in town for exact coordinates. The operator could keep listening for a second bearing or send the uncertain first one before the dish motor failed. The fighter watched a crack spread across the shot-up housing as the climber called again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s operators found the climber and guided rescuers across the ridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the observatory and used the last bearing for its search.
endings.draw: The first bearing reached town, but both sides set out for different red marker posts.

paragraphs: An old stone bridge carried a procession carrying food to homes cut off by a rockslide. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts met it at the near arch; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guards held the opposite bank. Water rose beneath the bridge, loosening one of the stones engraved with the names of its builders.

{{hero}} drove a defender back from the parapet and caught the loosened stone as it shifted under a porter’s foot. The fighter braced it long enough for the porter to cross. The next person in line carried a heavier basket, and another stone began to move nearby.

There was space on the bridge for one escort and one porter, no more. The far bank called for the food before the path behind them disappeared beneath water. The fighter could brace the arch again or pull the procession back to the high road.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts got the food across before the bridge closed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards held the far arch and sent the procession along a safer route.
endings.draw: A few baskets crossed, while both sides held the bridge closed until the water fell.

paragraphs: A remote district office was storing the names of residents who needed transport before an expected landslide. {{heroPlayer}}’s coordinators arrived to collect the final registry; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol was moving families toward the pass. A clerk had circled one household in red but left its address blank.

{{hero}} searched the office’s older ledgers and found the household listed under a trail name replaced on newer maps. The specialist located the trail at the foot of the unstable slope and sent a runner to warn the patrol. From that direction, a small lamp began signaling through the dusk.

The runner could follow the lamp or turn back before the slope moved. The transport bus had room for the household but was already pulling away from the office. The specialist held the old ledger open while the sound of loose rock came across the valley.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s coordinators found the household and brought them aboard before the slide.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol reached the old trail first and directed the evacuation.
endings.draw: The bus waited at a safe bend while both groups followed the lamp to the trail.

paragraphs: A mountain tracking station kept an orbital rescue capsule on its approach line while a storm hid the landing site. {{heroPlayer}}’s watch came to defend the dish; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge sentries had closed the access track. The capsule’s pilot reported that guidance fuel would last for only one correction.

{{hero}} held the dish gantry while a controller aligned its beam. Fire struck the support strut, and the fighter answered from behind the motor housing, keeping the controller at the console. The beam found the capsule, but the landing site shown below was a shallow lake rather than the dry meadow in the station map.

The controller could direct the pilot to the lake, within reach of a rescue boat, or wait for a dry site to appear through cloud. The pilot asked for a decision as the fuel gauge fell. The fighter saw the ridge sentries’ lamps moving toward the gantry stairs.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch guided the capsule to ground and recovered the pilot.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries took the tracking station and chose the landing site.
endings.draw: The capsule came down beside the lake, where both parties raced to reach its hatch.

paragraphs: A mine refuge beneath the pass lost its ventilation while surveyors were mapping an escape tunnel. {{heroPlayer}}’s tunnel crew arrived at the fan room; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain patrol held the old shaft. The surveyors had painted a line of arrows through the passage but stopped before the final turn.

{{hero}} opened the fan casing and found its drive packed with dust from a new breach. The specialist cleared enough for a short restart, sending air toward the unfinished arrows. Over the radio, a surveyor reported hearing water where the map showed solid rock.

The fan could run long enough to clear the refuge or be shut down so the crew could listen for the source of water. Above, the patrol began descending the shaft. The last arrow appeared through thinning dust, pointing toward a tunnel that had never been dug.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored the air and led the surveyors through the newly found exit.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the shaft and evacuated the refuge by its known route.
endings.draw: The surveyors came out safely while both sides sealed the unexplored turn against the water.

paragraphs: A monastery’s upper stair was the only path to a signal bell above the snow line. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to ring it for travelers lost in fog; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain defenders held the lower gate. An older monk waited beside the bell rope, listening for a reply from the valley.

{{hero}} forced a defender away from the stair railing and climbed to the landing. The fighter caught the bell rope as the monk collapsed, exhausted from holding the slippery steps alone. One pull sent a note across the fog; from below came a second bell, much farther away than expected.

The rope had begun to fray at the roof beam. The lost travelers needed several more notes to follow, but another hard pull could break it. The fighter steadied the monk on the landing as the defenders climbed the stair and the distant bell answered again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts held the stair and guided the travelers to the monastery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s defenders secured the bell and directed the travelers through the lower gate.
endings.draw: The bells exchanged one final call, and both parties searched the fog from opposite paths.

paragraphs: The upper tea terraces were drying while a storm filled the lower irrigation pond. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came to reopen the stepped channels; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge patrol had blocked the gate at the dividing wall. Water lapped against the lower homes while the highest plants curled in dry soil.

{{hero}} found an old bypass beneath a stone bench and worked its seized wheel free. A thread of water reached the first upper row, but the lower pond kept rising. The specialist noticed that the bypass could be opened wider only by closing the sluice protecting the homes below.

Residents at the lower wall began stacking sandbags as the patrol approached. Above, a grower called that the tea plants might survive one more day without water. The specialist held the bypass wheel between two positions, hearing rain strike both the dry leaves and the crowded roofs.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers balanced the channels and protected both homes and terraces.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the dividing wall and closed the bypass.
endings.draw: The lower homes stayed dry while the upper terraces received a narrow, temporary flow.

paragraphs: A summit train carried rescue equipment through a tunnel whose far signal had stopped answering. {{heroPlayer}}’s rail escort reached the beacon house; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain detail guarded the upper switch. A worker at the tunnel mouth held up a red lamp, too small for the approaching driver to see.

{{hero}} took cover beside the beacon lens while a signaler tried to restore its power. Shots struck the stonework, and the fighter returned fire from the window, keeping the signaler at the contacts. The red beacon lit for a moment, then blinked out as the power cell overheated.

The driver sounded the train horn from inside the tunnel. The signaler could cool the cell and try again, or run onto the track with the hand lamp. The mountain detail was crossing toward the switch, and the fighter watched their shadows pass behind the dark lens.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort stopped the train and delivered the rescue equipment safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the switch and halted the train beyond the tunnel.
endings.draw: The train stopped between signals while both groups held the equipment on its car.

paragraphs: A highland weather garden used sensitive vines to signal when the valley below needed shelter. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came when the plants began curling toward a windless sky; {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries held the ridge path. In the valley, the school remained open, its doors wide for the afternoon.

{{hero}} found warm air escaping from a fault beneath the garden beds, misleading one row of vines. The specialist closed the fault, but the remaining plants still curled in the same direction. Their roots were reacting to a tremor the instruments beside them had not yet recorded.

The school could be warned immediately, or the caretaker could wait for a mechanical reading to confirm the danger. The sentries’ radio crackled from the path, asking why the garden had gone quiet. A second tremor lifted loose soil from the vine roots.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers warned the school and guided its children away from the threatened slope.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s sentries secured the ridge and issued their own warning after confirming the tremor.
endings.draw: The school emptied while both sides watched the vines for the next sign.

paragraphs: An archive carved into a cliff held seeds collected from valleys since swallowed by reservoirs. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors came to extract one sealed case; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guards held the front corridor. Inside, rotating shelves had jammed while an archivist was still trapped behind them.

{{hero}} reached the shelf drive as a defender tried to throw its brake closed. The fighter shoved them clear and held the handle while a technician turned the shelves just far enough for the archivist to crawl through. The seed case appeared in the gap, but its label had been scraped clean.

The archivist recognized the case by a faded seal and warned that another, nearly identical one contained spoiled stock. The drive began pulling the shelves back toward the wall. The fighter could seize one case before the gap closed, with no time to check the contents until they reached daylight.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors brought out the archivist and the viable seeds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the archive and cataloged both cases themselves.
endings.draw: The archivist escaped, but both groups held an unmarked case whose contents remained uncertain.

paragraphs: A high-altitude survey station held an ice core whose layers could date the last deadly slide on the mountain. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards escorted a scientist to recover it; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge patrol watched the return path. The station freezer had failed, and meltwater was already running down the core’s case.

{{hero}} covered the loading door while the scientist wrapped the core in portable insulation. A shot struck the stair rail, and the fighter fired back from behind the freezer unit, keeping the scientist out of the open. The insulation alarm showed enough cooling for one descent, provided the lift did not stop.

The lift moved only a few feet before its cable snagged above the ridge patrol. The scientist could carry the core down an exposed service stair or stay with it while someone freed the lift. Water dripped onto the fighter’s glove as another shot sounded from below.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards delivered the core intact to the valley laboratory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the lift and took custody of the sample.
endings.draw: The scientist escaped with fragments of the core while both groups held the stalled lift.

paragraphs: A ridge festival had left its observation wheel standing so residents could watch the season’s first clear sunrise. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired security crew came when a gondola stopped near the top; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain wardens controlled the base. Two children inside held their hands against the fogged glass.

{{hero}} reached the brake platform as a defender tried to release the wheel all at once. The fighter forced them from the lever and held it while a mechanic engaged the manual drive. One gondola came down safely; the children’s remained above, where the main axle began to shake.

The mechanic said one more turn might bring the children within reach, but the axle could also slip and send the gondola past the landing. At the base, the wardens raised a rescue net. The fighter kept pressure on the lever as the children’s gondola emerged from the fog.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew lowered the children and secured the wheel before sunrise.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the base and used the rescue net to bring them down.
endings.draw: The gondola stopped above the net while both groups held the failing axle still.

paragraphs: A string of amateur telescopes on the mountainside began tracking the same point beneath the glacier instead of the night sky. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to check their linked clocks; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland watch held the upper observatory. A faint beacon was pulsing from the point every six seconds.

{{hero}} aligned the telescopes and found their mirrors reflecting a signal from a buried rescue pod. The specialist locked its position and sent coordinates to a recovery team. The beacon sped up, though the team was still an hour away, and the ice above the pod began settling.

One telescope could be dismantled for its heating cell to melt a narrow shaft, but doing so would erase the alignment the recovery team needed. The watch’s lights approached along the upper path. The specialist held the cell in one hand and a print of the coordinates in the other.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians opened a shaft and guided rescuers to the pod.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch secured the observatory and directed recovery from above.
endings.draw: The pod’s location remained marked while both groups waited for a safe way through the ice.

paragraphs: A mountain water station held the last clean reserve above a valley cut off by a rockfall. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards came to open the transfer line; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland detail held the upper pumps. Empty tanks waited on carts below, their drivers watching the station lamps.

{{hero}} covered the pump room while a worker checked the transfer valve. Shots struck the concrete beside the gauges, and the fighter returned fire from the doorway, buying the worker time to open the line. Water began to move, then the pressure gauge climbed past its red mark.

A blockage farther down the line could burst beneath the waiting carts. The worker could close the valve now, saving the pipes but leaving the valley dry, or run outside to clear the blockage under fire. The fighter heard the drivers shouting as the first cart filled too slowly.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards held the station while the blockage was cleared and the valley tanks filled.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s detail took the pumps and shut down the dangerous line.
endings.draw: A few tanks filled before both sides closed the valve and repaired the pipe.

paragraphs: Two survey teams reached a weather mast above the same valley, each carrying an order to claim its transmitter. The mast had been silent for years, but a wall of rain was coming over the western ridge. At the farm below, people were still working in the dry riverbed.

{{hero}} climbed into the transmitter housing with a coil of wire and found the old flood gauge jammed against its upper stop. A second team arrived at the base and began resetting the mast for its own network. The specialist bridged the corroded contacts; a warning lamp lit, then went dark as the other crew cut the feed.

Water appeared between the stones far below. To send the warning, someone had to hold the contacts together while another person aimed the antenna through the rain. From the narrow platform, the specialist could see an open route to the antenna and a rival climbing toward it. The farms had minutes, whichever team took the mast.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew held the transmitter long enough to warn the farms and mark the mast as theirs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew took the antenna, sent the warning, and kept the mast under its own claim.
endings.draw: The warning reached the valley, but neither crew could hold the mast after the rising water cut its approach.

paragraphs: An avalanche exposed a stone chamber beneath an old mountain cairn. Its carved ceiling showed a safe path across the ridge, one the mapmakers had lost after the last thaw. {{heroPlayer}}’s climbers reached the cairn from above while {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers approached by the snowbound pass below.

Inside, {{hero}} met a defender at the narrow entrance. The two grappled against the stone lip as loose snow poured through the roof; the fighter forced a gap just wide enough for a companion to carry out a rubbing of the ceiling. A fresh crack ran across the chamber, splitting the carved path in two.

Only the lower half of the route remained legible from the entrance. The rest lay beneath a slab that could be lifted if the rival team helped, but the chamber would not hold many people. Outside, travelers were already gathering to cross before dark. The fighter steadied the slab while boots scraped on both sides of the doorway.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s climbers recovered the complete route and guided the waiting travelers over the ridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers secured the chamber and brought out the route before the roof gave way.
endings.draw: The teams carried out half a map each and had to piece the crossing together as the snow returned.

paragraphs: The lights of a buried postal tunnel came on for the first time in a century. A courier’s iron dispatch box was moving through it on a belt nobody had started. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts entered at the eastern hatch; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol came through the western shaft, each hoping to recover the box before the belt reached the flooded section.

{{hero}} took cover beside a row of rusted sorting frames. Fire from the far hatch pinned the scout’s companion in the open, so the fighter shot the chain above the belt and dropped a screen of empty mail baskets between them. The companion reached the box, only to find it locked around the moving belt itself.

A blue line of water climbed the tunnel wall. Breaking the chain would free the dispatch but send the belt and its heavy wheels downhill toward the rival patrol; leaving it running would carry the box underwater. The fighter sighted along the chain while the companion shouted that the padlock had begun to turn.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts stopped the belt, carried out the dispatch, and kept the dry tunnel entrance.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol reached the box as the belt stalled and took the tunnel’s western end.
endings.draw: Water swallowed the box, and both patrols withdrew with only the tunnel’s route written down.

paragraphs: A reentry capsule struck the edge of a frozen reservoir and began broadcasting an identification code from an old exploration mission. The ice was thin around its scorched hull. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew reached the near shore as {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens raised lamps across the water; both wanted the capsule before it sank.

{{hero}} crawled over the ice with a tether and opened the capsule’s service panel. Inside was a recorder still warm enough to melt its mounting bracket. The specialist detached it just as a line of cracks spread from the hull toward the shore. A voice came over the recorder, counting down the remaining power in an emergency beacon.

The tether was long enough to pull either the recorder or the specialist across the widest crack, not both together. From the far shore, the wardens pushed a ladder toward the capsule. The beacon counted again. The specialist held the recorder above the black water and waited for the tether to tighten.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew recovered the recorder and established a safe line to the stranded capsule.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens bridged the ice first and secured the capsule and its surviving records.
endings.draw: The recorder was saved, but the capsule sank before either crew could claim the reservoir site.

paragraphs: A seed vault beneath the tundra kept its doors locked through every winter. This year a broken ventilation shaft let warm air in, and the first trays inside had begun to sprout in their sleeves. {{heroPlayer}}’s winter patrol arrived with replacement seals; {{otherPlayer}}’s survey party stood at the access hatch with a claim on the ground above it.

{{hero}} entered through the shaft while another fighter held the hatch. They collided at the manual wheel, both reaching for the release that would open the inner vault. The fighter forced the defender away from the wheel and turned it far enough to admit a technician. Frost fell from the ceiling as the ventilation fan stopped.

Without the fan, the room would warm and ruin its oldest stock. Reopening the outside hatch would bring cold air through but also let the rival party in behind them. The technician held a new seal against the door and called for room to work. The fighter stood at the wheel, hearing boots gather in the shaft.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol sealed the vault, saved the trays, and maintained its watch above the hatch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s survey party took the access point and installed the seal under its own guard.
endings.draw: The seeds survived the night, while the two parties divided the watch outside the vault.

paragraphs: The town’s wind farm stood on a narrow mesa above a failed radio repeater. Its blades could power a temporary relay, but whoever held the control hut could send traffic across half the frontier. {{heroPlayer}}’s road patrol found the gate chained; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts were already moving between the towers.

{{hero}} covered the crew crossing the open gravel toward the control hut. Gunfire struck a rotor, and a loose panel began to spin away over their heads. The fighter shot the tower’s emergency latch, dropping its blade into a safe brake while the crew made the last few meters. Inside, a technician found the relay cable cut at both ends.

The spare line lay coiled beneath the nearest tower. Reaching it would mean crossing the gravel again while the other scouts pressed toward the hut. The wind slackened and the lights flickered, leaving perhaps one working tower. The fighter watched the cable move in the grass and saw that someone else had reached for it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol restored the repeater and kept the control hut through the next broadcast.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the cable and powered the relay from their own position.
endings.draw: Both crews brought up a short emergency signal, but the damaged farm served neither side for long.

paragraphs: An abandoned field hospital kept a cabinet of cultures that could identify a sickness spreading through the nearby settlements. Its backup freezer was running on the last of its fuel. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical escort arrived by the east path; {{otherPlayer}}’s local watch had locked the front gate while its own doctors came up the road.

{{hero}} opened the cabinet and read the labels beneath a layer of frost. One sample matched the settlements’ symptoms, but the carrying case had no power cell. The specialist found a cell in the ruined diagnostic bench and fitted it just as the freezer alarm sounded and someone outside began working the gate open.

The sample could travel safely in its case; the remaining cultures would spoil if the freezer died. There was enough power to move one load, and the doctors on the road might save more if they reached the hospital. The specialist held the case at the door while the alarm counted down and two sets of footsteps converged.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort carried the matching sample out and held the hospital for the incoming doctors.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch reached the cabinet and secured the samples for its own medical team.
endings.draw: The teams shared the surviving samples, leaving the hospital’s claim undecided while the freezer failed.

paragraphs: An old border listening post started transmitting a voice recording that named every person approaching it. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators wanted the recorder; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens had orders to silence the post. The voice began repeating the name of a child in a hamlet below, where every radio was tuned to the same frequency.

{{hero}} slipped through a maintenance slot beneath the transmitter room. A guard blocked the ladder, and the fighter wrestled past without letting the guard fall onto the exposed generator contacts. At the top, they found a reel of names feeding a transmitter linked to a second antenna somewhere beyond the post.

Stopping this transmitter might only pass the recording to the hidden antenna. The control cabinet offered a way to trace the link, but its lights made the room visible through the upper windows. Outside, the wardens brought a cutter to the post’s main cable. The fighter reached for the cabinet while the voice reached another name.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators traced the hidden antenna and silenced both transmissions before the recording spread.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens cut the feed and took the post for a full search of its records.
endings.draw: The voices stopped, but the second antenna was never located, and both parties kept watch over the post.

paragraphs: A river barge ran aground beside a customs pier with its sealed cargo hanging over the water. The manifest listed drinking-water filters bound for three villages inland. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock guard sought to unload them; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier patrol suspected the manifest had been altered and held the pier’s landward end.

{{hero}} sheltered behind a bollard when fire caught the hoist operator at the crane. The fighter answered from the pier, forcing the shooters back while the operator raised the first crate. A broken pin slipped from the hoist, and the load swung toward the barge’s thin hull. The operator ducked, still gripping the controls.

Another shot might cut the crate loose before it struck the hull; a miss could send the filters straight into the river. The frontier patrol was closing on the customs shed where the original manifest lay. The fighter steadied the weapon as the crate swung back, and the operator called for a decision.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guard saved the filters, checked the manifest, and loaded the village convoy from the pier.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol seized the pier and inspected the cargo before directing its delivery.
endings.draw: The filters came ashore, but neither party kept exclusive control of the barge or its manifest.

paragraphs: A greenhouse roof collapsed during a cold snap, exposing beds of experimental winter grain to the open air. The caretaker asked both approaching teams to keep the seed stock alive until a transport arrived. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue crew took the heated packing room; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol held the door to the greenhouse itself.

{{hero}} found a manual heat exchanger behind the packing shelves and connected it to the surviving pipes. Steam reached the nearest beds, then stopped where the roof had crushed a junction. The specialist crawled beneath the hanging frame with a replacement collar while a voice from the opposite door ordered everyone away from the unstable beams.

A second collapse could trap the caretaker among the beds. The crew could carry the person out or finish the junction and keep the grain alive, but the low passage allowed only one worker at a time. The specialist felt the pipe warming under the collar and heard the caretaker call from the far end of the greenhouse.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored the heat, led the caretaker out, and protected the grain for transport.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the greenhouse and completed the rescue beneath its own guard.
endings.draw: The caretaker escaped and part of the grain survived, while both teams shared the remaining shelter.

paragraphs: A freight dirigible drifted into a frontier canyon with no crew visible at its windows. Its cargo bay contained the missing generator for a settlement’s water pumps. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage hands tethered the drifting craft from one cliff; {{otherPlayer}}’s search party climbed toward the opposite landing, each convinced the generator belonged on its side of the canyon.

{{hero}} held the narrow tether bridge while two mechanics boarded. Fire from the far ledge struck a mooring cable, and the craft lurched toward the rock. The fighter put shots into the cliffside winch to arrest the swing; the mechanics reached the generator, then found its shipping cage bolted through the deck.

The remaining cable was fraying. Cutting the cage loose would lighten the dirigible but send the heavy generator toward the bridge; keeping it aboard could pull everyone into the canyon. The fighter watched the mechanics brace at the last bolt as the far party reached the landing ring. The craft began another slow swing.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s hands lowered the generator intact and took charge of the drifting craft.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s party secured the landing ring and brought the generator down on its own side.
endings.draw: The generator was recovered, but both groups were needed to keep the damaged craft off the canyon floor.

paragraphs: A traveling theater had set up a night performance beside an abandoned navigation dome. Its projector unexpectedly filled the sky with coordinates to a supply cache under the seats. {{heroPlayer}}’s stage technicians rushed for the controls while {{otherPlayer}}’s local patrol moved to cordon off the dome; the audience thought the commotion was part of the show.

{{hero}} followed the projector cables beneath the platform and found a second lantern wired to the cache’s pressure sensor. The specialist cut the first feed, darkening the sky, but the hidden lantern stayed hot. A stagehand began clearing the seats as the other team reached the dome’s side entrance.

The cache could be reached through the prop trapdoor, directly below the last row of spectators. Moving the audience would expose the location; leaving them seated risked the sensor triggering beneath them. The specialist held the trapdoor latch while the performers kept speaking onstage and the side door opened.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians cleared the audience, isolated the sensor, and secured the cache beneath the stage.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the dome, evacuated the seats, and placed the cache under guard.
endings.draw: The performance ended safely, but the two teams locked the cache together until its contents could be counted.

paragraphs: An orbital cargo pod survived its descent into a quarry, wedged between two cliff faces with its airlock facing open space. Workers on both sides could hear tapping from within. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers brought a lowering harness; {{otherPlayer}}’s quarry crew had already anchored a ladder to the lower ledge.

{{hero}} crossed the pod’s narrow service rail and met a defender at the airlock crank. The fighters struggled with their boots braced against the hot casing, and the fighter pressed the other one away from the wheel without dropping them into the quarry. A hatch opened a hand’s width. Someone inside pushed a note through: two survivors, little air.

Opening the door wider would shift the pod off its perch. The riggers could take its weight with the harness, but the quarry crew’s ladder was closer to the survivors. The fighter gripped the crank and counted the taps from inside while both crews called out different plans from the ledges.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers anchored the pod, opened the hatch, and brought both survivors across their harness.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s quarry crew steadied the pod from below and carried the survivors down its ladder.
endings.draw: Both survivors came out, but the pod fell beyond recovery and neither crew kept the crash site.

paragraphs: A sealed escrow vault at a frontier market began releasing its deposits a day early. Whoever held the vault’s counter could identify the rightful owners before the packets reached the street. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors entered through the counting room; {{otherPlayer}}’s marshals secured the public doors while merchants gathered outside.

{{hero}} stopped the conveyor with a maintenance key and scanned the first packet. Its seal matched a missing ledger, but the next packet carried a different owner’s name over the same serial number. The specialist found a second ledger hidden beneath the counter as the stopped conveyor pulled hard against its brake.

If the brake failed, the packets would scatter among the waiting merchants. If the auditors locked the public doors, the marshals could no longer verify who had come to claim them. The specialist held both ledgers under the counter lamp while the machine began to creep forward and fists knocked against the glass.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors secured the counter and reconciled the deposits before the vault reopened.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s marshals took the counter and held the packets until their owners could be identified.
endings.draw: The conveyor stopped, but both ledgers remained in dispute and the packets stayed sealed.

paragraphs: A dead communications relay on a salt flat began answering calls in voices from a lost survey expedition. The messages pointed to a buried vehicle beneath the relay mast. {{heroPlayer}}’s search group advanced along the causeway while {{otherPlayer}}’s border scouts approached over the dry basin, each trying to reach the coordinates first.

{{hero}} took position beside the mast as a surveyor started to dig. Fire from a distant ridge shattered the relay dish; the fighter returned fire until the surveyor pulled a metal hatch clear of the salt. Under it lay a cab with lights still burning and a hand pressed against the glass from inside.

The hatch was held by a pressure lock connected to the broken dish. The surveyor could force it, risking the air in the cab, or repair the relay while the scouts closed on the mast. The fighter could still see the hand against the glass. An answering light blinked twice from within.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s group reopened the cab, brought its occupant out, and held the relay site.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts reached the hatch and took over the rescue beneath the mast.
endings.draw: The occupant was freed, but both groups lost the relay when the old mast fell into the salt.

paragraphs: A glassworks quarry held an unfinished lens large enough to focus sunlight on a whole block of stone. Its builders had vanished, leaving the lens suspended above the floor on a single chain. {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition arrived to recover the mechanism; {{otherPlayer}}’s prospectors had already marked the quarry as their next cut.

{{hero}} reached the crane platform as a defender grabbed for the chain brake. They fought shoulder to shoulder between the exposed gears, and the fighter wrested the brake free before the lens could drop. Below them, a worker uncovered a drawing that showed the lens pointed at an underground chamber, not at the stone face.

The brake would hold only if someone stayed on the platform. Lowering the lens might reveal the chamber but leave its keeper trapped above the fighting; swinging it clear would make the discovery inaccessible. The fighter kept a hand on the brake while workers below argued over where the shadow ought to fall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition brought the lens under control and opened a path to the chamber below.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s prospectors took the crane and secured the underground find for their own survey.
endings.draw: The lens held, but the chamber stayed shut while both parties disputed the crane platform.

paragraphs: An acoustic observatory on the frontier began repeating a distress call three seconds before anyone spoke it. {{heroPlayer}}’s listeners came to trace the delayed echo; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the hillside around the dish. A lone caretaker kept asking the radio to tell him whether his missing partner was still inside.

{{hero}} held the reflector walkway while the caretaker opened an inspection hatch. Fire from the hillside drove them behind a panel, and the fighter shot a hinge free to let the reflector swing across their line of fire. Through the open hatch the caretaker found a second receiver, still warm, and heard his partner answer from somewhere beneath the foundation.

The answer came before the caretaker called down. Reaching the foundation meant crossing a section of walkway that the swung reflector had stripped of its railing. The scout line was moving closer, and the second receiver began the partner’s reply again. The fighter stood beside the gap as the caretaker prepared to cross.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s listeners reached the foundation, found the missing partner, and kept the observatory working.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the dish and led the search beneath its foundation.
endings.draw: The partner answered from below, but the walkway remained impassable and both groups stayed to find another entrance.

paragraphs: A basalt pillar on the ridge opened at dawn and exposed a wall of tiny rotating drawers. Each held a fragment of a star map, though one drawer was empty and marked with a village’s coordinates. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party reached the pillar at sunrise; {{otherPlayer}}’s trail guard came up from the village to close it again.

{{hero}} aligned the drawers by their worn hinges and uncovered an image of a route running beneath the ridge. The specialist copied it onto a portable slate, then noticed the empty drawer beginning to close around a scrap of fresh cloth. Someone had reached the pillar before either party, and the cloth matched the village’s festival banners.

The pillar would seal when the sun passed the notch in the rock. The copied map might lead to the missing visitor, but its last section still sat inside the empty drawer. The trail guard was close enough to read the slate. The specialist held the drawer open as the first shadow reached its rim.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party copied the complete route and led a search beneath the ridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard closed the pillar, kept the map, and organized the search from the village.
endings.draw: The partial route was shared, and both parties followed it after the pillar sealed for the day.

paragraphs: A buried orchard of pale fruit trees was discovered beneath a collapsed transit station. Their roots had lifted the platform, leaving an old shelter trapped behind the trunks. {{heroPlayer}}’s foragers entered through a maintenance vent as {{otherPlayer}}’s watch pried open the station doors, both hearing movement beyond the shelter wall.

{{hero}} crossed the raised platform to a handwheel above the shelter. A defender seized the same wheel, and the fighter struggled for it among roots that shifted underfoot. When it turned, a shutter opened just enough to show the shelter was occupied by people shielding their eyes from the light.

Opening the shutter farther would let the foragers in, but the lifted platform might fall across the shelter entrance. The watch had found a support beam near the old doors. The fighter kept the wheel from turning back while someone inside asked which way led out; roots began to crack beneath the platform.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s foragers braced the platform, freed the occupants, and secured the orchard entrance.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch reinforced the station and brought the shelter occupants through its doors.
endings.draw: The occupants escaped together, but the platform collapsed and blocked the orchard from both sides.

paragraphs: At a crossroads outside the settlements, every signal lamp turned green at once. An automated freight train was due at the crossing, and two caravans were already approaching from different roads. {{heroPlayer}}’s traffic engineers reached the signal box while {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier patrol stopped the first carts at the barrier.

{{hero}} opened the controller and found its clock reading a different hour for each road. The specialist disconnected the faulty timing unit and began setting the signals by hand. The nearest lamps went red, but the rail warning remained green; beneath the box, a mechanical switch still pointed the train toward the crowded crossing.

One person could reach the track switch from below the box. Resetting it would divert the train onto an empty siding, but opening that door would leave the hand-set road signals unattended. The patrol called that the second caravan had entered the far approach. The specialist held the switch key and watched the rail warning blink.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers diverted the train, separated the caravans, and secured the signal box.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the crossing and managed the diversion from the trackside switch.
endings.draw: The crossing cleared in time, but neither party restored the controller before traffic stopped for the night.

paragraphs: A dome above the frontier market had projected the same night sky for forty years. That morning its stars shifted to show a second market, beneath the floor where the old observatory had been buried. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts wanted the projection kept running; {{otherPlayer}}’s watch closed the public steps after a vendor disappeared down them.

{{hero}} aligned the dome’s original star wheel with the new pattern and found a service hatch hidden in the central plinth. The specialist opened it to a stairwell full of dust and fresh footprints. From below came the vendor’s voice, followed by the sound of a door sliding shut. The projector began to overwrite the hatch location with a new sky.

Someone had to hold the wheel at its old setting while another person descended. The watch was bringing a search lamp through the entrance, and the analyst could not tell whether the footprints led out of the buried room. The specialist braced the wheel as the light crossed the floor and the vendor called once more.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts held the dome, found the vendor, and preserved the route to the buried observatory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch took the hatch and led the vendor back through its own cordon.
endings.draw: The vendor returned safely, but the dome changed again before either team could map the room below.

paragraphs: A drowned amphitheater appeared when the reservoir fell, its upper seats still dry above the mud. People sheltering on the central stage had made a rope ladder from their costumes. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers came down the western aisle; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill patrol approached the east, each seeking the one stable exit.

{{hero}} met a fighter at the top of the western stair, where loose stone left room for only one person. After a brief struggle, the combatant forced a passage and carried a section of railing down to the stranded people. They used it to bridge a gap between two rows, but the mud rose behind the stage as a dam sluice opened upstream.

A second railing could reach the far aisle if someone detached it from the high seats. That would leave the first bridge unsupported unless both teams held it. The combatant heard the sheltering people count their remaining steps across, while the patrol on the opposite side called out a shorter route through the water.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers carried everyone up the western aisle and held the dry amphitheater entrance.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the eastern aisle and brought the stranded people out ahead of the water.
endings.draw: Both routes met above the flood, and neither team controlled the amphitheater once the reservoir refilled.

paragraphs: The border archive began returning letters addressed to people who had not yet written them. One envelope described a dispute over the archive itself and bore tomorrow’s date. {{heroPlayer}}’s clerks entered to find its register; {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers held the mailroom while residents gathered to ask who had sent the letters.

{{hero}} unlocked the sorting ledger and found every future letter entered beside an older, unclaimed parcel. The specialist pulled that parcel from a lower shelf as the mailroom’s pneumatic tubes began delivering more envelopes. Inside the parcel was a blank boundary deed, sealed before either settlement existed.

The archive could stamp a valid deed only while its old date wheel still turned. Fixing the date might stop the strange deliveries, but it could also make the unclaimed parcel impossible to register. The specialist held the deed beneath the stamp as a ranger at the doorway asked whether the neighbors were ready to witness it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s clerks registered the deed and kept the archive open for both settlements to inspect.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers took custody of the deed and closed the mailroom pending a joint hearing.
endings.draw: The letters stopped, but the deed remained unsigned and both settlements retained a claim to the archive.

paragraphs: A shuttle landed hard on a glacier, far from its intended port, and its emergency lights glowed through the snow. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery detail arrived with a portable winch; {{otherPlayer}}’s ice patrol had already set markers around a crevasse between them and the hull. Through the cockpit glass, a passenger waved a broken radio.

{{hero}} covered the winch crew crossing a narrow bridge of snow. Fire splintered the ice ahead of them, and the fighter answered from a sheltered ridge while the crew ran its cable toward the shuttle. The cable caught, but its hook tore a panel loose and exposed a line of frost spreading across the cabin wall.

The crew could pull the shuttle a little closer, risking the panel, or take the passengers out one at a time over the crevasse. The ice patrol’s markers offered a safer route, if the detail could reach them. The fighter watched the passenger knock twice on the glass and saw the first crack climb toward the window.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail brought the passengers across and secured the stranded shuttle for recovery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s ice patrol opened its marked route and took charge of the shuttle rescue.
endings.draw: The passengers crossed safely, but the shuttle slipped into the crevasse before either party could hold it.

paragraphs: At the far end of the frontier, a geothermal lighthouse stopped turning just as a dust front swallowed the road. Its fixed beam pointed travelers toward a collapsed bridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s maintenance crew reached the tower with spare bearings; {{otherPlayer}}’s road wardens were already steering carts away from the false light.

{{hero}} climbed behind the lens and found a bearing packed with ash. The specialist cleared it and turned the mechanism by hand. One sweep revealed a second road marker almost hidden in the dust, but the motor stalled again before the travelers could see it. Someone below called that a cart had followed the fixed beam.

Keeping the lens moving needed a person at the crank; reaching the lost cart needed the lighthouse crew on the road. The wardens knew the marker’s position now, though they still distrusted the beam. The specialist drew a breath against the hot metal and heard wheels on the bridge approach, out beyond sight.
