endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored the rotating beam and led the cart onto the safe road.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens intercepted the cart and secured the tower before reopening the road.
endings.draw: The cart turned back in time, but the dust kept the lighthouse dark while both crews repaired it.

paragraphs: Wind chimes along a terraced garden rang in a pattern the gardeners had never heard. A crack was opening beneath the upper terrace, where the last families were packing their tools. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort reached the high path; {{otherPlayer}}’s valley scouts guarded a stone footbridge below, convinced it was the only safe way out.

{{hero}} climbed the high gate as a defender tried to close it against the shifting earth. The fighters grappled beside the latch, and the combatant won enough space to wedge it open with a fallen branch. Gardeners rushed through, but the path beyond the gate sagged toward the valley, pulling a row of chimes down with it.

One person could keep the gate from swinging into the path while the rest descended; the valley scouts could also lead the gardeners across their bridge if it held. The combatant braced the branch against the gate as the oldest gardener stopped to listen. All the surviving chimes were ringing in the same direction.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort cleared the terrace and guided the families along the high path before it failed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the bridge and brought the families to the valley below.
endings.draw: The families escaped by both paths, leaving the damaged terraces and their boundary markers behind.

paragraphs: A riverside clock tower began chiming whenever the ferry left its landing, even though the bell had been removed years ago. Fishermen said the sound came from a warehouse across the river. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators took the west bank; {{otherPlayer}}’s river patrol held the warehouse doors and refused to let anyone near the ferry’s old logbook.

{{hero}} covered a companion rowing toward a service window. Fire from the warehouse roof crossed the water, and the fighter shot through the rope holding an empty cargo net, dropping it between the skiff and the roof. The companion reached the window and found the missing bell hanging above a set of wires stretched to the ferry slip.

Each arriving boat pulled the wires tight enough to ring the bell. The next ferry was already midstream, and a loose weight above the logbook might fall when it docked. The fighter had a clear line to the wire, but the companion was still beneath the bell. The clock tower chimed from across the river.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators stopped the weight, recovered the logbook, and secured the warehouse.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol reached the rigging first and kept the ferry records under its guard.
endings.draw: The ferry docked safely, but the bell and the logbook were removed to separate banks pending an inquiry.

paragraphs: The spring festival’s signal kites were meant to guide supply carts through a forest cut. At noon they began pointing to a clearing that appeared on no map, and the first cart followed them in. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal team entered through the east trees; {{otherPlayer}}’s trackers approached from the ridge with a sketch of the older road.

{{hero}} climbed the central kite mast and found the lines crossed around a metal marker buried in the clearing. The specialist freed one line and read the marker’s warning: a sealed well lay directly under the cart track. Before the team could signal the first driver, a wheel dropped through the moss above the well.

The cart could be hauled back with the kite lines, but that would tear down the signals guiding those behind it. The ridge trackers were close enough to stop the next cart if they saw the warning. The specialist kept one line taut and watched the trapped driver lean out over the broken ground.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team freed the cart, rerouted the signals, and held the safe clearing for the convoy.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s trackers secured the clearing and led the carts along the mapped ridge road.
endings.draw: The cart came free, but both routes stayed closed while the old well was made safe.

paragraphs: A hollow tree at the edge of a canyon held a living archive: each leaf bore a mark from an expedition that had passed through. The newest leaves described a camp farther down the canyon, where nobody was meant to be. {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists came for a cutting; {{otherPlayer}}’s pathfinders wanted the tree left intact as a guide.

{{hero}} traced the new marks to a root exposed by erosion and found a strip of camp cloth caught beneath it. The specialist lifted the root, exposing a narrow ledge that led below the marked path. A fresh leaf unrolled with a different symbol as voices rose from the other side of the canyon.

Taking a cutting would preserve the clue if the tree fell, but opening the root farther might destroy the ledge someone had used. The pathfinders were bringing a rope to the far rim. The specialist held the cloth against the newest leaf and saw that its mark matched the voices’ location, not the hidden camp.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists preserved the new record and reached the hidden camp by the ledge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s pathfinders secured the tree and guided the search along the canyon rim.
endings.draw: The clue survived, but neither team could enter the camp before the canyon darkened.

paragraphs: At a rail waystation, a freight car arrived with its doors welded shut and its delivery seals already broken. The manifest said it held blankets for an outlying village. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired guards sought the loading ramp; {{otherPlayer}}’s local patrol held the points and wanted the car examined before it moved again.

{{hero}} took the roof of the station office while a cutter worked on the doors. Shots struck the ramp, and the fighter returned fire long enough for the cutter to expose a narrow gap. Through it came a child’s voice. The car carried people beside the blankets, and one of the couplings began to pull against the brake.

Opening the doors could free the passengers before the car rolled, but the welded edge was still hot. The patrol could lock the points and keep the car from the downhill track if it reached the lever. The fighter watched the coupling stretch while the cutter asked for another minute they might not have.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards freed the passengers and kept the freight car at the ramp for inspection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol locked the points and brought the passengers out under its own protection.
endings.draw: The passengers escaped, but the empty car rolled away before either party could claim the cargo.

paragraphs: A museum auction was interrupted when its prized sound cylinder began playing a battle no witness remembered. A collector said the recording proved ownership of the valley beyond the museum. {{heroPlayer}}’s security crew moved toward the playback room; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill militia blocked the gallery doors and demanded the cylinder for inspection.

{{hero}} covered a conservator crossing the gallery as shots chipped the marble behind them. The fighter fired into a display shutter’s release and brought it down between the conservator and the doors. At the player, the conservator found a second cylinder turning underneath the first, its wax still soft enough for new grooves to appear.

Stopping the machine would preserve the old recording but erase whatever was being cut into the new one. Across the shutter, the militia called for the collector to surrender his claim. The fighter kept the conservator in view as the unheard battle changed to a voice asking for the machine to be kept running.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured both cylinders and kept the gallery open for an independent examination.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s militia took the playback room and placed the cylinders under valley custody.
endings.draw: The new cylinder finished recording, but neither group agreed to let the other remove it.

paragraphs: The only bridge into a mining camp began counting each crossing on an old mechanical tollboard. It stopped one short of the number of people who had left that morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired escort sought the keeper’s booth to check the count; {{otherPlayer}}’s camp watch barred the bridge, worried someone was still beneath it.

{{hero}} pushed through the booth’s narrow doorway and caught a defender reaching for the tollboard’s crank. The two wrestled against its painted gears, and the fighter held the crank still long enough for a companion to read a second counter hidden behind it. That one showed an extra crossing, made after the keeper had locked the booth.

A maintenance ladder led under the bridge, but turning the crank would retract its lower rungs. Someone had been there since the count changed; the river below was rising with meltwater. The fighter kept one hand on the crank as the companion called into the darkness beneath the planks and received an answer.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort reached the person under the bridge and kept the tollbooth for the camp’s inquiry.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch took the booth and brought the missing traveler up its own ladder.
endings.draw: The traveler returned, but the two counters disagreed and both crews stayed to guard the bridge.

paragraphs: A tide clock in a landlocked laboratory began reporting the rise and fall of an ocean no one could see. Its readings predicted a surge at a dry drainage gate below the town. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians reached the instrument room; {{otherPlayer}}’s flood wardens went to the gate, certain the clock was broken.

{{hero}} opened the clock’s case and found its sensor connected to a buried reservoir instead of the distant sea. The specialist transmitted the pressure readings to the wardens and worked the manual release, but the handwheel stuck at halfway. Water began to knock beneath the laboratory floor. A caretaker found the reservoir’s old plans behind a cabinet.

The plans showed a spillway under the wardens’ position and a second release behind the locked laboratory door. Opening one might save the town and flood the other team’s route. The specialist held the plans against the turning clock face while a message came from the gate: the ground had begun to move.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians released the pressure safely and kept the laboratory and its records.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens controlled the spillway and secured the laboratory after diverting the water.
endings.draw: Both releases opened together, sparing the town but leaving the damaged clock under joint guard.

paragraphs: A cable car carrying a sealed geological core stopped above an abandoned mine. The car’s windows showed a worker inside, but the radio returned only static. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to the lower station to recover the sample; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge watch held the upper drive and said the cable might give way.

{{hero}} guarded the platform while a climber attached a rescue line. Fire from the upper station cracked a glass panel, and the fighter answered until the climber could reach the stopped car. The worker was awake and holding the core shut with both hands; a thin seam had opened along its casing.

Drawing the car down would bring the unstable casing through the crowded platform. Leaving it above the mine meant the worker would have to climb the rescue line while the car swayed. The fighter saw the ridge watch begin turning the upper drive by hand and tried to tell them what the worker was holding.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort brought the worker down and contained the core at the lower station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch held the cable and recovered the worker and core from above.
endings.draw: The worker reached safety, but the core remained suspended until both sides could secure its casing.

paragraphs: Two clans arrived at a winter hall with competing invitations to guard its hearth. Inside, an old bell rope marked the boundary between their assigned rooms. A storm had brought travelers to the hall as well, and neither guard could lock the doors while people were still coming over the pass.

{{hero}} reached the bell rope as a rival tried to pull the divider shut. The combatants wrestled across the threshold, and the fighter held the rope high enough for the travelers to pass. A stone fell from the chimney, sending smoke into the crowded hall and exposing a narrow flue above the hearth.

The flue could be cleared from the roof, but whoever climbed would leave the threshold in the other clan’s hands. Someone had to keep the door open while the smoke escaped. The fighter heard a child coughing behind the divider and saw the rival offer a ladder, its feet already set against the wrong wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guard cleared the flue and kept the hall warm under its own watch.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard took the hearth, opened the flue, and sheltered the travelers.
endings.draw: The smoke cleared, but the travelers kept both guards at the hearth until the storm passed.

paragraphs: An old hill fort still had a working semaphore on its eastern wall. A village below had sent up a runner to ask whether the ridge pass was open, but the fort’s flags were giving the opposite answer to travelers on the far side. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts climbed to the signal platform as {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders occupied the courtyard.

{{hero}} examined the gears beneath the flags and found one reversed by a fallen stone. The specialist corrected the first arm, exposing a second problem: someone had sent a warning from the opposite tower about a wagon stranded on the pass. A courier offered to carry the answer by foot while the highlanders called for the fort to be closed.

The platform could show either the safe route for the village’s travelers or the warning for the wagon’s rescuers; its damaged gearing could not display both at once. The specialist held one arm against the wind while the runner waited below, and from the pass came a small flash of reflected sunlight.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts signaled both routes in sequence and held the fort until the wagon was found.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the platform and directed the travelers from the courtyard.
endings.draw: The wagon and travelers were warned, but neither party could repair the flags before nightfall.

paragraphs: A weather balloon landed in a high pasture trailing a length of silver fabric across the shepherds’ footpath. Its recorder predicted a sudden freeze before morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery party wanted the instrument intact; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill watch feared the tether would bring down the old suspension bridge nearby.

{{hero}} shielded a technician moving toward the balloon as fire from the ridge sent the grazing animals scattering. The fighter returned fire from behind a stone trough while the technician read the first temperature record. The tether snagged the bridge’s outer cable, and each gust drew the two structures tighter together.

Severing the tether would save the bridge but send the recorder down the valley; pulling it in could strip away the cable that the shepherds needed to get home. The hill watch was coming across from the other bank with cutters. The fighter heard the bridge creak and saw the technician raise a hand for one more reading.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party recovered the recorder, freed the bridge, and sent the freeze warning down the valley.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch cut the dangerous tether and secured the pasture and bridge for the shepherds.
endings.draw: The bridge held and the warning went out, but the recorder blew away before either side could claim it.

paragraphs: An ice road across the moor began to glow from below, revealing a line of warm springs no map had recorded. The first supply sled stopped where its runners sank into softening ice. {{heroPlayer}}’s hill escort came along the near bank; {{otherPlayer}}’s winter patrol had already stepped onto the far end of the road.

{{hero}} reached the sled and found a defender pulling at the same harness buckle. The fighter forced a grip off the strap and dragged it around a rock, shifting the load toward firmer ground. Beneath the runners, the ice turned transparent; a long pipe could be seen carrying heat straight toward the narrowest part of the road.

The sled could be emptied and pulled back, but the supply barrels would need to cross before the villages ran out. Closing the buried pipe might freeze the road again, or it might crack it. The fighter held the harness as the winter patrol’s engineer knelt by a valve at the far bank.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort recovered the sled and marked a safe crossing for the supply barrels.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the valve and guided the barrels across a new route.
endings.draw: The supplies reached shore, but both parties closed the ice road until the warm pipe could be studied.

paragraphs: A centuries-old orchard stood across two survey lines, and both communities had kept bees there through the winter. The first blossom opened out of season, sending the hives toward a pump shed no one had used in years. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers came to inspect the water; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill wardens held the orchard path to protect the hives.

{{hero}} opened the pump shed and found a warm pipe feeding the roots beneath one side of the boundary. The specialist traced it to a buried valve and set a marker where its stem broke the soil. A sudden hum rose from the hives as the bees gathered over the marker, blocking the path the rangers needed for their measuring line.

Closing the valve might return the orchard to its normal season, but the early bloom was the bees’ only food after the long frost. Leaving it open could exhaust the shared reservoir. The specialist watched the wardens bring a spare hive box through the trees and wondered which survey line would still matter when spring arrived.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers regulated the warm pipe and secured the orchard for a shared spring harvest.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the pump shed and protected the hives while the reservoir was assessed.
endings.draw: The valve stayed open on a short watch, and both communities kept their boundary claims until spring.

paragraphs: Deep in a limestone quarry, miners uncovered a chamber whose walls breathed warm air through hundreds of small holes. An injured worker remained inside after a rockfall, beyond a gap too narrow for a stretcher. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue team brought a collapsible sled; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland crew controlled the quarry winch above.

{{hero}} mapped the breathing holes and found they connected to an old ventilation shaft. The specialist opened a grille and lowered a speaking tube to the worker, who answered that the air was fading. The quarry crew began clearing the main passage, but each strike sent fine dust through the holes and into the sealed chamber.

The rescue sled could pass through the shaft if the grille came free. Removing it might cut off the worker’s last clean air until the sled arrived. The specialist held the speaking tube while the winch creaked above and the worker asked how much farther the rescuers had to go.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team brought the worker through the shaft and secured the chamber for a careful survey.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s quarry crew cleared the main passage and led the worker out beneath its own watch.
endings.draw: The worker came out safely, but unstable rock kept the chamber closed to both crews.

paragraphs: A ridge beacon began sending orders in the voice of a commander who had died the previous winter. The messages pointed a supply column toward a closed mountain pass. {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers climbed the beacon steps to find its source; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the lower platform, ready to tear out the transmitter.

{{hero}} caught a defender at the narrow trapdoor beneath the beacon. The fighter forced past and found a speaking tube running from a hidden room into the transmitter housing. A fresh message began as they lifted its cover. Someone in the hidden room was reading the column’s location from a sheet still wet with ink.

The column was approaching the fork. Disabling the transmitter would stop the false orders, but the hidden reader might escape through a tunnel under the ridge. The highlanders below had found its other entrance. The fighter held the speaking tube, waiting to hear whether the reader knew the real road had been closed too.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers silenced the false orders, stopped the column, and secured the hidden room.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the beacon and warned the column from the lower platform.
endings.draw: The column halted safely, but the reader escaped before either team could learn who sent the messages.

paragraphs: At a mountain customs house, a set of scales began weighing every sack of seed grain twice. The ledgers showed a whole wagon missing from the count, though its wheel tracks ended at the locked shed. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors came through the trade road; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill guards held the shed door while farmers waited for their spring seed.

{{hero}} tested the scales with an empty sack and discovered a second pan concealed beneath the floor. The specialist followed its chain into the shed and found the missing wagon balanced on a lift over a disused cellar. A loose bolt dropped past their hand, and the wagon shifted toward the open shaft below.

Lowering the lift would bring the grain within reach but might break the last chain. The hill guards had a heavy rope ready, if the inspectors let them through the shed. The specialist held the ledger beside the lift handle as the waiting farmers counted the sacks they could see and the wagon moved again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors recovered the wagon and delivered the full seed allotment under customs seal.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the shed and brought the wagon down for the waiting farmers.
endings.draw: The grain reached the farmers, but the missing entries remained disputed at the customs house.

paragraphs: A fog machine left behind by a film crew began pumping a thick mist across a mountain infirmary’s only access road. An ambulance was due before sunset. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort sought the pump controls in a deserted shed; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill patrol controlled the road junction and thought the fog concealed a trap.

{{hero}} took a firing position beside the shed while a technician examined the machine. Fire from a stone wall struck the pressure tank, and the fighter answered to give the technician room to close a valve. The mist thinned on the road, revealing an overturned trailer and the missing film crew sheltering behind it.

The ambulance could squeeze past the trailer if it kept moving; stopping to collect the crew might block the road again. The hill patrol was already descending toward them, and the damaged tank continued to hiss. The fighter watched the technician reach for the final valve as the ambulance’s headlights appeared through the remaining fog.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort opened the road, recovered the film crew, and guided the ambulance through.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the junction and cleared the trailer before the ambulance arrived.
endings.draw: The ambulance passed, but both groups stayed at the broken machine to keep the road clear.

paragraphs: New boundary stones appeared overnight across a sheep meadow, each engraved with a different village’s seal. No cart tracks led to them. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey crew brought a scanner to the meadow; {{otherPlayer}}’s shepherds guarded the original stone and refused to let it be moved until the copies were explained.

{{hero}} scanned the engravings and found thin layers of printed material beneath the moss. One false stone hid a portable fabricator, still warm, and its feed tube ran under the grass toward the old boundary. The specialist followed the tube to a sealed box just as the machine began printing another claim.

The box held the molds for both villages’ seals. Opening it could identify the forger, but the tube crossed the sheep’s pen and a sudden pull might bring the fence down. The shepherds approached with the real stone’s worn survey marks. The specialist held the tube still while a fresh slab rose from the ground.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew stopped the fabricator and restored the meadow boundary from the original marks.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s shepherds took the box and protected the old stone until both villages could witness it.
endings.draw: The false stones were removed, but the owner of the molds remained unknown and the boundary stayed under watch.

paragraphs: A mountain chapel’s bell rang by itself whenever a traveler entered the pass below. The caretaker found a trail of wet footprints to the locked choir loft, though the roof had stayed dry. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators climbed the rear stairs; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland wardens guarded the front door and wanted the bell stopped before dark.

{{hero}} met a defender on the loft’s cramped landing and fought through to the bell rope. The fighter pulled it aside, exposing a wire attached to a small pressure plate hidden beneath the floorboards. A second wire disappeared into a side room where the caretaker said the chapel had stored its emergency provisions.

Cutting the first wire would quiet the bell, but might release whatever the second kept closed. The wardens were close to the side room from the other stair. The fighter listened as another traveler crossed the pass; the bell stayed silent, and the pressure plate under the loft began to sink.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators disabled the hidden mechanism and kept the chapel’s supplies secure.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the side room and made the bell safe for the pass travelers.
endings.draw: The bell stopped, but both teams sealed the loft when they could not trace the second wire.

paragraphs: A freight train stopped halfway across a high viaduct, its last car filled with timber needed to shore up a village school. One wheel had slipped off the rail. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers arrived with a jack from the west; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill crew held the east approach and insisted the bridge could bear no more weight.

{{hero}} covered a rigger crawling beneath the tilted car. Gunfire hit the iron truss above them, and the fighter returned fire from behind a signal post while the rigger fitted the jack. The wheel lifted a finger’s width. Then a bolt dropped from the truss, and the car shifted toward the outer edge.

The jack needed a heavier base, but the only spare sleepers were stacked at the guarded east end. The hill crew was signaling that it had a safer plan from that side. The fighter could see the school’s timber through the car’s broken door as another bolt worked loose overhead.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers reset the wheel, moved the timber, and kept the viaduct open for repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s hill crew secured the east approach and brought the car back onto the rails.
endings.draw: The timber came off safely, but both crews closed the viaduct until its trusses were rebuilt.

paragraphs: At an old sawmill, a locked cabinet began issuing receipts for logs that had never arrived. Each receipt charged a different farmer for the same grove of trees. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors came to the counting desk; {{otherPlayer}}’s woodland wardens blocked the loading bay, where someone had stacked freshly cut trunks.

{{hero}} opened the cabinet and found a mechanical printer connected to the mill’s weighing bridge. The specialist balanced an empty dolly on the bridge; the printer produced one more false receipt, pointing to a hidden counterweight under the floor. A quick inspection revealed a crawlspace with the real timber ledger at its end.

Pulling out the counterweight would end the fraud but might drop the bridge onto anyone in the crawlspace. The wardens were opening the bay to check the stacked wood. The specialist held the empty dolly still as footsteps sounded beneath the weighing platform, moving toward the ledger.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors recovered the ledger and corrected the false charges while holding the mill.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens secured the timber and brought the mill’s records to the farmers.
endings.draw: The printing stopped, but the true ownership of the stacked trunks remained under joint investigation.

paragraphs: A radio mast on a bare summit began carrying a shepherd’s song from three valleys at once. A research team claimed an unknown transmitter was buried beneath it; the hill wardens believed the mast had simply broken. {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors climbed from the north while {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol held the stone shelter beside the aerial.

{{hero}} held the path as a surveyor tested the mast footing. Fire from the shelter struck the metal housing, and the fighter answered while the surveyor dug a dark receiver from the rock. It was receiving the song from below the summit. When the aerial turned, the receiver’s faint light swung toward a second hill.

The buried device could be carried away, but removing it would cut off the signal that might lead to the missing singer. The hill patrol was bringing a spade to the other side of the footing. The fighter heard the song pause for a breath, then resume with a verse none of the shepherds knew.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors kept the receiver and traced the new verse to its hidden source.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the summit and followed the signal from the shelter.
endings.draw: The song faded, leaving both teams with part of the bearing and the summit still contested.

paragraphs: A stone floodgate had held a mountain lake for generations. Its keeper found the control chamber open and a fresh score cut across the old waterline. {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition came to inspect the mark; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders guarded the raised causeway as rain swelled the lake behind it.

{{hero}} entered the gatehouse and seized a loose chain as a defender lunged for the release lever. The fighters struggled above the grinding gate, and the combatant pulled the chain tight enough to stop its downward slide. From the opposite window, the keeper saw that the score on the stone was a warning: the old wall had shifted overnight.

The gate could be opened to relieve the pressure, but water would fill the lower path where travelers were sheltering. Holding it shut might spare the path until they moved, if the wall lasted. The combatant kept the chain wrapped around a post as the keeper shouted for the highlanders to clear the causeway.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition cleared the lower path, opened the gate safely, and held the control chamber.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the causeway and controlled the release after moving the travelers.
endings.draw: The water receded, but the damaged wall left the gatehouse under a shared emergency watch.

paragraphs: During an eclipse, a glass lake showed the reflection of a road that did not exist along its shore. A cart driver followed the image and disappeared behind a ridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s observers brought instruments to the water; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill trackers searched the real road for the driver’s prints.

{{hero}} set an instrument at the lake’s edge and found a second landscape projected through the glass from a hidden lens. The specialist aligned it with the ridge and exposed a narrow service track concealed by the falling shadow. A distant lantern appeared where the driver had vanished, then blinked as though someone were asking for help.

The service track would be visible only while the eclipse lasted. The trackers knew a longer path across the ridge, but the driver’s cart might already be trapped on the short one. The specialist kept the instrument aligned with one hand and signaled toward the lantern with the other as daylight began to return.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers reached the cart and marked the concealed track before the reflection vanished.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s trackers found the driver by the ridge path and secured the lake approach.
endings.draw: The driver returned, but the hidden track disappeared before either team could establish its route.

paragraphs: A ruined map room on a high plateau contained a wall of dark glass showing unfamiliar mountain passes. Someone had scratched a fresh route across its surface and marked a shelter that the hill patrol still used. {{heroPlayer}}’s cartographers entered the room; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders held the adjacent stair to prevent anyone following the new mark.

{{hero}} kept the stair in view as a cartographer measured the glass. Fire cracked the frame, and the fighter answered from the doorway while the cartographer pried away a loose panel. Behind it was a second map, cut into the stone before the glass had been installed, showing a path beneath the shelter rather than through it.

Removing the panel would reveal the full path but leave the glass wall unsupported above the cartographer. The highlanders said the shelter was occupied tonight, and someone was already moving toward its lower entrance. The fighter watched a new light appear behind the glass, directly over the mark for the occupied room.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s cartographers secured the map room and warned the shelter before reaching the hidden path.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the room and closed the path beneath their occupied shelter.
endings.draw: The shelter was warned, but the glass wall fell and buried the route before either party could claim it.

paragraphs: A root cellar beneath a shepherd’s cottage started growing pale moss shaped like the surrounding hills. One mound held a dark gap where the cottage’s well should have been. {{heroPlayer}}’s field observers came to examine the growth; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill watch arrived with the shepherd, who said his sister had gone down for water.

{{hero}} traced the missing well on the living map and located a blocked side shaft behind the shelves. The specialist eased the shelves aside and heard the sister answer from below. As the wall opened, the moss began to curl away from a second gap that pointed toward the shepherd’s house, as though the ground there were moving too.

The sister could climb the side shaft if it was cleared now, but someone needed to keep watch over the new gap beneath the house. The hill watch had brought a rope and a lantern. The specialist kept a hand on the shelves as the cellar floor gave a low crack, and the shepherd called his sister’s name again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers opened the shaft, brought the sister up, and secured the cottage before it shifted.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch recovered the sister and moved the shepherd from the threatened house.
endings.draw: Both escaped, but the cottage settled over the map and neither party could hold the cellar.

paragraphs: A village registry listed a stranger as the owner of every empty room, including the old assembly hall. The person had never arrived, yet a key had been cut for each door. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators came for the key press; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders occupied the hall while displaced families waited outside for shelter.

{{hero}} examined the registry and matched the false entries to a single stamp worn at one corner. The specialist found it in the basement press, set beside a stack of unsigned housing permits. Upstairs, the highlanders discovered that the hall’s storeroom door had already been locked from within, and a faint tapping came through it.

The press could void the false keys, but turning its lever would stamp the unsigned permits as well. Opening the storeroom first might reveal who made the entries, while the families remained in the cold. The specialist held the worn stamp against the oldest permit as someone inside the locked room asked for a light.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators exposed the false entries and reopened the hall for the waiting families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders secured the hall and issued rooms after taking custody of the press.
endings.draw: The families found shelter, but the stranger’s name remained on the registry under joint review.

paragraphs: A survey camera frozen into a mountain ledge sent out its first image in years: a bright doorway in a wall of ice. The hill patrol said there was no doorway there when it passed at dawn. {{heroPlayer}}’s retrieval crew sought the camera’s memory unit; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders watched the ice wall from a neighboring ridge.

{{hero}} covered a technician edging across the ledge. Gunfire from the ridge struck the ice beside the camera, and the fighter answered while the technician removed the memory unit. The next image showed the doorway opening outward, with a figure carrying something toward the slope. Then a crack ran between the ledge and the frozen wall.

The technician could save the camera or go after the figure, not both. The highlanders were already descending toward the wall by another route. The fighter saw a fresh track in the snow and heard a dull knock from behind the ice as the camera prepared its final exposure.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the images and reached the hidden doorway before the ledge fell.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders secured the ice wall and brought the figure out by their descent route.
endings.draw: The last image survived, but the doorway vanished when the ice broke away from the ledge.

paragraphs: The ceremonial forge at a mountain fair was meant to light a signal fire for the villages beyond the pass. Its bellows had been strapped shut, and the unlit brazier was already being carried up the ridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort reached the smithy from the fairground; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland guard controlled the lane to the signal platform.

{{hero}} caught a defender at the forge door and forced a way to the bellows in a tight struggle among the cold tools. The fighter cut the straps, and the smith pumped a first breath of air into the coals. A runner returned from the ridge: the brazier had arrived, but its bearer could not light it against the wind.

The coals could be carried up in a covered pan, if someone held the lane open long enough. The highland guard claimed it had another way to light the platform from above. The fighter lifted the pan while sparks caught in its lid and listened for the first signal call from the far village.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort carried the coals up the lane and lit the signal for the distant villages.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard secured the platform and sent the signal from its own fire.
endings.draw: The signal burned, but neither guard kept the forge once the fair returned to its work.

paragraphs: An abandoned mine began exhaling warm air through a courthouse floor during a hearing about who owned the mountain. The judge stopped proceedings when a miner identified the smell of fresh lantern oil. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors came through the cellar; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill guard kept the court above as witnesses gathered around the crack.

{{hero}} found a blocked vent beneath the judge’s bench and traced it to a side gallery shown on no mine plan. The specialist opened an inspection plate and uncovered a miner’s lamp burning on a ledge beyond. It had been left beside a row of survey pegs planted from inside the disputed hill.

Following the pegs might settle the hearing, but removing the inspection plate had let the mine’s air into the crowded court. The judge wanted the room cleared; the hill guard said it could hold the door while the inspectors went down. The specialist held the lamp up to the pegs and read a date older than either claim.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the gallery and presented the old survey line to the court.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard took the gallery and brought the dated pegs out for the hearing.
endings.draw: The court evacuated safely, but the gallery was sealed before anyone could establish the line’s full route.

paragraphs: A giant tracking dish on the moor turned toward a mountain rescue aircraft that had gone missing in clear weather. Its operator said the dish was following the plane’s emergency tag, though the signal came from inside the fenced compound. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery detail entered by the south gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill patrol held the control tower.

{{hero}} covered an operator crossing to the dish base as fire from the tower raked the fence. The fighter answered until the operator opened a buried junction box. Inside lay the missing plane’s tag, wired to a repeater pointing beyond the mountain. The repeater clicked twice, then showed a second signal from the far valley.

If the operator removed the tag, the false signal would stop, but the repeater might lose the plane’s real position. The hill patrol could turn the dish from the tower if it took over the controls. The fighter watched the far signal blink while the operator reached for the tag’s loose wire.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail held the dish and traced the aircraft to the far valley.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the controls and followed the plane’s second signal.
endings.draw: The false tag was isolated, but both teams shared the dish while the aircraft search continued.

paragraphs: A road tunnel lost its lights while a wedding procession was halfway through. An old evacuation map showed an exit on the ridge, but that door had been bricked up years ago. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers came to the west portal with portable lamps; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland volunteers entered from the east to lead the travelers back.

{{hero}} located the failed junction behind a wet service hatch and restored one row of lamps. Their light revealed a fresh crack across the tunnel roof and a narrow maintenance passage the map had omitted. The specialist marked it with reflective tape as the procession’s last cart reached the damaged section.

The new passage could take people on foot, but not the cart or its elderly passengers. Keeping the main tunnel lit might allow the cart through before the roof shifted; moving everyone into the passage would leave it behind. The specialist held a lamp beneath the crack while the volunteers called from the far portal.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers led the procession out and kept the tunnel closed for safe repairs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers brought the travelers and their cart through the east portal.
endings.draw: The people escaped, but the cart stayed inside and both crews guarded the tunnel until dawn.

paragraphs: A potter’s kiln on the mountain edge fired a set of tiles bearing a map of the old footpaths. The potter had promised the tiles to both villages, and each sent an escort to collect them before a heavy rain. {{heroPlayer}}’s party reached the kiln door; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill guard came by the path the map was meant to mark.

{{hero}} faced a defender in the kiln’s narrow loading bay and wrestled past the open door. The fighter caught a rack of cooling tiles before it fell into the coals. One tile showed a culvert running beneath the mountain path, where the rain was already pooling, and the potter said its old cover had been removed.

The tiles were too hot to carry all at once. The hill guard knew the shortest way to the culvert; the potter could identify which tile marked its remaining cover. The fighter held the rack steady as the first drops hissed on the kiln roof and a messenger called that the path had begun to sink.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party carried the map to the path and closed the dangerous crossing before the rain.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guard secured the kiln and used the tiles to warn both villages.
endings.draw: The crossing was marked, but the villages divided the hot tiles before either could claim the path.

paragraphs: A migratory flock stopped circling a hilltop fire tower and gathered on its empty signal frame. The tower keeper said the birds returned every year to a nesting cliff that had vanished behind a new quarry fence. {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers came to follow the flock; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill watch controlled the tower and feared the birds would scatter if fighting reached it.

{{hero}} held position beside the tower stairs while a tracker checked the keeper’s old field notes. Fire from the lower fence struck a rung, and the fighter answered until the tracker could reach the frame. There, a ring from one bird’s leg matched a mark on the notes beside a photograph of a cave in the fenced cliff.

The flock would leave at dusk. The cave entrance might be visible from the tower if its signal lamp turned toward the quarry, but the hill watch wanted the birds left undisturbed. The fighter watched the flock lift together and saw one bird fly low through a gap in the fence.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s trackers found the cave and secured the route before the flock moved on.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch kept the tower and guided the birds back to the cliff from above.
endings.draw: The flock reached its nesting cliff, but both parties left the cave unclaimed to protect the birds.

paragraphs: A high monastery offered shelter to anyone who could follow its lanterns through the fog. Tonight the lanterns pointed toward a ledge that had fallen away. {{heroPlayer}}’s pathfinders reached the upper shrine; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland patrol guarded the lower trail where travelers were beginning to gather.

{{hero}} opened the lantern mechanism and found an old paper route card jammed beneath its gearing. The specialist freed it and turned one lamp toward a surviving stair cut into the rock. A second lamp would not turn; its cable ran across the broken ledge to a small chapel where someone had lit a new flame.

Moving the trapped lamp by force could swing all the others toward the drop. The highlanders could wave the travelers onto the lower trail, but that way ended before the chapel. The specialist held the route card against the glass while the distant flame blinked once, as if somebody inside had seen the change.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s pathfinders corrected the lanterns, reached the chapel, and guided the travelers to shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the lower trail and led the travelers around the broken ledge.
endings.draw: The travelers reached shelter, but the chapel light went out before either party could claim the route.

paragraphs: A line of white roots broke through the mountain road and spelled a pattern across its surface. A botanist said they were following warmth from something buried beneath the pass. {{heroPlayer}}’s field team came with a sampling case; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland wardens stopped traffic while the roots spread toward an old water cistern.

{{hero}} traced the warmest strand and exposed a cracked pipe feeding the cistern. The specialist placed a sensor against the root and watched it pulse in time with knocks from inside the stonework. A small hatch beneath the road opened a finger’s width, releasing warm air and the smell of metal.

Widening the hatch would let the team inspect what lay beneath, but could sever the roots that marked its position. The wardens were preparing to dig at the cistern end before the road collapsed. The specialist watched the sensor’s pulse change as footsteps approached the buried chamber from somewhere below.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team preserved the living trail and opened the buried chamber safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens secured the cistern and closed the road while its foundation was explored.
endings.draw: The chamber stayed sealed, and both teams marked the living roots for a joint return.

paragraphs: A coal depot on the mountain line had one train full of fuel and two villages running out of heat. The depot’s weighing book claimed the train had already left, though its engine still stood on the siding. {{heroPlayer}}’s contracted guards approached the loading shed; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill watch held the points to keep the train from moving.

{{hero}} covered a worker climbing to check the coal hoppers. Fire from the points struck the signal post, and the fighter answered until the worker reached the first car. Its top layer was coal, but beneath it lay sacks of grain marked for a third village. The engine gave a sudden lurch against its brake.

Sending the train uphill would warm one village and strand the grain below; sending it downhill might leave both places cold by morning. The hill watch was calling for the manifest to be read before the points moved. The fighter kept a line on the engine as the worker threw down a grain sack for all to see.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards held the depot, divided the cargo, and sent both deliveries on their way.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch secured the points and arranged the deliveries from the full manifest.
endings.draw: The cargo was counted, but the train stayed at the depot while both villages argued over the fuel.

paragraphs: Photographic plates from a mountain survey appeared for sale in a shuttered gallery. The photographs showed a tunnel that ran under the hill wardens’ winter storehouse. {{heroPlayer}}’s contracted security reached the gallery first; {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens came to inspect the negatives before anyone could copy them.

{{hero}} guarded the darkroom while a photographer developed the last plate. Shots rang through the gallery and splintered a rack of empty frames. The fighter returned fire as the photographer lifted the wet image into the red light: the tunnel door was open, and a familiar supply crate was being carried inside.

The wet plate could be fixed and preserved if the photographer stayed in the darkroom. Going to the storehouse now might catch whoever took the crate, but the image would spoil and the wardens could close the tunnel unseen. The fighter watched the photographer lower the plate into its final bath as a door opened at the far end of the gallery.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s security kept the negatives and reached the hidden storehouse tunnel with the evidence intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the gallery and recovered the missing crate beneath their own storehouse.
endings.draw: The crate was found, but the final plate was spoiled before either team could establish who moved it.

paragraphs: The mountain aqueduct fed three flour mills from a single stone sluice. At dawn, its keeper found the wheel turned toward a fourth channel, one that ended in a bricked-up cellar. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired hands climbed to the control house; {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders held the main channel while the millers waited below.

{{hero}} met a defender at the wheel and fought for the cramped space between its spokes and the wall. The fighter stopped the turning wheel with a wooden wedge. Water backed up behind the gate, and a voice sounded from the blocked cellar: someone was trapped on the far side of the new channel.

The fourth channel could be drained to reach the voice, but that would shut all three mills at once. The highlanders said they could break through from the outside if the gate held long enough. The fighter felt the wedge begin to splinter as the keeper counted how fast the water was rising.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s hands drained the cellar, freed its occupant, and restored the aqueduct to the mills.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s highlanders took the sluice and opened the cellar from their side.
endings.draw: The occupant escaped, but the mills stayed shut while both crews repaired the strained wheel.

paragraphs: A hydrophone in a mountain lake picked up hammering that came at the same hour each afternoon. The divers who installed it said there was no wreck beneath the water, only a drowned road. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians brought a cable reel; {{otherPlayer}}’s hill watch held the boathouse and worried the sound came from its old foundations.

{{hero}} calibrated the hydrophone against the boathouse wall and found the hammering closer than the divers thought. The specialist lowered a camera beside the lake steps, revealing a sealed maintenance door below the waterline. Its handle moved once against the current, and the cable reel began to pull toward it.

The door could be opened from the boathouse cellar, but the cellar would flood if its lower seal gave way. The hill watch was carrying sandbags through the upper doors. The specialist watched the cable go taut as the hammering started again, this time in a pattern that matched the camera’s light.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians opened the maintenance door and secured the boathouse before the cellar flooded.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch held the boathouse and reached the door from the dry cellar.
endings.draw: The sound was traced, but the flooded door remained shut under a watch shared by both teams.

paragraphs: The village weather tower flashed a fire warning while snow still lay in the streets. Residents smelled smoke near a store of lamp oil, but the tower keeper insisted its sensors were reading heat from underground. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors reached the oil store; {{otherPlayer}}’s highland wardens secured the tower ladder.

{{hero}} covered an electrician crossing between the tower and the store. Fire from a nearby roof struck the warning bell, and the fighter answered while the electrician found a wire leading into the snow-covered cellar. The cellar wall was hot to the touch. Under it, someone had been burning a path through the frozen ground.

Opening the cellar might release the heat beneath the oil drums; leaving it shut might let the hidden fire spread under the houses. The wardens were calling for the tower’s old drainage plans. The fighter watched the electrician mark the warm wall while a line of steam rose from the snow at the first doorstep.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors diverted the underground heat and kept the oil store and tower safe.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens took the tower and opened the drainage route before the fire spread.
endings.draw: The oil was moved, but both groups evacuated the street until the underground fire burned out.

paragraphs: Two patrols received identical sealed dispatches ordering them to claim the same frontier signal hut. The hut’s operator had gone missing, leaving a lantern lit and a kettle still warm. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts came through the pines; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol entered from the old road, each carrying a key that fit the same door.

{{hero}} opened the signal register and found an unfinished message marked for both patrols. The specialist held its page to the lantern and read a warning about a fallen bridge, then noticed a second line written in fading ink beneath it. The other key turned in a cabinet at the back of the hut.

The fading line could identify where the operator had gone, if the page was copied before it vanished. The bridge warning had to be sent before the next supply wagon arrived. The specialist placed the page beside the transmitter while the other patrol opened the cabinet and found a pair of muddy boots.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts sent the warning, found the operator, and kept the signal hut through the night.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol took the hut and followed the operator’s trail after warning the wagon.
endings.draw: The wagon was warned, but both patrols kept copies of the fading message and shared the watch.

paragraphs: A rocket’s spent guidance ring fell into a hillside vineyard without burning the vines. Its indicator still showed an incoming object that the local skywatch had not reported. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery team reached the vineyard gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts held the stone terraces and wanted the ring removed before harvest.

{{hero}} covered an engineer working on the ring as fire from the terraces struck a metal post. The fighter answered while the engineer copied a set of coordinates into a notebook. The ring’s needle swung toward the workers’ cottages across the valley and began marking a time that was suddenly minutes away.

The ring might guide a warning if its transmitter remained powered. Carrying it away would protect the vines but lose the signal to whatever was coming. The scouts had a path down to the cottages; the recovery team had the transmitter key. The fighter watched the needle settle as the engineer asked who would warn the residents.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team sent the warning and secured the guidance ring for a safe recovery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the vineyard and alerted the cottages from the terraces.
endings.draw: The residents moved to safety, but the guidance ring failed before either team learned what it tracked.

paragraphs: A cartographer’s winter cabin contained an atlas that revealed new roads when its pages warmed beside the stove. One page now showed a crossing over a ravine where the rope bridge had been cut. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol reached the stove; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts came through the back window to secure the atlas.

{{hero}} held the bookcase against a defender trying to drag the atlas away. The fighter pushed free and carried the warm page toward the window, where the crossing appeared as a thin line under the snow. The stove door swung open during the struggle, and sparks caught a stack of the cartographer’s older maps.

The page would lose its route as it cooled. Saving the maps meant returning to the stove, while following the line meant leaving the cabin before the snow covered it. The scout at the window called that someone had started across the ravine already. The fighter held the atlas open to the last bright mark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol saved the atlas and reached the hidden crossing before its mark faded.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the cabin and guided the traveler back from the ravine.
endings.draw: The maps survived, but the warm route disappeared and both patrols left the crossing unclaimed.

paragraphs: Smoke appeared in a protected forest, but the firewatch tower showed no heat at all. The watcher’s last message described a line of white ash crossing a dry creek. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers entered along the creek bed; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts guarded the tower, whose lens still pointed at the wrong slope.

{{hero}} followed the ash to a hollow stump containing a live ember and a length of insulated wire. The specialist traced the wire toward the tower and found it tied into the lens motor. Turning off the motor brought the true hillside into view: someone had laid a chain of fires beneath the trees.

The rangers could cut the wire to stop the false reading, but doing so would lose the tower’s powered alarm. The scouts were bringing water from the creek while the watcher climbed down with a hand bell. The specialist held the wire apart and watched the first true flame reach a branch above the creek.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers restored the warning and contained the fire before it crossed the creek.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the tower and stopped the fires from the high slope.
endings.draw: The forest was spared, but the burned wire left the tower under a shared night watch.

paragraphs: A botanical caravan arrived at a border conservatory carrying a rare plant whose scent identified a contaminated spring. Its jars had to reach the greenhouse before their seals dried out. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to the east doors; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts controlled the west entrance and asked to inspect every jar.

{{hero}} guarded a porter crossing the conservatory floor. Fire from the west shattered a pane overhead, and the fighter returned fire while the porter sheltered the jars beneath a planting table. One jar began to leak. The exposed plant turned its leaves toward a drain that carried water from the spring into the conservatory.

The porter could seal the jar, preserving the sample, or follow the drain and find the contamination before more water reached the plants. The scouts were coming through the west greenhouse door with an empty test case. The fighter watched the leaf tips darken as the first drops ran under the table.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort saved the sample and closed the contaminated feed at the conservatory.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the greenhouse and traced the bad water to its source.
endings.draw: The feed was shut, but the damaged sample left both teams without a complete test of the spring.

paragraphs: A courier station under the frontier road held letters meant to be opened only after a ceasefire. Its keeper reported that someone had begun reading them aloud through the old speaking tubes. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators entered from a storm drain; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts held the mail hatch, determined to preserve the sealed packets.

{{hero}} reached the central sorting table as a defender tried to close the drain grille. The fighter wrestled through and caught a falling bundle before its seals broke. Beneath it sat a speaking tube with its mouthpiece still warm and a register open to a delivery scheduled for the following morning.

Silencing the tube would protect the unread letters, but might also leave the unseen reader free to warn whoever was coming for tomorrow’s delivery. The scouts called from the mail hatch that the keeper had gone missing. The fighter held the bundle as a voice in the tube began reading a letter addressed to the keeper himself.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators found the reader and secured the unopened letters before delivery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the sorting room and kept the packets sealed under guard.
endings.draw: The voice stopped, but the keeper’s letter remained sealed and the station stayed under joint watch.

paragraphs: The only ferry across a border gorge arrived with its deck empty and a ledger full of passenger names. The ferryman was nowhere aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock inspectors entered the lower quay; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts guarded the upper landing where the missing passengers’ families had gathered.

{{hero}} checked the ferry’s chain and found its counterweight rigged to stop at a narrow ledge halfway across. The specialist lowered a mirror on a pole and saw several passengers sheltering there with the ferryman. The ledge’s rope ladder had broken, and the chain would move again at the next tide change.

The inspectors could reverse the ferry to reach the ledge, but that would bring its deck against the fragile rock. The scouts had a rope long enough from the upper landing if someone held the ferry still. The specialist gripped the counterweight brake as a passenger waved from under the overhang.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors held the ferry and brought the passengers back to the lower quay.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the upper landing and lifted the passengers from the ledge.
endings.draw: Everyone returned, but the damaged ferry remained tied between the two landings.

paragraphs: A seismograph in a hill clinic drew a sharp line just as the floor began to hum. The doctor feared a rockfall would seal the recovery ward from the outside. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers arrived with a portable brace; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts held the back path, where patients were waiting to be moved.

{{hero}} studied the instrument’s older traces and found the tremor was moving toward the clinic’s buried cistern. The specialist fitted the brace to the ward door and uncovered an emergency drain in the floor. Water rose through it, carrying grit from below, and the seismograph drew a second line closer than the first.

Draining the cistern would relieve the pressure but could undermine the back path while patients crossed. Keeping it full might hold the path and break the ward wall. The specialist held the drain key as the doctor called for the next stretcher and the scouts shouted that stones were falling near their exit.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers stabilized the ward and moved the patients before the cistern failed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts held the back path and evacuated the patients under their guard.
endings.draw: The patients reached safety, but both teams left the damaged clinic closed for repairs.

paragraphs: A portable printing press appeared beside a forest trail, turning out fresh maps of a clearing that none of the local scouts recognized. Each sheet added one more building than the last. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage crew came to examine the machine; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier patrol held the trailhead and warned hikers away from the unmarked path.

{{hero}} stopped the press between sheets and found its rollers etched from a slowly changing image feed. The specialist rewound the last print to reveal a child-sized silhouette at a window in the newest building. A mechanical shutter clicked inside the press, and another sheet started feeding through, now showing the window open.

Following the map might lead to the child, if the press was showing a real place. Removing its image unit would preserve the source but end the live prints. The patrol could see a clearing through the trees, empty except for one foundation. The specialist held the new sheet beside the old one as the shutter clicked again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew traced the image feed and reached the building before the press fell silent.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the clearing and found the source of the changing maps.
endings.draw: The final sheet preserved the clue, but both groups lost the live feed before locating its subject.

paragraphs: At a forest puppet theater, the last performance ended with one puppet speaking in the voice of a missing stagehand. The audience had gone home, but the curtain kept moving on its own. {{heroPlayer}}’s stage crew returned through the painted side door; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts guarded the exit to the woods.

{{hero}} reached the fly gallery and caught a defender trying to cut the main curtain rope. The fighter wrestled the knife free and held the rope while a puppeteer crossed the dark stage. Behind the curtain, they found the missing stagehand in a narrow service booth, operating a warning light aimed at the trees.

The stagehand said someone was following the light toward the theater. Bringing the curtain down would hide the booth, but trap the stagehand behind a jammed floor hatch. The frontier scouts had seen a second light in the woods. The fighter gripped the rope while the puppeteer tried the hatch and the painted trees onstage began to sway.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew freed the stagehand and held the theater until the second light was found.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the stage and guided the person in the woods to safety.
endings.draw: The stagehand escaped, but the source of the second light remained beyond the theater’s boundary.

paragraphs: At a quarry’s upper lift, a cage of saplings hung over a freshly cut cliff road. The village had ordered the young trees to stabilize the slope, but the lift was stuck above an exposed fault. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers came with a spare motor; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts held the lower road beneath the load.

{{hero}} covered a mechanic crossing the quarry rim as fire struck the empty cable drum. The fighter answered while the mechanic fitted the motor and ran the cage down a few meters. A branch caught on a survey flag, pulling its stake free; the fresh fault ran directly beneath the workers’ planned planting line.

The saplings could be set farther up the slope, if the riggers held the cage long enough to move them by hand. The scouts said a safer line lay across the road under their control. The fighter watched a crack follow the fallen flag stake and saw the mechanic reach for the lift brake.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers lowered the saplings and planted them along a stable line above the road.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the lower road and established a safe planting line from below.
endings.draw: The trees survived, but neither crew reopened the cliff road until its fault was mapped.

paragraphs: A frontier inn kept a sealed cabinet of travel bonds for people crossing in winter. One morning every bond inside bore the same stranger’s signature, and the innkeeper refused to open the main road until the accounts were checked. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors took the counting table; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts held the stable where the travelers had gathered.

{{hero}} examined the cabinet lock and found a thin ribbon threaded through its hinge. The specialist pulled it free to reveal a roll of genuine signatures hidden behind the false bonds. At the far end of the ribbon was a ticket for a cart due to leave that afternoon, with one traveler’s name crossed out by hand.

The auditors could verify the bonds and let the crossing reopen, but the altered ticket might point to someone about to vanish. The scouts were checking the cart in the stable while the travelers waited in the cold. The specialist held the ribbon to the window and saw a second name written under the crossed one.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors restored the bonds, located the missing traveler, and reopened the road.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the cart and the cabinet for the innkeeper’s inquiry.
endings.draw: The crossing reopened, but the altered ticket remained under joint examination when the cart departed.

paragraphs: A peat bog began releasing bright spheres of light each time someone crossed the old boardwalk. The last walker had left a boot behind and disappeared into the mist. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers approached from the dry bank; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts held the far end of the boards, calling for everyone to stay clear of the water.

{{hero}} kept the searchers covered as they followed the loose boot. Shots cut through the mist, and the fighter returned fire toward the far bank until a searcher found a metal box beneath one plank. Its lid was warm. Opening it dimmed the lights and revealed a second boot wedged in mud a few steps ahead.

The spheres could guide the searchers farther into the bog if the box stayed open, but each light made them visible to anyone on the far bank. The scouts were throwing a rope toward the second boot. The fighter watched the lights gather over a patch of reeds as a voice called from beyond it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers reached the missing walker and secured the box and boardwalk.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts found the walker by rope and took control of the bog crossing.
endings.draw: The walker came back safely, but the lights returned after both parties left the box in place.

paragraphs: The bell in an old granite watchtower rang every time stones shifted on the mountain above it. This afternoon it would not stop. {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition climbed to the bell chamber while {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts held the village road, where a line of carts had already formed.

{{hero}} grappled with a defender at the chamber’s narrow stair and forced enough space for a surveyor to inspect the bell. It was being struck by a counterweight linked to a rock face beyond the village. The surveyor found a new crack along the link as the bell began ringing twice as fast.

Cutting the link would quiet the tower but remove the last warning of a slide. Keeping it intact meant the carts could not tell one strike from another. The fighter braced a hand against the swinging weight while the scouts below shouted that the last cart had lost a wheel.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition secured the tower and signaled the carts through before the rock face shifted.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts cleared the village road and took over the warning from below.
endings.draw: The carts escaped, but the tower was abandoned when the bell’s link finally broke.

paragraphs: A floodplain appeared dry in the morning and filled with reflected stars by noon, though the sky was blue. A survey wagon had stopped in its center, its driver afraid to cross the shining ground. {{heroPlayer}}’s observers entered from the north; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts marked the far bank with rope.

{{hero}} set a probe among the reflections and detected a thin sheet of water beneath a clear film. The specialist traced a seam to a buried drainage key while the driver waved from the wagon. A stone dropped onto the film did not break it; a wheel turning slowly left a spreading white line.

Opening the drain might save the wagon but draw the hidden sheet toward the scouts’ rope line. Leaving the film untouched meant the driver could run out of daylight. The specialist held the key above the seam as the wagon horse stepped forward and the white line lengthened.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers drained the plain and led the wagon out over solid ground.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the rope line and pulled the wagon toward the far bank.
endings.draw: The driver escaped, but the wagon stayed on the plain until the strange film disappeared.

paragraphs: At the top of a forest observatory, a telescope showed a map painted on the underside of its own mirror. The map led to a sealed clearing that neither nearby patrol recognized. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers sought the mirror controls while {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts guarded the stair down to the trees.

{{hero}} held the dome entrance as a researcher turned the telescope. Shots hit the metal shutter, and the fighter answered while the map slid into focus. One mark showed a maintenance hatch beneath the clearing; a second appeared only when a lamp shone through the mirror, marking someone’s fresh footprints beside it.

The researcher could detach the mirror and preserve the evidence or leave it aligned to guide a team through the forest. The scouts were already moving toward the clearing from the lower stair. The fighter watched the lamp’s beam move across the new footprints while the dome motor began to slip.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers held the telescope and opened the marked hatch before its alignment failed.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the clearing and reached the hatch from below.
endings.draw: The mirror was saved, but both teams lost the footprints before either could identify who made them.

paragraphs: A patch of pale fungi spread through an abandoned maze garden, tracing the footsteps of visitors who had entered before the gates were locked. A gardener said one set never came out. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers reached the central fountain; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts held the gate with a hand-drawn plan.

{{hero}} followed the newest fungal marks to a hedge grown over an old maintenance door. The specialist eased it open and found a glove beside a ladder leading under the fountain. A faint knock came from below, but the fungus on the door began closing over the gap as soon as fresh air entered.

The searchers could hold the door and send one person down, or cut the hedge and risk destroying the tracks that led to the missing visitor. The scouts brought their plan to the opposite side of the fountain. The specialist held the glove above the opening while the knock came again, weaker.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers reached the visitor and kept the garden entrance for the rescue.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts found the fountain ladder and brought the visitor through the gate.
endings.draw: The visitor emerged safely, but the living tracks vanished before either party could keep the maze.

paragraphs: A pottery village woke to find its water gate opening and closing in time with the kiln fires. The canals flooded whenever the potters stoked their furnaces. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers went to the gate controls; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts stood between the canals and the loaded kilns.

{{hero}} traced the gate’s control wire to a temperature sensor bolted behind a clay oven. The specialist disconnected it and held the gate steady, but the canal level kept rising. A second sensor was buried beneath the oldest kiln, where a firing of ceremonial tiles could not be interrupted without ruining them.

The potters could stop their firing and expose the sensor or keep the kilns hot while the scouts blocked the canal by hand. The specialist watched the oldest kiln’s chimney turn red and heard the gate motor strain against its new setting. One more surge would reach the workshop floors.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers separated the sensors, protected the tiles, and held the water gate.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts secured the canal and kept water away from the working kilns.
endings.draw: The workshops stayed dry, but the gate remained under joint manual control until the firing ended.

paragraphs: A weather station beside a gorge stopped transmitting after recording a sharp fall in temperature. Its keeper’s snowshoe tracks ended at the station fence, beside a dropped glove and an unopened field notebook. {{heroPlayer}}’s retrieval team approached through the pines; {{otherPlayer}}’s frontier scouts guarded the suspension path across the gorge.

{{hero}} covered a technician crossing the fence while fire struck the station’s vane. The fighter answered from a rock shelf as the technician recovered the last data card. It showed a pocket of cold air rising from a hollow beneath the station, with a recent heat trace moving toward the gorge bridge.

The data might lead to the keeper, but the bridge was icing faster than anyone could cross. The scouts were bringing a rope from the far side. The fighter saw a figure under the bridge lift an arm, then vanish behind the frozen beams as the wind turned colder.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team reached the keeper and secured the station’s last records.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the bridge and brought the keeper across with their rope.
endings.draw: The keeper escaped the cold, but the station remained inaccessible until the ice thawed.

paragraphs: The glassworks’ abandoned furnace held a mirror tilted toward the forest road.
